【中文】
第242章 梵天陨落的零件

石室的空气里弥漫着红水银特有的金属腥味。

薇若兰蹲在地上，用极细的镊子将一颗黄铜铆钉嵌入炸弹外壳的凹槽。她的手指很稳，即使外面已经传来金属碰撞的闷响，也没有抖一下。

阿方索在她旁边，蜘蛛巢腕表上八只微型机械蜘蛛的信号灯有节奏地明灭着。那是他最新的改装，每只蜘蛛的腹部都嵌着一枚针尖大小的红水银微晶，信号强度比旧版提高了四倍。

"第二批空投件到了。"唐璜扛着一个沉重的金属箱走进来，箱面上烙着密涅瓦机关的六翼猫头鹰徽记，"从翡冷翠直飞，二十七个小时。"

他把箱子搁在地上，擦了一把额头上的汗。

碧儿跪在图纸旁，用极细的炭笔在零件清单上做标记。她没有说话，但笔尖移动得很快。石室里除了校准仪偶尔发出的嘀嗒声，只有纸页翻动的细响。

薇若兰拆开箱子。

里面是一层又一层的影金属减震垫，减震垫中间固定着一颗拳头大小的球形容器。容器通体暗银色，表面刻着细如发丝的纹路——那是世界树神经祈祷文和完美合金特有的原子级晶体排列纹路。容器中央嵌着一个拇指盖大小的圆孔，圆孔边缘打磨得极其光滑，像是一枚等待钥匙的锁孔。

"核心容器。"薇若兰低声说，"密涅瓦初代总长留下的最后一块完美合金，重量只有普通秘银的三分之一，但强度是影金属的两倍。整块合金经过特殊电磁场处理，原子排列被完全锁定——这世界上没有第二块了。"

阿方索的目光落在容器底部。

他的动作停住了。

容器底部嵌着一块红水银晶块核心，但那块核心并非普通的圆柱形红水银能量模块。它的外壳上有一道清晰的旧伤——像是被某种极其锋利的武器贯穿后修复的裂痕，裂痕两侧的合金表面有微弱的烧蚀痕迹。

"这是——"阿方索蹲下身，凑近去看，瞳孔在容器底部那道裂痕上凝住了。

他的蜘蛛巢腕表突然发出一声极轻的电子音。那是八只机械蜘蛛的信号反馈——当目标体内部的能量信号特征与数据库中某条记录吻合时，它们会自动报警。

阿方索抬起头，看着薇若兰。

"这不是普通的红水银核心。"他说，声音压得很低，"这是……二代普罗米修斯的红水银核心。"

石室里的空气像是凝固了。

"什么？"唐璜的眉毛挑了起来。

"蓝鲟的二代普罗米修斯。"阿方索重复了一遍，他的目光没有离开那块核心，"四年半前马斯顿事件，密涅瓦机关从圣域里偷走的那具残骸。我当时参与了拆解和回收——这块核心上的裂痕是龙牙剑刺穿的造成的，位置在核心偏左下方四十五度角，深度七厘米。"

他的声音很平，像是在陈述一条技术参数。

但他的手在微微发抖。

"蓝鲟。"碧儿抬起头，炭笔停住了。

"对。"阿方索说，"蓝鲟·德·拉·罗萨，翡冷翠地下斗兽场出身，代号蓝鲟。十连战的时候驾驶二代普罗米修斯残骸——就是后来的密涅瓦回收的那台——被老板一剑穿心。"

石室里安静得能听见自己的心跳。

西泽尔站在石室入口处，他一直站在那里。

他没有说话。

那块红水银核心在暗银色的容器底部静静地躺着，核心表面那道裂痕在石室的火光下泛着暗淡的青色光泽。裂痕两侧的世界树神经祈祷文已经磨损了大半，但剩余的铭文在某种微弱的能量激发下仍然在轻轻跳动。

然后——

那道裂痕里透出了一丝极其微弱的蓝色光芒。

蓝得像是高加索山脉暗河上方的天光。蓝得像是蓝鲟第一次穿上普罗米修斯甲胄时，面甲后面那双冰蓝色的眼睛。

光芒持续了不到一秒钟就消失了。但西泽尔看到了。

他的后颈黄金套管在同一时刻微微发烫。

"它在……"西泽尔低声说。

他的声音很轻，轻得像是在自言自语。

"它在跟我说话。"

西泽尔走到容器前，单膝跪下。

他的手指悬在那块核心上方，没有触碰，但距离近得能感受到红水银散发的微弱热量。

"对不起。"他说。

他的声音平静，没有起伏，像是在陈述一个已经无法改变的事实。

"当年我杀了你。"

石室里没有人出声。

"但现在我要用你的残骸拯救世界。"

他说完这句话，站起身来，转向薇若兰。

"开始组装。"

薇若兰看了他一眼，没有问什么。她从工具箱里取出一套精密的校准仪，开始将红水银晶块核心与暗银色容器进行对接。

"梵天陨落反物质炸弹的原理，我解释一下。"她一边操作一边说，声音恢复了技术人员特有的冷静和精确，"初代总长设计这套系统的时候，用的是反物质触发机制——当红水银核心在完美合金容器内被激发到临界状态时，会产生一场瞬时的湮灭反应，释放出足以摧毁一切的伽马射线暴。"

"普通红水银核心做不到这一点。"阿方索接过话，"它们太'纯'了，纯到只能释放能量而不能产生反物质。必须用经过实战检验的、承载过神经电流和机械共振的核心——才能在激发态下产生那种'不纯'，那种让核心结构内部产生对称破缺的条件。"

"所以需要二代普罗米修斯的核心。"唐璜说。

"对。"薇若兰说，"只有这种经历过真实战场的高强度能量循环的核心，才能在临界激发时产生足够强度的反物质。"

"那引爆密钥呢？"昆提良问。

薇若兰从工具箱底层取出一只黑色丝绒袋，解开袋口的金线，露出一枚银莲花项链坠。

西泽尔的目光落在项链坠上。

"这是你母亲琳琅夫人的遗物。"薇若兰说，"项链坠背面刻着一行古锡兰文，是达·芬奇·博尔吉亚用微雕工艺在三百年前刻上去的。"

她把项链坠翻过来。

背面果然有一行极细的铭文，笔法像是弯曲的蛇形符号，在石室的火光下泛着淡淡的金色。

"这行铭文就是梵天陨落反物质炸弹的引爆密码。"薇若兰说，"它和完美合金容器底部那个圆孔锁孔是配套的——把项链坠插入锁孔，旋转四分之一圈，密码就会激活。"

"然后呢？"昆提良问。

薇若兰没有立刻回答。

她看了西泽尔一眼。

"然后需要完美适配者的血。"她说，"从锁孔下方的针孔注入。完美适配者的血液会和容器内的红水银核心产生共振，将核心激发到临界状态。"

"也就是说——"唐璜的眼睛微微眯起来。

"也就是说，钥匙是项链坠，催化剂是血。"薇若兰说，"两者缺一不可。"

石室里又安静了。

唐璜蹲下身，围着炸弹外壳转了一圈。他的目光很专业——盗贼的眼睛，对隐藏机关有天生的敏感。

"等等。"他说。

他的手指停在炸弹外壳底部一个不起眼的凹槽上。凹槽里藏着一枚极小的金属拨片，拨片被焊死在凹槽里，但边缘有一圈细细的缝隙。

"这里有个开关。"唐璜说。

"什么？"薇若兰走过来。

唐璜从工具箱里取出一把极细的刻刀，沿着缝隙小心地撬动。拨片被他完整地取了出来。

拨片背面刻着一行字。

"达·芬奇·波吉亚。"唐璜念出来。

阿方索和薇若兰对视一眼。

这个名字在密涅瓦机关的历史里意味深长——初代总工程师，博尔吉亚家族成员，三百年前设计了这座地下城的人。

"初代总长……不，密涅瓦初代总工程师。"薇若兰说，"这枚开关是达·芬奇留下的。"

她从唐璜手中接过拨片，对着火光端详。拨片的金属表面有极细的齿轮纹路，和密涅瓦机关所有精密设备上的纹路如出一辙。

"需要完美适配者的神经电流才能激活。"她说，"我能感觉到。"

石室入口处，一个苍老而平静的声音传来。

"那是缩小范围开关。"

所有人转头。

一个身材高大的老人站在入口处，影金属长袍的下摆沾着火山灰。他的头发全白，眼窝深陷，但站姿笔挺如铁塔。

是屠龙者圣乔治甲胄中那道残留意识——机械神教叩门者的创始人之一，莲生用红水银秘药保存了三百年的存在。

"达·芬奇·波吉亚在设计梵天陨落的时候，预留了这个开关。"老人缓缓走进来，目光落在那枚拨片上，"梵天陨落反物质炸弹如果没有这个开关，爆炸的湮灭范围将覆盖方圆五十公里——足以将王屋山周围的一切化为灰烬。"

他的目光扫过石室里的每一个人。

"但如果激活这个开关——"他说，"爆炸范围会缩小到只摧毁世界树主根节点和所有欧米茄原型体。方圆不超过五百米。"

"这不好吗？"碧儿急切地问。

"好。"老人说，"但有一个代价。"

他看着西泽尔。

"缩小范围需要完美适配者用自己的生命作为锚点。"他说，"完美适配者的神经系统会与炸弹核心形成完全的神经耦合，在爆炸的瞬间承受全部的湮灭能量反冲。"

石室里的空气仿佛被抽空了。

"换句话说——"唐璜的声音有点哑。

"换句话说，使用缩小范围开关的人，将永远消失。"老人说。

"不！"碧儿猛地站起来，炭笔从她手中滑落。

西泽尔站在原地。

他的脸上没有任何表情。

"如果不用这个开关呢？"昆提良问，"如果就用原始的爆炸范围呢？"

"那你们所有人都会死。"老人说，"连同王屋山周围三十个村庄的百姓。"

"那你为什么要告诉我们？"阿方索问，声音很沉。

老人没有回答。

他只是看着西泽尔。

"达·芬奇·波吉亚把这个选择权留给了完美神使。"他说，"他知道三百年前一定会有人面临这个选择。他把这个决定写进了炸弹的结构里。"

西泽尔走向那枚拨片。

"老板！"唐璜一步跨出，挡在他面前。

西泽尔没有停步。

"让开。"

"你不能——"

"让开。"

他的声音很轻，但很稳。

唐璜的手悬在半空中，僵住了。

西泽尔绕过唐璜，走到炸弹前。

他蹲下身，从薇若兰手中接过那枚刻着"达·芬奇·波吉亚"的金属拨片。

他把拨片放回凹槽里。

然后他的手指按在了拨片侧面的测试键上。

"老板！"阿方索冲上来。

"等等！"薇若兰喊。

西泽尔没有回头。

他的手指在测试键上稳稳地按下去。

咔哒一声极轻的机械响动。

炸弹底部的完美合金容器内部亮起了一团微弱的反物质光芒——那是一种冷冽到极点的蓝白色光芒，像是宇宙深处某颗正在坍缩的恒星的核心。

蓝白色的光在容器内缓缓旋转，照亮了西泽尔的脸。

他的后颈黄金套管在同一时刻剧烈发烫，烫得他后颈的皮肤都泛起了淡紫色。他的瞳孔中浮现出紫金色的纹路，那纹路随着他的心跳明灭。

反物质光芒只持续了五秒钟就熄灭了。

但在那五秒钟里，石室里的每一个人都感觉到了一种深入骨髓的冷意——那是完美适配者的神经系统与炸弹核心完成耦合的瞬间。

老人看着西泽尔，眼中闪过一丝复杂的神色。

"达·芬奇等了三百年。"他说，"终于等到了。"

就在这时——

阿方索的蜘蛛巢腕表再次发出刺耳的警报声。

这一次不是预警。

是紧急警报。

"第三波。"阿方索看着腕表上疯狂跳动的数字，脸色铁青，"超过一万架。"

"什么？"唐璜的声音变了调。

"一万架以上。"阿方索重复，"从东方平原过来。"

西泽尔站起身。

他走向石室入口，每一步都很稳。

"守一小时。"他没有回头，"炸弹还需要一小时。"

石室外面，夕阳正在沉入东方平原的地平线。

夕阳的余晖被一片暗金色的金属洪流遮蔽了。

那不是一千架。

那是超过一万架的欧米茄原型体，密密麻麻地排列成莲花状的同心圆阵列，从地平线的尽头一直延伸到王屋山的脚下。每一架原型体的胸腔都嵌着跳动的红水银核心，暗金色的光在雾气中连成一片。

而在这片金属洪流的最前方——

一台特殊的原型体走在一万架原型体的最前面。

那台原型体比普通欧米茄原型体高出一倍，全身覆盖着暗金色与黑色交错的厚重装甲板，肩部刻着倒置五芒星与齿轮纹路交织的徽记。它的胸腔内嵌着的不是普通的红水银核心，而是一颗硕大的暗金色晶块，晶块表面刻满了世界树神经祈祷文——

那是第三代普罗米修斯·古洛诺斯。

原罪机关主人的座机。

晶块上方，一个全息投影缓缓浮现。

投影中，那张银色猫头鹰面具在夕阳下泛着冷光，露出的下颌和右手都是精密的机械假肢，关节刻着微型梵文，每一节都发出精密齿轮咬合的细微声响。

"新弥赛亚。"投影中传出冰冷而机械的声音，"你的时间到了。"

王屋山的防线开始动摇。

一百台鬼武者Ⅱ型甲胄已经折损过半，残存的甲胄骑士们在山道上背靠背结成圆阵，被越来越多的欧米茄原型体逼得节节后退。神怒Ⅲ型甲胄骑士同样伤亡惨重，瓦莲京娜驾驶着她的改装神怒Ⅲ型在山腰处与三架古洛诺斯原型机缠斗，暗银色装甲上满是金红色的烧蚀痕迹。

"一小时。"薇若兰的声音从西泽尔腰间的密涅瓦最高级别加密通讯器中传来，"炸弹还需要一小时。你们必须守住。"

"一小时太长了，老板。"唐璜的声音从另一台通讯器中传来，背景是金属碰撞的巨响，"我们可能连二十分钟都守不住。"

西泽尔站在王屋山的半山腰。

他看着山下那片正在吞噬夕阳的金属洪流。

然后他看见了楚舜华。

楚舜华驾驶着鬼武者原型机——那台世界树残根意识连接器——从王屋山山顶冲下来。鬼武者原型机的胸甲浮雕着皇族夔龙纹，右臂加装的小型蒸汽连铳喷出密集的火舌，左臂的精钢重盾在夕阳下反射着金色的光。

他朝着古洛诺斯冲去。

孤身一人。

"楚舜华！"西泽尔的声音在山风中猛地拔高。

楚舜华没有回头。

他的鬼武者原型机越过了防线，越过了所有残存的甲胄骑士，朝着那台比它高出整整一倍的古洛诺斯直冲而去——

像一头明知必死仍然冲锋的夔龙。

【English】
Chapter 242 — The Parts of Brahma's Fall

The air of the stone chamber carried the metallic tang of red mercury.

Verolan knelt on the floor, setting a brass rivet into a recessed slot in the bomb's outer shell with a pair of fine tweezers. Her hands did not shake. Outside the chamber, somewhere down the long rock throat of the passage, metal struck metal, and the sound carried only as a low, far-off complaint.

Alfonso crouched beside her. On his wrist the Spider-Nest watch showed eight tiny mechanical spiders, their signal lamps pulsing in steady sequence. The latest modification. Each spider carried, in its belly, a red mercury microcrystal no larger than a pinhead. Signal strength was four times the older version.

"Second airdrop is in." Don Juan came through the entrance carrying a heavy metal case, the lid stamped with the six-winged owl of the Minerva Order. "Direct flight out of Florence. Twenty-seven hours."

He set the case on the floor. Wiped his forehead with the back of his hand.

Bier knelt over the schematic, marking off parts on a sheet of paper with a fine charcoal stick. She did not speak. The charcoal moved in quick, sure strokes. The only sounds in the chamber were the soft tick of a calibration instrument and the page-against-page whisper as she turned a sheet.

Verolan opened the case.

Inside, layer upon layer of shadow-metal shock padding. At the center of the padding, a fist-sized spherical container. The container was dark silver all over, its surface inscribed with hairl-thin lines — the atomic-level crystalline grain of World Tree neural prayer script and Perfect Alloy. In the middle of the sphere was a circular hole no larger than a thumbnail. The rim of the hole had been polished to glass-smoothness, like a keyhole waiting for a key.

"The core container," Verolan said, low. "The last piece of Perfect Alloy left by Minerva's first Master. A third the weight of common orichalcum, twice the strength of shadow metal. The whole ingot went through a special electromagnetic treatment — the atomic arrangement is locked. There is no second piece in the world."

Alfonso's gaze went to the bottom of the container.

He stopped.

Set into the base of the container was a red mercury crystal core, but the core was not the usual cylindrical module. Its casing bore a clear old wound — a crack that had been repaired, the kind of crack you get when something very sharp has punched through and someone has since soldered the body back together. Either side of the crack showed a faint pattern of ablation.

"This is —" Alfonso crouched, leaned close, his pupils fixed on the crack.

His Spider-Nest watch gave a tiny electronic tone. Eight spiders reporting back. When the energy signature inside a target object matched a record in the database, the watch would warn him on its own.

Alfonso looked up. Looked at Verolan.

"This isn't an ordinary red mercury core," he said. He kept his voice down. "This is the red mercury core of the Second Generation Prometheus."

The air in the stone chamber seemed to set.

"What?" Don Juan's eyebrows went up.

"Blue Sturgeon's Second Generation Prometheus," Alfonso said again. He did not look away from the core. "Marston, four and a half years ago. The Minerva Order stole the wreckage from the Holy Domain. I was part of the salvage and the disassembly. The crack in this core was made by a dragon-tooth sword. Forty-five degrees off the left-lower of the core. Depth, seven centimeters."

His voice was level. The voice a man uses to read out a technical parameter.

But his hand, on his knee, was trembling.

"Blue Sturgeon," Bier said. She had raised her head. The charcoal had stopped.

"Yes," Alfonso said. "Blue Sturgeon de la Rosa. Out of the Florence underground beast-pits. Callsign, Blue Sturgeon. Ten-fight streak. He was piloting the Second Generation Prometheus wreck when it came into Minerva's hands — the same wreck. Got a blade through the heart, from the boss."

The chamber went so quiet a man could hear his own pulse.

Cesare stood at the entrance to the chamber. He had been standing there the whole time.

He did not speak.

The red mercury core lay at the bottom of the dark-silver sphere, still. The crack along its surface caught the lamplight and gave back a dim, cyan sheen. Most of the World Tree prayer script on either side of the crack had worn away. What was left of the inscription still pulsed faintly, stirred by some small current of energy.

Then —

A thread of blue light came out of the crack.

A blue like the sky above the underground rivers of the Caucasus. A blue like the ice-colored eyes that had once looked out from behind the visor of a Second Generation Prometheus the first time Blue Sturgeon put it on.

The light lasted less than a second. Then it was gone. Cesare had seen it.

At the same instant, the gold sleeve-pipes at the back of his neck grew warm.

"It is —" Cesare said.

His voice was low. Low enough to be a man talking to himself.

"It is speaking to me."

Cesare walked to the container. Dropped to one knee.

His fingers hovered above the core. He did not touch it. But he was close enough to feel the small heat the red mercury gave off.

"I am sorry," he said.

His voice was even. No rise, no fall. The voice of a man stating a fact that could not be changed.

"I killed you, four and a half years ago."

No one in the chamber spoke.

"But now I am going to use what is left of you to save the world."

He stood. Turned to Verolan.

"Begin the assembly."

Verolan looked at him. She did not ask. She reached into her toolbox and took out a precision calibration set, and began coupling the red mercury crystal to the dark-silver container.

"The principle of the Brahma's Fall antimatter bomb," she said, working as she spoke, her voice back to the cool, exact voice of a technician. "When the first Master designed the system, he used an antimatter trigger. When the red mercury core inside the Perfect Alloy container is driven to its critical state, it produces a momentary annihilation reaction. Releases a gamma-ray burst large enough to destroy anything in its path."

"A common red mercury core can't do that," Alfonso said. "They're too pure. Too pure to release antimatter — they only release energy. You need a core that's been battle-tested, that's carried real neural current and real mechanical resonance. Only a core like that will, at critical excitation, develop the kind of impurity you need. The kind of impurity that produces symmetry-breaking in the internal structure."

"So you need the Second Generation Prometheus core," Don Juan said.

"Yes," Verolan said. "Only a core that's been through that kind of high-intensity energy loop on a real battlefield can produce antimatter of the strength you need at critical excitation."

"The detonation key?" Quintilian asked.

Verolan reached to the bottom of the toolbox. Drew out a small black velvet bag. Unknotted the gold cord at its mouth. Inside, a silver lotus pendant on a fine chain.

Cesare's eyes went to the pendant.

"This is your mother's keepsake," Verolan said. "Lady Linlang's. On the back of the pendant, micro-engraved in three-hundred-year-old Ceylonese script, by Da Vinci Borgia."

She turned the pendant over.

On the back, a line of fine inscription in curving serpentine characters, glinting faintly gold in the lamplight.

"This inscription is the arming cipher of the Brahma's Fall antimatter bomb," Verolan said. "It pairs with the circular keyhole on the base of the Perfect Alloy container. Insert the pendant into the keyhole, turn a quarter turn, and the cipher is activated."

"Then what?" Quintilian said.

Verolan did not answer at once.

She glanced at Cesare.

"Then you need the blood of the Perfect Adapter," she said. "Injected through the needle-port below the keyhole. The Perfect Adapter's blood will resonate with the red mercury core inside the container, and drive the core to its critical state."

"So," Don Juan said. His eyes had narrowed a fraction. "The key is the pendant. The catalyst is the blood. You need both."

The chamber went quiet again.

Don Juan crouched down. Walked a slow circle around the bomb's outer shell. His eyes were the eyes of a thief — born sensitive to anything hidden in a mechanism.

"Wait," he said.

His finger had stopped on a small, unremarkable recess in the base of the bomb. Inside the recess, a tiny metal tab. The tab had been welded into the recess, but around its edge was a fine seam.

"There's a switch in here," Don Juan said.

"What?" Verolan came over.

Don Juan took a fine engraving knife from the toolbox. Worked the tip carefully into the seam. Levered. The tab came out whole.

On the back of the tab, a line of letters.

"Da Vinci Borgia," Don Juan read.

Alfonso and Verolan looked at each other.

The name carried weight in the history of the Minerva Order. First Master Engineer. A Borgia. The man who, three hundred years ago, had designed the underground city.

"The first Master — no, the first Master Engineer of the Minerva Order," Verolan said. "This switch was left by Da Vinci."

She took the tab from Don Juan. Held it up to the lamp, studying it. The metal surface carried the same fine gear-tooth patterning that ran across every piece of precision equipment in the Minerva Order.

"It needs the neural current of a Perfect Adapter to activate," she said. "I can feel it."

From the entrance to the chamber, an old voice, calm.

"That is the range-reduction switch."

Every head turned.

An old man stood in the entrance. Tall. A long shadow-metal robe, its hem dusted with volcanic ash. White hair. Sunken eyes. A back held like an iron pillar.

The remnant consciousness in the Saint George the Dragon-slayer armor. One of the founders of the Order of the Knocker. A presence Liansheng had kept alive for three hundred years in a red mercury tincture.

"Da Vinci Borgia left this switch in the design of the Brahma's Fall," the old man said. He walked slowly in. His eyes went to the tab. "If the Brahma's Fall antimatter bomb goes off without this switch, the annihilation range will be fifty kilometers in every direction. Enough to turn everything around Mount Wangwu to ash."

His gaze went around the chamber. Took in each face.

"But if the switch is activated, the blast range contracts to the World Tree's main root-node and to all Omega prototypes within. A radius of no more than five hundred meters."

"Isn't that good?" Bier said, leaning forward.

"Good," the old man said. "But it has a cost."

He looked at Cesare.

"Reducing the range requires the Perfect Adapter to use his own life as the anchor. The Perfect Adapter's nervous system forms a full neural coupling with the bomb core. At the moment of detonation, the adapter takes the full backwash of the annihilation energy."

The chamber's air seemed to be drawn out.

"In other words," Don Juan said. His voice was rough at the edge.

"In other words," the old man said, "the man who uses the range-reduction switch will be gone. Permanently."

"No!" Bier was on her feet. The charcoal stick fell out of her hand.

Cesare stood where he was.

His face showed nothing.

"And if we don't use the switch?" Quintilian said. "If we let the blast run at its original range?"

"Then you all die," the old man said. "Along with the thirty villages around Mount Wangwu."

"Why tell us, then?" Alfonso said. His voice was heavy.

The old man did not answer.

He only looked at Cesare.

"Da Vinci Borgia left this choice to the Perfect Divine Envoy. He knew, three hundred years ago, that someone would have to make it. He wrote the decision into the structure of the bomb."

Cesare walked toward the tab.

"Boss!" Don Juan stepped out, blocked him.

Cesare did not slow.

"Move."

"You can't —"

"Move."

His voice was quiet. But it was steady.

Don Juan's hand hung in the air. Froze.

Cesare stepped around him. Walked to the bomb.

He crouched. Took the metal tab — the one engraved with the name of Da Vinci Borgia — out of Verolan's hand.

He set the tab back into the recess.

Then he pressed the test contact on the side of the tab.

"Boss!" Alfonso lunged forward.

"Wait!" Verolan shouted.

Cesare did not look back.

His finger held, steady, on the test contact.

A tiny mechanical sound. A soft click.

Inside the Perfect Alloy container at the base of the bomb, a cold blue-white light came on — a light so cold it was almost nothing, a light like the heart of some collapsing star at the bottom of the universe.

The blue-white light turned slowly inside the container. It lit Cesare's face.

At the same instant, the gold sleeve-pipes at the back of his neck grew suddenly, viciously hot. Hot enough that the skin at the back of his neck flushed violet. Purple-gold lines came up in his pupils, pulsing with his heartbeat.

The antimatter light lasted five seconds. Then it went out.

In those five seconds, every person in the chamber had felt it — a cold that went bone-deep. The moment of a Perfect Adapter's nervous system completing its coupling with the bomb core.

The old man looked at Cesare. Something complicated moved in his eyes.

"Da Vinci waited three hundred years," he said. "And at last, his man has come."

Then —

Alfonso's Spider-Nest watch let out a shrill alarm.

This was not a warning.

This was an emergency.

"Third wave," Alfonso said. He was looking at the numbers racing across the face of the watch. His face was the color of iron. "Over ten thousand."

"What?" Don Juan's voice cracked.

"Over ten thousand," Alfonso said. "Coming in from the eastern plain."

Cesare stood up.

He walked to the entrance of the chamber. Each step was steady.

"Hold for one hour," he said. He did not look back. "The bomb needs one more hour."

Outside, the sun was going down into the eastern horizon.

The last of the sunlight was being eaten by a tide of dark-gold metal.

It was not a thousand.

It was more than ten thousand Omega prototypes, packed tight in a concentric lotus-formation, stretching from the end of the horizon to the foot of Mount Wangwu. Each prototype carried a beating red mercury core in its chest. The dark-gold light, running through the haze, ran together into a single sheet.

And at the very front of that tide of metal —

A single prototype walked ahead of the ten thousand.

This one stood twice as tall as a common Omega prototype. Its body was sheathed in heavy armor plating, dark gold and black intercut, the shoulder carved with the sigil of an inverted five-pointed star woven through with gear-teeth. The chest did not carry an ordinary red mercury core. It carried a single, massive dark-gold crystal, its surface inscribed edge to edge with the World Tree's neural prayer script —

The Third Generation Prometheus. Chronos.

The personal mount of the master of the Original Sin Order.

Above the crystal, a holographic projection took shape.

Inside the projection, a silver owl mask caught the last of the sun, the only thing that gleamed cold. The exposed jaw and the right hand were precision mechanical prostheses, the joints cut with minute Sanskrit, each knuckle making the small clean sound of meshing gears.

"New Messiah," the projection said. The voice was cold. The voice of a machine. "Your time is up."

On Mount Wangwu, the defensive line was giving way.

A hundred Ghost Warrior Mark II suits had already lost more than half their number. What was left of them, the surviving armor-knights, had fallen back up the mountain paths, forming a circle back to back, being pressed, step by step, by the ever-rising number of Omega prototypes. The Divine Wrath Mark III knights were taking losses almost as heavy. Valentina, piloting her modified Divine Wrath Mark III, was fighting three Chronos prototypes at the mid-slope. The dark-silver plating of her armor was covered in gold-red ablation marks.

"One hour," Verolan's voice came through the highest-encryption Minerva communicator at Cesare's waist. "The bomb needs one more hour. You have to hold."

"One hour is too long, boss," Don Juan's voice came through another communicator, the sound of metal striking metal loud behind it. "We may not hold for twenty minutes."

Cesare stood on the mid-slope of Mount Wangwu.

He looked down at the tide of metal that was swallowing the last of the sun.

Then he saw Chu Shunhua.

Chu Shunhua was piloting the Ghost Warrior prototype — the unit that linked to the consciousness of the World Tree's residual root — and he came down off the summit of Mount Wangwu. The breastplate of the Ghost Warrior prototype was embossed with the imperial Kui-dragon crest. The small steam repeater mounted on the right arm spat a dense stream of fire. The heavy steel shield on the left arm caught the last of the sun and threw back a sheet of gold.

He was making for Chronos.

Alone.

"Chu Shunhua!" Cesare's voice climbed, suddenly, over the wind on the mountain.

Chu Shunhua did not look back.

His Ghost Warrior prototype crossed the defensive line. Crossed the last of the surviving armor-knights. Bore down, full, on the Chronos that stood a full head taller than itself —

Like a Kui-dragon that knows it is going to die, and charges anyway.

第243章 龙雀的陨落

【中文】
第243章 龙雀的陨落

楚舜华的鬼武者原型机如同一头浑身漆黑的夔龙，从王屋山山顶直冲而下。

原型机没有外挂重盾，夔龙首钢盔上的龙睛在暮色中射出两点暗红色的光——那是世界树残根意识连接器被全功率激活的标志。他的左臂夹着那面精钢重盾，右臂没有持剑，夔龙角剑和青蛇剑都收在背后的武器挂架上。

他还没有拔剑。

"楚舜华！你疯了吗！"阿方索的声音从通讯器中炸了出来。

没有人回答。

原罪机关主人的第三代普罗诺斯·古洛诺斯就站在第三波欧米茄原型体群的最前方。暴龙级动力核心在它胸腔深处发出低沉的轰鸣，每一声都像巨兽的心跳。六米长的反曲锯齿巨刃斜斜拖在地上，刃口在暮光中泛着冷蓝色的寒光。

它的龙吼炮架在左肩。炮管粗如古井，内壁镌刻着细密的世界树神经祈祷文，那是三百年前初代教皇从阿瓦隆冰原带回的符文，能让炮弹在射出后自动锁定高能红水银信号源。

楚舜华距古洛诺斯还有三百米。

两百米。

一百米。

古洛诺斯动了。

不是攻击，是后退。暴龙级动力核心的输出瞬间拉满，蒸汽喷射口喷出青蓝色的高压蒸汽，七米高的钢铁巨兽竟然像一头猫科动物那样轻巧地向后滑了五步。

它在用龙吼炮瞄准楚舜华。

"现在！"楚舜华的声音从通讯器中传来，平静得像在茶室中吩咐上茶。

他拔剑了。

双手同时探向背后。夔龙角剑从左侧武器挂架上弹出，天然纹理如凝固闪电的剑身在暮色中泛着暗红的光——那是夔龙角本身的色泽，三百年来从未褪去。青蛇剑从右侧挂架上弹出，剑身窄而弯曲，覆着一层淡绿色铜锈。

双剑入手的瞬间，楚舜华踏碎了脚下的山道。

鬼武者原型机以不可能的速度前冲。残根意识连接器将数百米范围内所有移动物体的轨迹灌入他的神经，每一颗欧米茄原型体的关节转动都清晰得像画在纸上的线条。他看见了古洛诺斯龙吼炮炮口的微调，看见了那个青铜关节齿轮转动的预判角度。

他看见了原罪机关主人即将开火前零点三秒的呼吸间隙。

双龙斩。

夔龙角剑自上而下斩落，剑锋在空气中拉出一道笔直的暗红色光芒，精准切入古洛诺斯左肩炮架与甲胄主体的连接缝隙——那是被自愈神经纤维覆盖最薄的位置。青蛇剑紧随其后，弯曲的剑身绕过了锯齿巨刃的格挡弧线，从龙吼炮炮管根部横扫而过。

两声金属断裂的脆响几乎同时炸开。

龙吼炮从古洛诺斯左肩脱落，连同半截炮架一起砸在山道上，溅起大片的碎石和火星。炮膛内未发射的红水银炮弹滚落在地，发出沉重的闷响。

第三代普罗罗诺斯的龙吼炮，被斩断了。

山腰处传来叶尼塞神怒骑士团骑士们的惊呼。他们昨天下午才刚刚见识过这尊火炮的恐怖——五架欧米茄原型体被一炮轰成碎片。没有人相信有谁能用近身武器切断它。

可楚舜华用两把剑做到了。

原罪机关主人没有说话。古洛诺斯的动作停顿了零点五秒，驾驶舱内传来精密齿轮咬合的声响——那是机械关节在重新校准指令的反应。

然后反击来了。

没有任何预兆。古洛诺斯右臂的六米反曲锯齿巨刃自下而上撩起，速度快得几乎撕裂空气。刃口在暮色中拖出一道冷蓝色的弧光，锯齿与空气摩擦发出尖锐的啸叫。

这一刀不是劈斩，是斩首。

楚舜华举盾。

鬼武者原型机左臂的精钢重盾迎上锯齿巨刃，五层交错锻造的盾面硬接六米巨刃的全力一击。影金属外层在接触瞬间发出刺耳的金属嘶叫，冲击波将楚舜华脚下的山道压出一个半米深的凹陷。

巨刃没有切开重盾。

但古洛诺斯的动力远超鬼武者原型机。暴龙级动力核心的输出还在攀升，巨刃上叠加的力量越来越大，重盾表面开始出现细密的裂纹。

楚舜华弃盾了。

他的身体在原型机内部猛地后仰，重盾脱离左臂挂架，被巨刃的力量拍飞出去，旋转着砸进山壁。几乎在同一瞬间，他右手的夔龙角剑从下方刺出，直取古洛诺斯的右臂关节。

剑锋入甲三分，卡在了自愈神经纤维层中。

巨刃偏了。

原本斩向楚舜华胸腔的那一击斜斜地削过鬼武者原型机的右肩，锯齿撕裂了外层装甲，斩断了内部的动力传动轴。原型机的右臂连同半截肩甲一起飞了出去，在山道上翻滚着坠入山崖。

楚舜华被斩断了一臂。

山风灌进断裂的肩部装甲，原型机内部的警报灯疯狂闪烁。楚舜华低头看了一眼自己失去的右臂，夔龙角剑还插在古洛诺斯的关节里，剑柄随着巨兽的动作微微晃动。

他拔出了左手最后那把青蛇剑。

"楚舜华！撤回来！"西泽尔的声音从通讯器中传来，不再是冷静的低声。

楚舜华没有回答。

古洛诺斯抽回了右臂巨刃，断裂的关节处涌出暗金色的血液——那是自愈神经纤维被割断后的欧米茄体液。液体在空气中迅速凝固，但神经纤维已经开始以肉眼可见的速度生长，试图重新连接。

原罪机关主人发出了一声低沉的机械笑声。投影中银色猫头鹰面具泛着冷光，露出的下颌和右手都是精密的机械假肢。

"不错的剑术。"冰冷而机械的声音从古洛诺斯的外置扬声器中传出，"但你的甲胄已经残了。"

楚舜华低头看了一眼自己断裂的右肩。

然后他做了一件事。

他用青蛇剑刺穿了自己原型机胸腔下方那个硕大的备用蒸汽核心外壳。

剑尖没入红水银与蒸汽的混合腔体，引发了内部的连锁反应。备用蒸汽核心发出越来越响的嘶鸣声，金属外壳开始变形。

"你要做什么？"原罪机关主人的声音第一次出现了波动。

楚舜华没有回答。

他伸手按下了原型机弹射座椅的启动键。

座椅在爆炸前零点五秒从胸腔中弹出，拖着楚舜华的身体朝山下飞射。几乎在同一瞬间，备用蒸汽核心引爆了。

赤红色的火球吞噬了方圆三十米的空间。

十二架欧米茄原型体被爆炸直接撕碎，更多的被冲击波震得失去平衡，像被风暴掀翻的铁皮玩具那样从山道上滚落。距离最近的古洛诺斯也被爆炸的余波推出了十几米，巨刃上被炸出几个深坑，暗金色的体液从坑洞中涌出。

但古洛诺斯没有倒。

暴龙级动力核心在爆炸的瞬间全功率输出，蒸汽喷射口喷出青蓝色的高压蒸汽，将七米高的钢铁巨兽从爆炸的冲击中硬生生稳住。锯齿巨刃插入地面，将机身固定。

楚舜华的备用蒸汽核心爆炸摧毁了第三波欧米茄原型体群前方三分之一的阵列。

但古洛诺斯只受了一点皮外伤。

弹射座椅在山腰的碎石堆中翻滚了数圈后停下。楚舜华从座椅上跌落，整个人趴在碎石间，动也不动。他的右臂被弹射时的冲击震得脱了臼，肩膀处的军服被鲜血浸透。

他的脸朝下贴着地面。

但他还在呼吸。

有人看见了他的眼睛。

那双眼瞳曾经是带着金色纹路的灼热亮紫——星见血脉共鸣时的紫瞳金纹。但此刻，那金色纹路正在褪去，像退潮的金色水迹，从瞳孔边缘一圈圈黯淡下去。

紫瞳金纹消失了。

但紫色的虹膜还在。只是不再发亮。

"楚舜华！"

瓦莲京娜的声音从通讯器中传来，几乎同时，改装神怒Ⅲ型甲胄的身影从山腰的混战中脱离，如同一道暗银色的闪电直冲而下。破甲锤和叶尼塞战斧都还握在手中，背部的蒸汽喷射推进器喷出青蓝色的尾焰。

她在俯冲。

改装神怒Ⅲ型在楚舜华坠落的位置急停，蒸汽喷射口朝地面喷出高压气体，将碎石吹得四散。叶尼塞公主从驾驶舱中探出半个身体，金色的长发在蒸汽中飞扬。

她伸手抓住了楚舜华的后领，将这个比她高出一个头的男人像拎一袋粮食一样拽进了驾驶舱的副座。

"别动。"瓦莲京娜的声音冷得像冰原上的风。

她将楚舜华靠在副座靠背上，迅速检查伤势。右肩脱臼，肋骨可能断了三根，头部有撞击伤，颅内可能有淤血。鲜血从耳朵里渗出来。

"死不了。"她下了结论，语气平淡得像在评价一件货物的成色。

改装神怒Ⅲ型重新启动，蒸汽喷射推进器全力输出，暗银色的甲胄拔地而起，朝着王屋山世界树主根节点的方向飞去。驾驶舱内，瓦莲京娜一手握着操纵杆，一手按着楚舜华的胸口，确认他的心脏还在跳动。

"撑住。"她说。

楚舜华的眼睛半睁着，紫色的瞳孔暗淡无光。他张开嘴，嘴唇翕动了几下。

"我……还能打。"

"闭嘴。"瓦莲京娜冷冷地说。

楚舜华闭上了眼睛。

西泽尔站在王屋山半山腰的一块岩石上，看着那架暗银色的甲胄带着楚舜华消失在暮色中。

他的大脑一片空白。

那是他最恐惧的时刻，不是面对古洛诺斯，不是面对欧米茄原型体群，而是看到一个他愿意信任的人倒下去。不是倒下，是被炸得只剩一口气，从甲胄里弹射出来，像个破碎的人偶那样趴在碎石堆里。

楚舜华是星见之子。

是他的同盟。

是他在这场战争中除了瓦莲京娜和三个旧部之外唯一可以依靠的同等级的战力。

西泽尔的手开始发抖。

不是恐惧，是愤怒。一种他从未感受过的、像是有什么东西在胸腔里炸开的愤怒。那种愤怒不是火焰，是岩浆，从他的心脏沿着血管流向四肢，每一寸皮肤都像是被灼烧过。

后颈的黄金套管开始发烫。

越来越烫。

然后是瞳孔。

西泽尔的瞳孔从棕色变成了被金色纹路贯穿的灼热亮紫。金纹不是楚舜华那种整齐的环形，而是龙形的——像两条金色的小龙从瞳孔中央旋转着向外延伸，尾端带着细小的红色火焰。

那是不朽之王系统的完全启动。

不是三分钟的安全阈值激活，是完全启动。芯片过载了。

系统发出了刺耳的警告声，但西泽尔听不见。他只看见山下的金属洪流，只看见古洛诺斯那尊七米高的钢铁巨兽正率领着残存的欧米茄原型体群朝王屋山推进。

"西泽尔！你疯了！"阿方索的声音从通讯器中传来，"不朽之王系统完全启动的话八分钟后就——"

西泽尔已经冲了出去。

他没有穿甲胄。他冲向的是山道上那台被斩断右臂的鬼武者Ⅱ型残骸——某个被欧米茄原型体击毁后被推到路边的骑士的机体。右臂断裂，左臂尚存，动力核心还剩三成。

他钻进了驾驶舱。

"你不会真的想用那台破烂——"昆提良的声音在通讯器中炸开。

西泽尔没有回答。他伸手在断裂的驾驶舱操控台上摸索，扯出了一把散落的线缆。线缆的另一头连接着操控台下方的电路板。

他把线缆插进了后颈的黄金套管接口。

神经接驳强行建立。

鬼武者Ⅱ型残骸的右臂传动轴已经断了，但左臂还能动。蒸汽核心的残余动力被他用最粗暴的方式拉到极限，蒸汽压力表的指针直接弹到了红区。

这台残骸被他启动了。

然后他看到了让他瞳孔进一步收缩的画面。

成千上万只青铜微型机械蜘蛛从王屋山的山体裂缝中涌出。不是昨天那批，是更多。多得像一层流动的青铜地毯，沿着山道向古洛诺斯的方向铺展。

所有蜘蛛的头部凹槽都亮着两点绿光。

"新神使。"一个苍老而沙哑的声音从通讯器中传来。

是莲生。

这位封存三百年的屠龙者圣乔治的驾驶者，此刻正站在王屋山世界树主根节点的石室入口处。鬼武者原型机已经报废，他失去了自己的甲胄，但他还在。

"叩门者全体集合。"莲生的声音平静得不像是在报告一场自杀式攻击，"所有青铜蜘蛛自毁程序启动。"

他的右手按在石室的岩壁上。那只三百年前被达·芬奇焊接在他身上的青铜机械手臂，关节处亮起了微弱的红光。

"保护新神使。"

西泽尔看见那片青铜地毯开始加速。

数以万计的机械神教叩门者涌向第三波欧米茄原型体群，每一只蜘蛛的腹部红水银微晶都在同时启动。它们的甲壳打开，释放出针对欧米茄原型体神经接驳系统的宽频电磁脉冲。

蜘蛛的脉冲在空气中汇成一张无形的网。

网覆盖了整个第三波阵列。

欧米茄原型体的动作几乎同时停滞。自愈神经纤维在电磁脉冲的干扰下暂时失去了传导功能，红水银核心的跳动频率被打乱，每一台原型体的关节都僵在了原地。

"三分钟。"莲生的声音从通讯器中传来，"只有三分钟。"

西泽尔驾驶着鬼武者Ⅱ型的残骸冲入了停滞的欧米茄原型体群。

他用的是最原始的方式——用残存的左臂反复撞击面前的欧米茄原型体。每一次撞击都让他的身体承受巨大的反冲，黄金套管传来的剧痛像针一样扎进他的脊椎。但他已经感觉不到了。

不朽之王模式完全启动后，他的痛觉阈值被提升到了一个不可能的高度。

"唐璜。"西泽尔的声音从通讯器中传来。

"收到。"唐璜的声音从另一台通讯器中传来。

蔷薇之鬼的暗红色身影从山腰的混战中脱离，如同一道暗红色的闪电直插第三波阵列的核心。

唐璜的武器是锥子枪。

蔷薇之鬼的试制型炽天使甲胄是为刺杀第三代普罗米修斯骑士舱而设计的特化机体，超轻型装甲换来的是不可能的加速度和单点穿刺力。锥子枪的枪尖是完美合金锻造的，硬度足以刺穿影金属装甲。

唐璜的目标是古洛诺斯。

古洛诺斯在叩门者的电磁脉冲中也暂时失去了行动能力，但暴龙级动力核心还在运转。自愈神经纤维正在加速修复被干扰的接驳系统。

三分钟。

唐璜只有三分钟。

蔷薇之鬼在停滞的欧米茄原型体群中穿行，锥子枪收在身侧。超轻型装甲的蒸汽喷射推进器喷出暗红色的尾焰，将甲胄的加速度拉到极限。

他冲到了古洛诺斯面前。

锥子枪刺出。

枪尖精准地扎入古洛诺斯骑士舱盖板与颈部装甲的接缝。完美合金的硬度远超普通影金属，枪尖没入接缝两寸，卡在了自愈神经纤维层中。

暗金色的体液从刺入点喷涌而出。

"命中了！"唐璜的声音带着狂喜。

但他的狂喜只持续了半秒。

古洛诺斯的自愈神经纤维在电磁脉冲的干扰下仍然在以极其缓慢的速度修复。那种修复不是瞬间的，而是像某种古老的本能一样在进行——神经纤维从伤口边缘向内生长，试图将入侵的异物推出。

唐璜的锥子枪正在被缓慢地推出。

"还有两分半！"莲生的声音从通讯器中传来。

"老板！"唐璜对着通讯器吼了一声。

"我看到了。"西泽尔的声音从通讯器中传来，平静得不像是一个正在用意志力对抗神经反噬的人。

他在鬼武者Ⅱ型的残骸中看见了古洛诺斯骑士舱上被唐璜刺出的那个洞。洞口的装甲板正在被自愈神经纤维一点一点地合拢。

就在这时，一个声音从密涅瓦最高级别加密通讯器中传来。

"炸弹还有最后十分钟组装完成。"薇若兰的声音从通讯器中传来，背景是金属碰撞声和焊接的嘶嘶声，"你们必须坚持住。"

十分钟。

西泽尔的嘴角扯动了一下。那不是笑，是某种更复杂的东西。

三分钟的叩门者干扰，加上十分钟的炸弹组装。

十三分钟。

而他的不朽之王系统完全启动后，芯片过载的安全阈值是三分钟。超过五分钟他可能永久失去身体控制权。超过八分钟他会彻底被英雄人格吞噬。

十三分钟。

他只有三分钟。

"阿方索。"西泽尔说。

"在。"

"让昆提良接应唐璜撤退。你给我接通薇若兰的全息通讯。"

"你要做什么？"

"我要告诉她，十三分钟。"

通讯器中传来阿方索沉默的呼吸声。

"收到。"

山风从王屋山的山道灌过来，夹带着红水银燃烧后的刺鼻气味。西泽尔驾驶着残骸的鬼武者Ⅱ型，站在古洛诺斯面前那台被他撞得面目全非的欧米茄原型体上。

他的紫色瞳孔中，两条金龙在旋转，尾端的红色火焰在跳动。

他在等。

叩门者的干扰还剩两分钟。

唐璜的锥子枪还在被缓慢推出。

古洛诺斯的自愈神经纤维还在修复。

而在王屋山世界树主根节点的石室中，薇若兰正在用世界树残根守护符的青铜镜面校准梵天陨落反物质炸弹的最终引爆频率。

西泽尔母亲的银莲花项链坠安静地躺在炸弹的核心组件旁。

等待它真正主人的血。

就在这时，古洛诺斯动了。

叩门者的干扰还剩一分半。

但古洛诺斯的暴龙级动力核心突然爆发出超越设计极限的输出。自愈神经纤维以不可能的速度修复了被干扰的接驳系统。骑士舱盖板猛地弹开，将唐璜的锥子枪弹飞。

唐璜的蔷薇之鬼被一股无形的力量拍飞，在空中翻滚了数圈后砸在山壁上。

古洛诺斯的骑士舱顶盖缓缓升起。

蒸汽从舱内溢出。

一个身影从舱内站了起来。

他摘下了银色猫头鹰面具。

那是一张脸。

年轻的、清瘦的、带着学者气质的脸。轮廓与佛朗哥教授年轻时的样子一模一样——同样的高鼻梁，同样的薄唇，同样的下颌线条，甚至连右眼角那颗小痣的位置都完全相同。

但佛朗哥教授已经死了。

死在马斯顿王立机械学院的地下。

这张脸不可能是佛朗哥教授。

可它就是佛朗哥教授的脸。

原罪机关主人站在古洛诺斯的骑士舱中，暮色中那张年轻的脸没有任何表情，露出的下颌和右手都是精密的机械假肢，关节刻着微型梵文。

他开口了。

声音不再是冰冷的机械音，而是一个温和的、带着些许沙哑的人类嗓音。

"三百年了。"他说，目光穿过山道上所有的残骸与尸体，落在王屋山世界树主根节点的方向，"终于等到了一个能走完这条路的人。"

他的嘴角微微上扬，那是一个与佛朗哥教授完全相同的微笑。

"新弥赛亚……不，西泽尔·博尔吉亚。"

他叫出了西泽尔的名字。

"欢迎来到机械神国。"

西泽尔看着那张脸，紫瞳中的金龙停止了旋转。

他的世界在这一刻被抽空了所有的声音。

那张脸。

那张他曾经在密涅瓦机关地窖里见过无数次的脸。

他的老师的脸。

他的朋友的脸。

他的引路人的脸。

佛朗哥教授的脸。

出现在原罪机关主人的头上。

【English】
Chapter 243 — The Fall of the Longque

The Onimusha prototype plunged down the spine of Mount Wangwu like a black, four-legged dragon — the Kuilong silhouette stripped to its bones.

No external shield hung on the frame. The two ember-red points in the helmet's dragon eyes were the only glow against the dusk, and they meant the World Tree stump-nexus coupler was running at full draw. Under the left arm, a slab of folded steel. The back-mounted weapon rack still held the Kuilong Horn blade and the Green Serpent — both undrawn.

He had not yet drawn his swords.

"Chu Shunhua! Are you mad—"

Alfonso's voice cracked the comm like a sheet of ice.

No one answered.

The third-generation Pronos Kronos stood at the head of the third Omega wave, where its pilot had meant it to be seen. Somewhere deep in its chest a Tyrannosaur-grade power core knocked out its slow iron heartbeat, thump after thump. The six-meter reverse-curved serrated great blade trailed at an angle, its edge drinking the last of the daylight in a cold blue line. Mounted on the left shoulder, the Dragon-Roar cannon: bore as wide as an old well, the inner wall inscribed with the World Tree neural prayers the first Pope had carried back from the Avalon icefields three centuries ago. The prayers would, after firing, lock the shell onto the strongest red-mercury signal in range.

Three hundred meters to the Kronos.

Two hundred.

One hundred.

The Kronos moved.

Not to strike. It stepped back. The Tyrannosaur core slammed to full output, the steam vents blasting high-pressure cyan vapor, and the seven-meter iron beast slid five steps backward with the loose grace of a cat. It was ranging the Dragon-Roar cannon onto Chu Shunhua.

"Now."

His voice came across the comm with the calm of a man asking for tea.

He drew.

Both hands went behind him in a single motion. The Kuilong Horn sword leapt from the left rack, the natural grain of its blade — patterns like frozen lightning — catching the dusk in a dull arterial red, the color of the horn itself, unchanged in three hundred years. The Green Serpent slipped from the right rack, narrow, slightly curved, a patina of pale verdigris laid over its surface.

The moment both hilts met his palms, Chu Shunhua cracked the switchback beneath his feet.

The Onimusha prototype lunged forward at a speed that should not have been possible. The stump-nexus coupler poured the trajectories of every moving object within hundreds of meters straight into his nerves; he could see the turning of every Omega joint as cleanly as lines drawn on a chart. He saw the micro-adjustment of the Kronos cannon's muzzle. He saw the bronze gear inside the joint take its predicted angle. He saw, in the pilot's pre-fire cycle, a 0.3-second breath.

Twin Dragon Slash.

The Kuilong Horn came down from above, its edge drawing a straight dark-red line through the air, and found the seam between the Kronos's left shoulder cannon mount and the main body — the spot where the self-healing nerve fiber was thinnest. The Green Serpent followed, its curved blade sliding under the arc of the serrated great sword and scything through the cannon's root.

Two snaps of torn metal, almost together.

The Dragon-Roar cannon broke away from the Kronos's shoulder, half the mounting with it, and crashed onto the switchback. Stone and sparks fountained. The unfired red-mercury shells rolled out of the bore, thumping heavily onto the road.

The third-generation Pronos Kronos had been disarmed of its cannon.

A murmur went up from the Yenisei Divine Wrath Knights watching from the switchbacks below. They had seen what that gun could do the day before — five Omegas erased in a single shot. None of them had believed any man could take it from the beast with hand weapons.

Chu Shunhua had done it with two.

The pilot of the Original Sin Bureau did not speak. There was a half-second pause in the Kronos's motion, the sound of fine gears seating themselves — mechanical joints recalibrating to new orders.

Then the counter came.

No warning. The Kronos's right arm, the six-meter reverse-curved serrated blade, swept upward from below, fast enough to seem to tear the air. The edge dragged a cold blue arc through the dusk, the teeth of the saw shrieking as they bit the air.

This was not a cleave. It was a beheading.

Chu Shunhua raised his shield.

The Onimusha's left arm, the folded-steel slab, met the great blade head-on, five alternating forge-layers taking the full force of the six-meter stroke. The shadow-metal face screamed. The shockwave stamped a half-meter crater into the stone under his feet.

The blade did not cut the shield.

But the Kronos outpowered the Onimusha prototype. The Tyrannosaur core kept climbing, the stacked weight on the blade mounting, and hairline cracks began to walk across the shield's face.

Chu Shunhua dropped the shield.

His body wrenched backward inside the cockpit. The shield left the arm cradle, was slapped spinning by the force of the great blade, and smashed into the mountain wall. In the same instant, his right hand drove the Kuilong Horn upward, point-first, into the Kronos's right arm joint.

The blade bit three inches of armor and stopped in the self-healing nerve layer.

The great blade skewed.

The stroke that had been aimed at his chest slid sideways, the saw-teeth tearing through the Onimusha's right shoulder plate, shearing the internal drive shaft. The prototype's right arm, with half the shoulder, flew free, tumbled down the switchback, and was gone over the cliff.

Chu Shunhua had lost an arm.

Wind poured through the torn shoulder. Warning lights went mad inside the cockpit. He looked down at the empty socket. The Kuilong Horn was still buried in the Kronos's joint, its hilt swaying faintly with the beast's small motions.

He drew the Green Serpent in his left hand.

"Chu Shunhua! Fall back!" Cesare's voice on the comm was no longer a low murmur.

Chu Shunhua did not answer.

The Kronos pulled its right arm back. From the cut joint a dark gold liquid welled — the Omega's body fluid, pouring from the severed nerve fibers. It began to set as it touched the air, but the fibers themselves were already growing back, plainly visible to the eye, reaching toward each other to reconnect.

The pilot of the Original Sin Bureau made a low mechanical laugh. In the projection the silver owl-mask caught the cold light. The jaw and the right hand that showed beneath it were precision mechanical prostheses, their joints incised with miniature Sanskrit.

"Fine sword work." The voice that came from the Kronos's external speaker was cold and uninflected. "But your armor is finished."

Chu Shunhua looked at his ruined shoulder.

Then he did something.

He drove the Green Serpent through the housing of the prototype's reserve steam core, the great drum set into the chest cavity below the cockpit.

The tip entered the mixed red-mercury-and-steam chamber, and the chain reaction began. The reserve core began to keen, louder and louder, its metal housing starting to deform.

"What are you doing?" The pilot's voice wavered for the first time.

Chu Shunhua did not answer.

He reached up and pressed the cockpit ejection key.

The seat fired. Half a second before the detonation, it tore out of the chest cavity, dragging Chu Shunhua's body with it, and shot down the mountain. In the same instant, the reserve core let go.

A red fireball ate a thirty-meter circle.

Twelve Omegas were torn apart inside it. More were knocked flat by the pressure wave, sent rolling down the switchback like tin toys in a storm. The Kronos, nearest of all, was thrown back ten meters; its great blade came out of the blast peppered with craters, dark gold fluid running from each.

The Kronos did not fall.

The Tyrannosaur core had run to full output the instant the blast went off. The steam vents blasted cyan, and the seven-meter iron beast braced itself out of the shockwave by main force, driving the serrated blade into the rock to anchor itself.

The third Omega wave's forward third array was gone.

The Kronos had taken a scratch.

The ejection seat tumbled through a scree field halfway down the mountain and stopped. Chu Shunhua fell out of the seat onto the stones. He did not move. The ejection shock had dislocated his right shoulder, and blood had soaked the uniform across the chest.

His face was pressed to the ground.

He was still breathing.

Someone saw his eyes.

The irises had been a burning violet threaded with gold — the Star-seer bloodline resonance, purple iris and gold rings. Now the gold was retreating. Like the mark of a tide going out, the gold tracery was dimming in rings from the outer edge of the pupil inward.

The gold was gone.

The violet iris remained. It no longer shone.

"Chu Shunhua!"

Valentina's voice cracked across the comm, and at the same instant the dark silver figure of the Modified Divine Wrath Mk. III broke out of the mid-slope melee and plunged downward like a bolt. The armor-piercing hammer and the Yenisei war-axe were both in her hands. The steam thrustors on its back trailed cyan fire.

She was in a dive.

The Modified Divine Wrath braked hard at the place where Chu Shunhua had fallen. Steam jetted at the ground, scattering the scree. The Yenisei princess leaned half out of the cockpit, gold hair streaming in the vapor.

She caught him by the back of the collar and hauled the man, who was a full head taller than her, into the cockpit's second seat as if he were a sack of grain.

"Don't move." Valentina's voice was the cold of the icefield wind.

She leaned him against the second seat's back and made a quick field check. Dislocated right shoulder. Three cracked ribs, possibly. A head impact, possibly a subdural. Blood was seeping from the ear.

"You'll live." The verdict came with the flatness of a merchant grading a piece of merchandise.

The Modified Divine Wrath's thrustors fired at full. The dark silver machine pulled itself off the ground and turned toward the World Tree main-root node beneath Mount Wangwu. In the cockpit, Valentina held the control stick with one hand and kept the other pressed flat against Chu Shunhua's chest, making sure his heart was still moving.

"Hold on," she said.

Chu Shunhua's eyes were half open, the violet of them dull. His lips moved once, twice.

"I can still fight."

"Shut up," said Valentina, coldly.

Chu Shunhua closed his eyes.

Cesare stood on a rock at the mid-slope of Mount Wangwu, watching the dark silver armor carry Chu Shunhua into the dusk.

His mind was a blank.

That was the thing he feared most. Not the Kronos. Not the Omega waves. To see a man he had chosen to trust go down. Not go down — be blown to one breath, ejected from his armor, dropped onto the scree like a broken doll.

Chu Shunhua was a Star-seer son.

He was Cesare's ally.

He was, in this war, the only peer-level combatant Cesare could rely on, besides Valentina and his three old retainers.

Cesare's hands began to shake.

It was not fear. It was anger. A kind of anger he had not felt before, the feeling of something detonating inside his own chest. That anger was not fire. It was magma, running from his heart along his veins to his four limbs, and every inch of skin felt as if it had been burned.

The gold collet on the back of his neck began to heat.

Hotter. Hotter.

Then his pupils.

Cesare's pupils went from brown to a burning violet shot through with gold. But the gold was not Chu Shunhua's neat rings. It was dragon-shaped — two small gold dragons spiraling outward from the center of the iris, with tiny red flames licking at the tail.

The Undying King system had come up to full activation.

Not the three-minute safety threshold. The whole thing. The chip was overdriven.

The system was screaming its warning. Cesare could not hear it. He saw only the metal flood below. He saw the seven-meter iron beast of the Kronos leading the surviving Omegas up the switchback toward Mount Wangwu.

"Cesare! You are out of your mind!" Alfonso's voice on the comm, "If the Undying King is at full — eight minutes and you —"

Cesare was already running.

He wore no armor. He ran, instead, for the wreck of an Onimusha Mk. II that had been knocked off the road when its rider fell — right arm gone, left arm still attached, power core at three-tenths.

He climbed into the cockpit.

"You cannot actually mean to use that piece of —" Quintilian's voice burst across the comm.

Cesare did not answer. He groped on the broken control deck and pulled a fistful of loose cabling free. The other end of the cabling ran into the circuit board under the console.

He jammed the cabling into the interface on the back of his neck, into the gold collet.

The neural handshake forced itself into place.

The Onimusha Mk. II wreck's right arm drive shaft was broken. The left arm could still move. He hauled the residual steam pressure to its limit in the crudest way he could, slamming the gauge needle into the red.

The wreck came up under him.

Then he saw the sight that made his pupils contract further.

Tens of thousands of small bronze mechanical spiders were pouring from the cracks in Mount Wangwu's flank. Not yesterday's lot. More. So many that they moved like a flowing bronze carpet, unrolling down the switchback toward the Kronos.

Every spider had two green points lit in its head socket.

"New God-Sworn," said an old, dry voice across the comm.

Liansheng.

The driver of Saint George the Dragonslayer, who had been sealed away for three hundred years, was standing at the entrance to the stone chamber of the World Tree's main root node. His Onimusha prototype was a write-off. He had lost his armor. He was still there.

"All Knocker units, assemble." Liansheng's voice was calm in a way no one should have been, reporting a suicide attack. "Initiate self-destruct on every bronze spider."

His right hand rested against the rock of the chamber wall. The bronze mechanical arm that Leonardo had welded onto him three hundred years ago was glowing faintly red at the joints.

"Protect the New Messiah."

Cesare saw the bronze carpet begin to run.

Tens of thousands of mechanical Knocker devotees of the Church of the Machine poured into the third Omega wave, and on each spider the red-mercury microcrystal in the abdomen powered up at the same instant. Their carapaces opened, and from them poured a wide-band electromagnetic pulse aimed at the Omega neural handshake.

The pulses of the spiders wove themselves into an invisible net in the air.

The net fell over the entire third array.

The Omegas stopped at the same time. The self-healing nerve fibers, jammed by the pulse, lost their conduction. The red-mercury cores lost their rhythm. Every joint in every prototype locked in place.

"Three minutes," Liansheng's voice said on the comm. "Three minutes only."

Cesare, in the wreck of the Onimusha Mk. II, drove into the stalled Omega array.

He used the oldest method there was. He rammed the surviving left arm, again and again, into the Omegas in front of him. Each impact sent a shockwave back through his body, and the gold collet fed a needle of pain into his spine. He could no longer feel it.

With the Undying King at full activation, his pain threshold had been lifted to a place that should not have been possible.

"Don Juan," Cesare's voice said on the comm.

"Receiving," said another voice on a different comm.

The dark-red figure of the Rose Ghost pulled out of the mid-slope melee and plunged like a red lightning bolt into the heart of the stalled third array.

Don Juan's weapon was the awl-pike.

The Rose Ghost was a prototype Seraphim armor designed for a single purpose: the assassination of the third-generation Prometheus knight-cabin. The trade had been super-light plating for impossible acceleration and single-point penetration. The tip of the awl-pike was a perfect alloy, hard enough to pierce shadow metal.

Don Juan's target was the Kronos.

The Kronos, in the EMP field of the Knocker spiders, had lost the ability to move. But the Tyrannosaur core was still turning. The self-healing nerve fibers were already working at speed to repair the jammed handshake.

Three minutes.

Don Juan had three minutes.

The Rose Ghost threaded its way through the stalled Omegas, the awl-pike held in at the side. The super-light armor's steam thrustors trailed dark red; the machine was running at the edge of its acceleration.

He came up to the Kronos.

The awl-pike went in.

The tip found the seam between the Kronos's cockpit hatch and the neck plate, and sank in two inches. The perfect alloy was harder than any shadow metal, and it lodged itself in the self-healing nerve layer.

Dark gold body fluid erupted from the wound.

"Hit!" Don Juan's voice was bright with triumph.

The triumph lasted half a second.

The Kronos's self-healing nerve fibers, even under the EMP, were still repairing at a crawl. It was not an instant repair. It was something older, an instinct — the fibers growing inward from the wound's edge, trying to push the invader back out.

Don Juan's awl-pike was being slowly pushed out.

"Two and a half minutes left!" Liansheng's voice on the comm.

"Chief!" Don Juan shouted into the comm.

"I see it," said Cesare's voice on the comm, calm in the way only a man fighting the neural backwash with sheer will could be.

In the Onimusha Mk. II wreck, Cesare saw the hole Don Juan had made in the Kronos's hatch. The plate around the hole was already being closed, hair by hair, by the self-healing fibers.

Then, from a Minerva top-grade encrypted comm, a voice.

"The bomb has ten minutes left on the final assembly." Verlaine's voice, with metal-on-metal and the hiss of a welding torch in the background. "You have to hold."

Ten minutes.

Cesare's mouth moved. It was not quite a smile. It was something more complicated.

Three minutes of Knocker interference. Plus ten minutes of bomb assembly.

Thirteen minutes.

And after the Undying King went to full activation, the chip's overload safety margin was three minutes. Past five minutes, he might lose control of his body forever. Past eight, the hero-personality would swallow him whole.

Thirteen minutes.

He had three.

"Alfonso," Cesare said.

"Here."

"Tell Quintilian to cover Don Juan's retreat. Get me a full holo-link with Verlaine."

"What are you going to do?"

"I am going to tell her thirteen minutes."

There was a silence on the comm that was only Alfonso's breathing.

"Understood."

The wind off the switchback came in across the road, carrying the sting of burnt red-mercury. Cesare, in the Onimusha wreck, stood on the Omega he had beaten flat in front of the Kronos.

The two gold dragons in his violet irises turned. The red flame at their tails flicked.

He waited.

Two minutes of Knocker interference left.

Don Juan's awl-pike was still being slowly pushed out.

The Kronos's self-healing fibers were still growing.

And in the stone chamber of the World Tree's main root node, Verlaine was using the bronze mirror of the World Tree stump-ward to calibrate the final detonation frequency of the Brahma's Fall antimatter bomb.

Cesare's mother's silver anemone pendant lay quiet beside the bomb's core component, waiting for the blood of its true owner.

At that moment, the Kronos moved.

A minute and a half of Knocker interference left.

But the Kronos's Tyrannosaur core suddenly threw out an output past its design limit. The self-healing nerve fibers repaired the jammed handshake at a speed that should not have been possible. The cockpit hatch slammed open and spat Don Juan's awl-pike out.

The Rose Ghost was slapped aside by a force that should not have existed, cartwheeled through the air, and smashed into the rock wall.

The Kronos's cockpit canopy rose slowly.

Steam spilled out of it.

A figure stood up in the cockpit.

He took off the silver owl-mask.

A face.

A young, thin, scholar's face. The contours were exactly those of Professor Franco in his younger years — the same high nose, the same thin mouth, the same jaw line, even the small mole at the corner of the right eye in exactly the same place.

But Professor Franco was dead.

He had died beneath the Marston Royal Mechanical Institute.

This face could not be Professor Franco's.

And it was.

The pilot of the Original Sin Bureau stood in the Kronos's cockpit, and the young face, in the dusk, held no expression at all. The jaw and the right hand that showed beneath it were precision mechanical prostheses, their joints incised with miniature Sanskrit.

He spoke.

His voice was no longer the cold mechanical tone. It was a human voice, warm, faintly hoarse.

"Three hundred years," he said, his gaze passing over all the wreckage and the bodies on the switchback, and settling at last on the World Tree main-root node under Mount Wangwu. "At last, a man who could walk this road to the end."

The corner of his mouth lifted. It was Franco's smile. The same one.

"New Messiah … no, Cesare Borgia."

He said Cesare's name.

"Welcome to the Kingdom of the Machine God."

Cesare looked at the face. The two gold dragons in his violet irises stopped turning.

In that instant his world was drained of every sound.

The face.

The face he had seen a hundred times in the Minerva Bureau cellar.

His teacher's face.

His friend's face.

The face of the man who had shown him the way.

Professor Franco's face.

On the head of the pilot of the Original Sin Bureau.

【中文】
第244章 佛朗哥的老师

西泽尔站在山道上，看着古洛诺斯骑士舱中那张脸。

暮色正浓，最后一缕阳光从云层缝隙里漏下来，打在那张年轻的脸上，把高鼻梁、薄唇和右眼角的小痣照得分外清晰。那不是模仿，不是人皮面具的拙劣复制，因为没有任何一张面具能复制出一个人脸上那些细碎的、仿佛被时间风化了三百年的纹理。

他的老师。

他的朋友。

他的引路人。

佛朗哥教授。

这个人教他认识自己的紫瞳，教他在恐惧深渊的最底层找到冷静，教他把红龙甲胄穿在身上却不发疯。这个人给他留下了世界树的秘密，给他留下了密涅瓦的全部遗产，给他留下了一整个可以依靠的家族。

这个人已经死在马斯顿的地下。

可是他的脸此刻就悬在欧米茄原型体群的前方，离西泽尔不到三百米。

"你不该是这副表情。"那个温和的、带着些许沙哑的嗓音再度响起，"你应该是惊喜的。我特地选在这个时候现身，就是为了让你亲眼看一看——你的老师究竟是谁。"

西泽尔没有回答。

他的手指在身侧微微发紧，指节抵着剑柄慢慢收拢。不朽之王模式的芯片仍在运作，但那些金色的龙纹和红色的火焰正在从他紫瞳的边缘一点一点地褪去，像退潮的海水，露出下面那片冰冷而安静的深紫。

"你叫什么名字？"西泽尔问。

那张脸微微偏了偏头。

"莱昂纳多·波吉亚。"他说，"这个名字你大概没有听过，但它的另一个名字你一定听过——达·芬奇·博吉亚。"

山道上有一阵短暂的静默。

"你姓波吉亚。"西泽尔说。

"是。"莱昂纳多点头，"我是达·芬奇·博吉亚的直系后裔，也是这个家族现存的最长者。我看着这个家族从翡冷翠的一个小贵族变成教皇国的实际统治者，看着弥赛亚圣教从无到有，看着红水银的矿脉被挖空，看着一台又一台的欧米茄原型体从世界树残枝上被复制出来。"

他抬起右手。

那是精密的机械假肢，每一个关节都刻着微型梵文，指尖的金属在暮光里泛着银灰色的冷光。

"三百年了。"他平静地说，"你看到的是我这副身体——百分之八十二的机械结构，百分之十一的红水银循环系统，剩下百分之七是我原本的血肉，主要集中在颅腔和心脏。我的大脑还是我自己的，所以我还记得三百年来的每一件事。"

"包括佛朗哥。"西泽尔说。

"他是我的学生。"莱昂纳多说，"也是我最得意的学生。我花了一百五十年时间培养他，给他灌输达·芬奇·博吉亚的全部机械学知识，让他成为密涅瓦机关最优秀的总长。可惜他最终还是背叛了我，背叛了家族的使命。"

他低下头，看了看自己的机械右手。

"我也曾经有过一双真正的手。那双手画过世界树的图纸，铸造过第一代炽天使的骨架，亲手把圣徽安装到黑铁巨门上。后来红水银侵蚀了我的皮肤，我换掉了这双手。再后来红水银侵蚀了我的肺，我换掉了肺。慢慢地，我身上属于人类的部分越来越少，到最后只剩下这百分之七。"

"为什么？"西泽尔问。

"因为我不愿意死。"莱昂纳多说，"初代教皇——我的祖先——在阿瓦隆冰原发现了世界树残枝。那是一株活着的机械之树，它用红水银作为自己的汁液，树上结出的果实就是欧米茄原型体。初代教皇把世界树残枝带回西方，建造了密涅瓦机关和原罪机关，创立了弥赛亚圣教和教皇国。但他做了一件我最无法原谅的事——"

他的声音平静得没有任何起伏。

"他用自己一半的意识封印了世界树残枝，阻止了机械神国的重启。他既是我的祖先，又是我最大的敌人。他把自己分裂成了两个人，一个叫教皇波吉亚一世，要毁灭世界；一个叫达·芬奇·波吉亚，要拯救世界。这两个身份互相博弈了三百年，最终达·芬奇赢了，他亲手封印了初代教皇的意识，让教皇国走上了一条相对温和的道路。"

"但你不同意。"西泽尔说。

"我不只是不同意。"莱昂纳多摇头，"我是达·芬奇·博吉亚的直系后裔，我的血脉里同时流淌着初代教皇和达·芬奇两支的因子。我继承了他们两位的全部记忆、知识和执念。我看着达·芬奇用三百年的时间封印了初代教皇的意识，看着机械神国的大门被锁上，看着世界树残枝在维苏威火山的深处沉睡，看着红水银被小心翼翼地开采、提炼、限制使用——"

"这一切都是错误的。"他说，"这个世界本来可以更好。如果机械神国重启，红水银将不再稀缺，瘟疫和饥荒可以被彻底根除，战争会因为失去意义而消失。所有人类都将成为神国的一部分。"

"代价呢？"西泽尔问。

"代价是自由意志。"莱昂纳多说，"人是有缺陷的。人类会因为贪婪而发动战争，会因为恐惧而互相残杀，会因为无知而重复同样的错误。机械神国由我的意志统一掌控，将彻底消除所有这些'不稳定因素'。"

"包括东方。"西泽尔说。

"东方必须被征服。"莱昂纳多点头，"夏国的巫教和史前文明一脉相承，他们手中掌握着大量我们不知道的史前遗迹。如果让东方先于西方找到那些遗迹，机械神国的钥匙就会落入他们手中。所以我制订了圣战之路计划，要让教皇国的军队踏平整个东方，建立从大西洋到太平洋的庞大帝国。"

"由你来统治。"西泽尔说。

"由我。"莱昂纳多平静地说，"我是新的弥赛亚。我将坐在世界树残枝的顶端，统治整个地球。"

"这就是你的目的。"西泽尔说。

"这不只是我的目的。"莱昂纳多看着他，"这也是你来到这个世界的目的。"

西泽尔没有说话。

"你以为自己是一个意外。"莱昂纳多说，"你以为自己的紫瞳、自己的天赋、自己的命运都是偶然。可是你错了。我花了三百年时间，挑选、培养、安排了你生命中的每一个人——"

他伸出机械右手，指向西泽尔。

"你的母亲琳琅夫人，是我从锡兰末代星见的血裔中挑选出来的。锡兰末代星见残枝01号用自己的血和骨封印了世界树残枝，但她的血脉并没有断绝。我找到了那个血脉最后的传承者，把她送到了教皇的身边。她爱上了教皇，这不在我的计划之内，但结果比计划更好——她生下了你。"

"你说什么？"西泽尔的声音压得很低。

"你是我用三百年时间孕育的完美适配者。"莱昂纳多说，"你必须同时拥有锡兰星见的紫瞳血脉和博尔吉亚家族的机械适配基因，二者缺一不可。整个西方世界，能够同时满足这两个条件的血脉只有你一个。琳琅夫人是我安排在教皇身边的棋子，她生下你是为了完成我重启机械神国的最后一步。"

"不是。"西泽尔说。

"什么？"

"她不是为了你。"西泽尔说，"她爱我父亲。她爱我。她生下我，是因为她想要一个家。"

莱昂纳多安静了一瞬。

"这重要吗？"他问。

"重要。"西泽尔说，"你用三百年时间布了一盘棋，把我母亲当作棋子，把我当作工具，把所有人都当作你的棋子。你甚至连你自己的家族——你的祖先——都要否定。达·芬奇·博吉亚用三百年时间阻止了初代教皇重启机械神国，你却要用三百年时间完成初代教皇未竟的事业。"

"他是我祖先。"莱昂纳多说。

"他也是你最大的敌人。"西泽尔说，"他否定你，不是因为他不知道机械神国的好处，而是因为他知道——"

他停了一下。

"他知道，人不是'不稳定因素'。"

莱昂纳多看着他，目光里第一次出现了某种接近兴趣的神色。

"人是什么？"他问。

"人是会犯错的。"西泽尔说，"人会贪婪、会恐惧、会互相残杀。但人也会爱，会为了保护另一个人而拼上自己的命。琳琅夫人爱我父亲不是因为我的血脉能连接世界树残枝，是因为他愿意在翡冷翠的秋阳下和她跳舞。佛朗哥教授教我认识自己的紫瞳，不是因为他想让我成为你的工具，是因为他真的把我当学生。"

"这些感情，"莱昂纳多说，"恰恰就是你说的'不稳定因素'。"

"不。"西泽尔说，"这些感情是人最强大的武器。"

莱昂纳多安静地看着他。

暮色已经彻底降临，王屋山的天空从暗红变成深紫，远处的一千多架欧米茄原型体在黑暗中泛着暗金色的冷光，像一整片沉默的钢铁森林。

"你说的人性很有意思。"莱昂纳多忽然说，"但你大概还不知道，我用同样的方法，测试过另一个人。"

"谁？"

"龙德施泰特。"

西泽尔的眼睛微微眯起来。

"那个名字你不陌生吧？炽天骑士团的黑龙，曾经的世界第一骑士，背叛教皇国投奔撒旦教团的叛徒。"莱昂纳多的语气平淡得像在讲述一个与自己无关的旧闻，"你一定以为他是为了那个沉睡的未婚妻蒂兰才叛变的吧？"

"难道不是？"

"那只是表象。"莱昂纳多说，"蒂兰的确是个罕见的适格者，枢机会急于求成把她训练成炽天使骑士，结果神经系统被甲胄侵蚀成了活死人。龙德施泰特恨枢机会，但他没有能力带走蒂兰——一个被冰封在黑铁棺里的活死人，炽天骑士团看守得密不透风。"

"他需要外部的力量。"西泽尔说。

"他需要我。"莱昂纳多纠正道，"我给了他一个选择。撒旦教团的人帮他偷走蒂兰、帮他找到能够修复蒂兰神经损伤的方法。作为交换，他需要替我做三件事。"

"第一件。"莱昂纳多竖起一根金属手指，"在马斯顿的地下斗兽场，测试我新研发的新型炽天使甲胄——也就是你穿的那台红龙的原型机。我需要知道甲胄在实战中的数据，需要知道它和适格者的耦合极限。"

"第二件。"他竖起第二根手指，"带走蒂兰，趁乱把马斯顿王立机械学院搅成一锅粥，让枢机会和密涅瓦机关都焦头烂额。"

"第三件。"他看着西泽尔，"在事发之后，把所有的线索都指向你。"

山道上安静了几秒。

"龙德施泰特带走了蒂兰，又把偷走炽天使的罪名栽到了你的头上。你当时还是个刚入学的学生，什么都没有证明自己的能力，却被扣上了私藏圣物的罪名。"莱昂纳多说，"你母亲为了赎你的罪，不得不接受了查理曼的婚约。"

"那桩婚约——"西泽尔的声音像是从牙缝里挤出来的。

"也是我安排的。"莱昂纳多说，"查理曼国王迪迪埃想要一个博尔吉亚家族的女儿做儿媳，而你需要一桩足够分量的婚约来换取自由。我只是在两边都推了一把。"

西泽尔的手指在剑柄上慢慢收紧。

"龙德施泰特知不知道你的身份？"他问。

"他不知道我是谁。"莱昂纳多说，"他只知道有一个藏在幕后的力量能帮他偷走蒂兰，帮他找到那个能起死回生的魔女贝尔纳黛特——当然，贝尔纳黛特本身也是我安排的棋子之一，他也是我三百年计划中的一部分。但龙德施泰特在偷走蒂兰之后，发现蒂兰的神经损伤无法用常规方法修复，他需要我的后续帮助。"

"所以他成了你的棋子。"

"暂时的棋子。"莱昂纳多说，"等到蒂兰的问题解决，他就没有利用价值了。一个被感情支配的骑士，恰恰是你所说的'不稳定因素'的最好注脚。"

"你说的也许有道理。"莱昂纳多最后说，"但机械神国不需要武器。机械神国需要的是秩序。而秩序要求所有人放弃他们的'感情'，成为神国的一部分。"

"那就从我开始。"西泽尔说。

他抬起手，Excalibur残刃的剑尖指向莱昂纳多。

"你错了三百年。"西泽尔平静地说，"今天就让你知道错在哪里。"

就在这一刻，他后颈的黄金套管猛地发烫。

不是不朽之王模式的那种灼烧，而是另一种——来自密涅瓦机关最高级别加密通讯频率的震动。他伸手从腰间取出一枚拇指大小的接收器，薇若兰的声音从接收器里传来，清晰得仿佛她就在他身边。

"西泽尔，炸弹组装完成了。"

西泽尔的手指在接收器上停了一瞬。

"蓝鲟留下的二代普罗米修斯红水银核心已经就位，引爆密钥也已经从你母亲的项链坠上取下来了。"薇若兰说，"现在只差最后一步——需要你的血，滴在密钥上，才能激活临界状态。"

"我知道了。"西泽尔说。

"西泽尔。"薇若兰的声音里多了一点什么，"达·芬奇在梵天陨落的设计图里预留了一个开关，激活之后爆炸范围可以从五十公里缩小到五百米。但是——"

"我知道。"西泽尔说，"代价是我。"

通讯器里短暂地沉默了一瞬。

"你不必——"薇若兰说。

"薇若兰。"西泽尔打断了她，"把炸弹准备好。我马上过去。"

他关掉了通讯器。

山道上，昆提良驾驶的奥古斯都炽天使甲胄缓缓从山道另一侧绕了过来。他刚才被古洛诺斯拍飞之后摔进了山壁里，但秘银重盾撑住了最大的冲击，五层交错锻造的影金属和硬金只是表面出现了一些裂痕，狮头纹章的耳朵被打掉了，狮眼被裂缝切开，可它依然屹立着。

"老板。"昆提良的声音从通讯频道里传来，带着一些粗哑，"我听见了。"

"你听见了什么？"西泽尔问。

"我听见你说人性是最强大的武器。"昆提良说，"我不知道那是什么狗屁道理。但是老板，你说过要带我打回翡冷翠的，我还没跟你打过几场像样的仗呢。"

他举起奥古斯都的秘银重盾。

"所以你不能死。"

通讯频道里传来阿方索冷静的声音："所罗门王已就位。阿方索·卡斯特罗，随时待命。"

唐璜的声音紧接着响起："蔷薇之鬼还能动。唐璜·莫拉莱斯，随时待命。"

瓦莲京娜的声音也跟了上来："改装神怒Ⅲ型已锁定目标。瓦莲京娜·罗曼诺夫，随时待命。"

楚舜华没有说话，但他的鬼武者Ⅱ型在山道另一端举起了精钢重盾，夔龙角剑的刃口在暮色中发出冷光。

西泽尔看着他们。

"掩护我。"他说。

他转身朝着世界树主根石室的方向跑去。Excalibur残刃握在手中，刃口上的红水银纹路在黑暗中泛着暗金色的光，像一截燃烧的树枝。

他身后，奥古斯都举着秘银重盾迎向了古洛诺斯。

"来啊！"昆提良怒吼着，把重盾狠狠地砸在了古洛诺斯的巨刃上。

金属与金属的碰撞声在山道上炸开，仿佛一头巨鲸在暗夜里翻身。

古洛诺斯的暴龙级动力核心再次爆发出超越设计极限的输出，自愈神经纤维在机械的深处疯狂生长，把被打裂的接驳系统修补完好。巨刃带着毁灭一切的力量从上方砸下，奥古斯都的秘银重盾硬生生地接住了这一击。

秘银重盾发出了一声沉闷的哀鸣。

五层交错锻造的影金属和硬金在巨力下变形，狮头纹章的眼睛彻底裂开了，裂缝沿着狮口向下延伸。但它没有碎。

昆提良的腿甲深深地陷进了山道的岩石里，整个人被巨力压得往后退了半步，但他的双臂没有弯曲。

"阿方索！"他吼道。

"已经启动。"阿方索的声音冷静得没有任何波动。

所罗门王甲胄胸腔打开，六只微型机械蜘蛛从蜘蛛巢腕表里弹射而出，拖着细长的电缆在夜空中划出六道弧线。它们的腹部嵌着高纯度红水银微晶，飞行中发出微弱的齿轮咬合声，像六只叩门的青铜小兽。

这些青铜蜘蛛在三十年前曾经保护过初代总长，三十年后它们响应了完美神使的召唤，从密涅瓦机关的档案库、从翡冷翠的城墙上、从坎特伯雷堡的壁炉里、从维苏威火山的矿道里全部飞出，集合到了王屋山。

六只蜘蛛只是先头部队。

更多的青铜蜘蛛从夜空中落下，从地面钻出，从树丛中爬出——它们共享同一个意识，响应着西泽尔后颈黄金套管的共鸣。数百只青铜蜘蛛在古洛诺斯的周围聚拢，每一只的腹部都嵌着红水银微晶。

"启动自毁。"阿方索低声说。

数百只青铜蜘蛛同时引爆了腹部的红水银微晶。

宽频电磁脉冲在古洛诺斯的周围炸开，呈球形向外扩散。电磁脉冲专门针对欧米茄原型体的神经接驳系统，瘫痪其自愈神经纤维，打乱红水银核心跳动频率。莱昂纳多的机械身体在脉冲波的冲击下剧烈地颤抖了一下，机械关节里的红水银晶片发出刺耳的尖啸声，他抬起右手想抓住什么，但手指在电磁干扰下失控地颤抖着。

"雕虫小技。"莱昂纳多平静地说。他低头看着自己正在颤抖的机械手臂，红水银晶片在干扰中发出忽明忽暗的光。

"是的，雕虫小技。"阿方索说，"但这雕虫小技足够你用三分钟去克服。"

"三分钟已经足够了。"西泽尔的声音从通讯频道里传来。

山道上，他的身影已经消失在了通往世界树主根石室的暗道入口。

唐璜的蔷薇之鬼在夜空中划过一道弧线，曲刃镰从侧后方刺向古洛诺斯暴露的管线。

"掩护老板！"唐璜吼道。

秘银重盾再次承受住了古洛诺斯的巨刃。

这一次，盾没有碎。

但昆提良的奥古斯都甲胄发出了一声金属断裂的脆响——左肩关节的轴承在巨力下被硬生生地扭断了，齿轮从关节里崩出来，在夜空中划出几点火星。

昆提良没有退后。

他用仅剩的右臂把秘银重盾举高，挡在西泽尔消失的暗道入口前方。

"老板。"他低声说，"我还没还完欠你的酒钱呢。"

古洛诺斯的巨刃再次落下。

秘银重盾终于碎了。五层交错锻造的金属片在暮色中四散飞溅，狮头纹章裂成了两半，半只狮头带着缺口飞出了几十米远，砸在山道上翻滚了几圈才停下来。

但秘银重盾在碎裂前最后一刻完成了它的使命。

它用碎裂换来了三秒钟。

三秒钟足够阿方索释放出第二批青铜蜘蛛的电磁脉冲。

三秒钟足够唐璜的蔷薇之鬼刺穿古洛诺斯的左侧管线。

三秒钟足够瓦莲京娜的改装神怒Ⅲ型从侧翼杀到，硬金破甲锤狠狠地砸在古洛诺斯的右膝关节上，把暴龙级动力核心的一条输出管道砸得变了形。

三秒钟。

足够西泽尔跑完那条通往世界树主根石室的暗道。

石室深处，薇若兰站在梵天陨落反物质炸弹旁边。

炸弹已经组装完成。一个直径约一米的球形结构，通体暗金色，外壳刻满了细密的梵文。球体的一端连着一根细长的红水银引信，引信的末端连着一个拇指大小的密钥——琳琅夫人银莲花项链坠背面的古锡兰文铭文。

薇若兰抬起头，看着走进石室的西泽尔。

他没有穿甲胄。Excalibur残刃握在手中，刃口上暗金色的光在石室里照出了他的脸。苍白，冷静，紫瞳中的金龙已经停止了旋转，但也没有完全黯淡。

"你来了。"薇若兰说。

"嗯。"西泽尔说。

他走到炸弹旁边，低头看着那个密钥。银莲花项链坠的背面刻着古锡兰文——那是琳琅夫人留给他的最后一件遗物，藏了二十年的秘密。

他伸出手。

手指停在密钥上方一寸的位置。

"西泽尔。"薇若兰说。

"嗯？"

"……达·芬奇日记的最后几页被我撕掉了。"薇若兰说，"佛朗哥临死前让我不要让你看到。"

"我知道。"西泽尔说。

"你知道？"薇若兰看着他。

"我不知道那几页写了什么。"西泽尔说，"但我知道它们一定写了某种代价。否则你不会撕掉。"

"你——"

"薇若兰。"西泽尔说，"那不重要。"

他低下头。

手指落在了银莲花项链坠上。

"我答应过阿黛尔，会给她留一个家。"他说，"我答应过我父亲，会保护母亲和她。我答应过瓦莲京娜，会把叶尼塞的冬天还给她。"

他抬起手。

手腕内侧有一道浅浅的伤疤——不是这一世的，是更深远的血脉里的。

"我还答应过我自己。"他说，"要守护人类最强大的武器。"

他用 Excalibur 残刃的刃尖划开了自己的手腕。

血珠涌出来，暗红色的，带着淡淡的金色纹路。

那是锡兰星见的血。

血滴在了银莲花项链坠背面的古锡兰文铭文上。

铭文亮了。

【English】
Chapter 244 — Franco's Teacher

Cesare stood on the mountain road, looking up at that face inside the cockpit of the Goulonoth.

The dusk was thick. The last ribbon of daylight leaked through a seam in the clouds and fell across the young face there, picking out the high bridge of the nose, the thin mouth, the small mole at the corner of the right eye with terrible clarity. It was not a forgery. It was no crude copy pressed in some second-rate human-skin mask, because no mask could imitate those fine, weathered lines — the kind that time and grief had carved into a man across three hundred years.

His teacher.
His friend.
The one who had first taken him by the hand and walked him down into himself.

Professor Franco.

The man who had taught him to read his own violet eyes, who had taught him to find stillness at the bottom of the well of fear, who had taught him to wear the Red Dragon armor and not be swallowed by it. The man who had left him the secret of the World Tree, who had left him Minerva's whole inheritance, who had left him an entire household he could lean upon.

That man was dead, somewhere beneath Marston.

And yet his face hung suspended at the front of the Omega prototypes, three hundred meters from where Cesare stood.

"You should not be wearing that expression."

The voice was warm, faintly hoarse at the edges — the voice of a man who has been speaking softly for a long time.

"You should be pleased. I chose this moment to appear precisely so you could see for yourself — who your teacher really was."

Cesare did not answer.

His fingers at his side drew slowly tight. The knuckles settled against the grip of his sword and held. The King Immortal mode was still running, but the gold dragon-fret and the red fire were fading now from the rim of his violet irises, like a tide drawing back to reveal the cold, quiet purple underneath.

"What is your name?" Cesare asked.

The face tilted, almost fondly.

"Leonardo Borgia," he said. "You have probably not heard that name. But you have heard his other name — da Vinci Borgia."

There was a small silence on the mountain road.

"You are Borgia," Cesare said.

"I am." Leonardo inclined his head. "I am the direct descendant of da Vinci Borgia, and the longest-lived of the line. I have watched my family grow from a minor Florentine house into the de facto rulers of the Papal States. I have watched the Holy Church of the Messiah rise from nothing. I have watched the cinnabar veins be emptied. I have watched one Omega prototype after another be copied off the World Tree Remnant and walked out into the world."

He raised his right hand.

It was a precision mechanical prosthesis, every joint inscribed with minute Latin characters, the metal at the fingertips giving off a cool, pewter gleam in the dying light.

"Three hundred years," he said, calmly. "What you see is what is left of me — eighty-two percent mechanical structure, eleven percent cinnabar circulatory system, the remaining seven percent my original flesh. The flesh is concentrated in the cranium and around the heart. My brain is still my own. I remember every day of the last three centuries."

"Including Franco," Cesare said.

"He was my student." Leonardo's voice did not change. "And my best. I spent a hundred and fifty years raising him, pouring the whole of da Vinci Borgia's mechanical knowledge into him, making him the finest Minister-General Minerva ever had. It is a pity he betrayed me in the end. Betrayed the family. Betrayed the mission."

He looked down at his mechanical hand.

"I once had a real pair of hands. With them I drew the first diagrams of the World Tree. With them I cast the skeleton of the first Seraph. With them I set the holy emblem into the black iron gate myself. Later, cinnabar ate the skin of my hands, and I had them replaced. Later still it ate my lungs, and I had them replaced. Bit by bit, the human part of me grew smaller. In the end only this seven percent was left."

"Why?" Cesare asked.

"Because I do not wish to die." Leonardo looked at him. "The first Pope — my ancestor — found the World Tree Remnant on the Avalon ice fields. It was a living mechanical tree, and cinnabar was its sap. The fruit that grew on it was the Omega prototype. The first Pope brought the Remnant back to the West, founded the Minerva Bureau and the Bureau of Original Sin, founded the Holy Church of the Messiah and the Papal States. But he did one thing I have never been able to forgive."

His voice stayed perfectly level.

"He sealed the World Tree Remnant with half of his own consciousness, and so prevented the Mechanical Kingdom from restarting. He was both my ancestor and my greatest enemy. He split himself into two — one called Pope Borgia the First, who wished to unmake the world; one called da Vinci Borgia, who wished to save it. These two identities struggled against each other for three hundred years. In the end da Vinci won. With his own hands he sealed away the first Pope's consciousness, and locked the Papal States onto a gentler road."

"But you disagreed," Cesare said.

"Disagreed is too small a word." Leonardo shook his head. "I am the direct descendant of da Vinci Borgia. The blood of both the first Pope and of da Vinci runs in my veins. I inherited the whole of their memories, their knowledge, their obsessions. I watched da Vinci take three hundred years to imprison the first Pope's consciousness. I watched the gate of the Mechanical Kingdom be locked. I watched the World Tree Remnant sleep beneath Vesuvius. I watched the cinnabar be mined and refined and rationed out, carefully, carefully —"

"All of it was a mistake," he said. "The world could have been better. If the Mechanical Kingdom were restarted, cinnabar would no longer be scarce. Plague and famine could be rooted out entirely. War would lose its meaning and die. All mankind would become part of the Kingdom."

"At what price?" Cesare asked.

"Free will." Leonardo said it as though he were naming a tool that had outlived its usefulness. "Human beings are flawed. They make war out of greed. They murder one another out of fear. They repeat the same foolishness out of ignorance. The Mechanical Kingdom, governed by a single will — my will — would purge the world of all these instabilities."

"Including the East," Cesare said.

"The East must be conquered." Leonardo inclined his head. "The Xia realm and its shamanic traditions descend in a direct line from the pre-cataclysm civilizations. They hold a great number of pre-cataclysm ruins unknown to us. If the East were to find those ruins before we did, the key to the Mechanical Kingdom would fall into their hands. So I drew up the Holy War Plan, to march the Papal armies across the East and build an empire that reaches from the Atlantic to the Pacific."

"Ruled by you," Cesare said.

"By me," Leonardo agreed, calmly. "I am the new Messiah. I shall sit at the crown of the World Tree Remnant and rule the whole earth."

"That is your purpose," Cesare said.

"That is not only my purpose." Leonardo looked at him. "It is also the purpose for which you were brought into this world."

Cesare said nothing.

"You think yourself an accident," Leonardo went on. "You think your violet eyes, your gifts, your destiny, are all a matter of chance. You are wrong. I have spent three hundred years selecting, training, arranging every person in your life —"

He extended his mechanical right hand toward Cesare.

"Your mother, the Lady Linglong, I chose from the last bloodline of the Ceylonese Star-Seers. The last of the Star-Seers, who numbered herself Remnant 01, sealed the World Tree Remnant with her own blood and bone. But her line did not die out. I found the last inheritor of that line and placed her beside the Pope. She fell in love with the Pope — that was not in my plan — but the outcome was better than the plan. She bore you."

"What did you say?" Cesare's voice dropped very low.

"You are the perfect adapter I have been carrying for three hundred years." Leonardo spoke as though he were reading from an inventory. "You must possess both the violet-eyed Star-Seer blood of Ceylon and the mechanical-adaptive genes of the Borgia line. Both are required, neither alone will do. In the whole of the West you are the only one whose veins carry both. The Lady Linglong was a piece I placed beside the Pope. She bore you to complete the last step in the restart of the Mechanical Kingdom."

"No," Cesare said.

"I beg your pardon?"

"She was not for you." Cesare's voice was level. "She loved my father. She loved me. She bore me because she wanted a home."

Leonardo was quiet for a moment.

"Does it matter?" he asked.

"It matters." Cesare said. "You spent three hundred years at your chessboard, made my mother a piece, made me a tool, made every one of us a piece. You would even deny your own ancestor. Da Vinci Borgia gave three hundred years of his life to stop the first Pope from restarting the Mechanical Kingdom, and you have spent three hundred years trying to finish what the first Pope could not."

"He is my ancestor," Leonardo said.

"He is also your greatest enemy." Cesare's voice came evenly. "He did not deny you because he did not understand the goodness of the Mechanical Kingdom. He denied you because he understood —"

Cesare stopped.

"— that human beings are not instabilities."

Something that might almost have been interest passed through Leonardo's eyes.

"What are human beings?" he asked.

"They are the creatures who make mistakes." Cesare said. "They grow greedy. They grow afraid. They murder one another. But they also love. They will throw their lives in front of a stranger's child, for no reason at all except that the child is there. The Lady Linglong did not love my father because my blood could be plugged into a World Tree. She loved him because he was willing to dance with her in the autumn light of Florence. Professor Franco did not teach me to read my own eyes because he wanted to make me into your tool. He taught me because he was, in fact, my teacher."

"These feelings," Leonardo said, "are precisely the instabilities you have just named."

"No." Cesare said. "These feelings are humanity's most powerful weapon."

Leonardo was quiet, looking at him.

The dusk had come down fully now. The sky above the Wangwu range had gone from a deep red to a deep violet, and the thousand-odd Omega prototypes in the distance gave back a dull, cold gold of their own — a silent steel forest, watching.

"Your notion of human nature is interesting," Leonardo said, at length. "But perhaps you do not yet know that I tested another man, by the same method."

"Who?"

"Lohenstein."

Cesare's eyes drew a fraction narrower.

"That name you have heard before, I think. The Black Dragon of the Seraphic Order, once the foremost knight in the world, the traitor who forsook the Papal States and threw in his lot with the Satanic Congregation. You must have believed he turned coat for the sake of his sleeping betrothed, Tilan."

"Did he not?"

"That was the surface of it." Leonardo's tone was the tone of a man recounting some anecdote in which he had never truly been involved. "Tilan was indeed a rare-grade adapter. The Curia grew impatient and tried to rush her into service as a Seraph knight, and the armor ate through her nervous system. She became a living corpse. Lohenstein hated the Curia for that. But he had no means of taking her with him — a living corpse locked in a black iron casket, watched over day and night by the Seraphic Order."

"He needed a force outside the Order," Cesare said.

"He needed me." Leonardo corrected him. "I offered him a choice. Men of the Satanic Congregation would help him steal Tilan, and would help him find the means to repair her ruined nerves. In return, he would do three things for me."

"The first." Leonardo held up one metal finger. "Test the new prototype Seraph I had been developing — the same chassis your Red Dragon is descended from. I needed to know what it could do in real combat. I needed to see where the adapter coupling would break."

"The second." A second finger rose. "Take Tilan. In the confusion, tear the Royal Marston College of Mechanism apart, and keep both the Minerva Bureau and the Curia too busy to look elsewhere."

"The third." He looked at Cesare. "After it was done, plant every false clue in the world on you."

The mountain road went quiet for a few seconds.

"Lohenstein took Tilan, and he also laid the theft of the Seraph armor at your door. You were a first-year student then. You had done nothing to earn a name, and yet you were charged with the private hoarding of a holy relic." Leonardo's voice was the voice of a man reading aloud from a ledger. "Your mother, in order to ransom you from the charge, had no choice but to accept King Didier of Charlemagne's offer of marriage."

"That betrothal —" Cesare's voice came from between his teeth.

"Was also arranged by me." Leonardo said. "King Didier wanted a Borgia daughter for his son, and you needed a betrothal heavy enough to buy your freedom. I simply pushed a little, on both sides."

Cesare's fingers closed, slowly, around the grip of his sword.

"Did Lohenstein know who you were?" he asked.

"He did not know who I was," Leonardo said. "He knew only that there was a hidden power that could help him steal Tilan, and could help him find the witch Bernadette who knew how to raise the dead — Bernadette herself, of course, was another of my pieces, another strand in my three-hundred-year plan. But after he had Tilan in hand, Lohenstein discovered that her nerve-damage could not be repaired by ordinary means. He would need my further help."

"So he became your piece."

"A temporary piece." Leonardo inclined his head. "Once Tilan's problem was solved, he had no further use. A knight ruled by his feelings is the very best illustration of the instabilities you have just described."

"Perhaps you are right about that," Leonardo concluded, after a pause. "But the Mechanical Kingdom has no need of weapons. It has need of order. And order requires that every soul surrender its feelings, and become part of the Kingdom."

"Then I will be the first."

Cesare raised his hand. The broken tip of the Excalibur shard leveled itself at Leonardo.

"You have been wrong for three hundred years," he said. "Today I will show you where."

At that exact moment, the golden bushing at the back of his neck flared hot.

It was not the burning of the King Immortal mode. It was a different sort of heat — the vibration of a Minerva Bureau frequency of the highest encryption. He drew a thumb-sized receiver from his belt, and Violante's voice came through it as clearly as though she were standing at his elbow.

"Cesare. The bomb is assembled."

Cesare's fingers paused on the receiver.

"The second-generation Prometheus cinnabar core Blue Sturgeon left us is in place. The ignition key has been taken off your mother's locket pendant." Violante's voice was steady, professional, and at the same time not quite steady. "There is only the last step remaining. We need your blood, dropped onto the key, to bring it to the threshold state."

"Understood," Cesare said.

"Cesare." Something else had crept into her voice. "In da Vinci's design for Brahma's Fall there is a switch he left. If it is thrown, the blast radius collapses from fifty kilometers to five hundred meters. But —"

"I know," Cesare said. "The cost is me."

The receiver was silent for a moment.

"You don't have to —" Violante began.

"Violante." Cesare cut her off. "Have the bomb ready. I am coming."

He killed the line.

On the mountain road, the Augustus Seraph Quintian was piloting came around the far curve of the path, slow and heavy. He had been hammered into the cliff face by Goulonoth a moment before, but the mithril tower-shield had taken the worst of the blow. The five cross-forged layers of shadow-metal and hard gold had only surface cracks to show for it — the ears of the lion sigil were knocked off, the lion's eyes had been split by fissures, but the shield was still on its feet.

"Chief." Quintian's voice came through the line, hoarse. "I heard."

"What did you hear?" Cesare asked.

"I heard you say that human feeling is the most powerful weapon a man has." Quintian said. "I don't know what kind of horseshit that is. But Chief, you once said you were going to take me back to Florence and fight beside me there, and I haven't had that many good fights with you yet."

He lifted the mithril tower-shield.

"So you are not allowed to die."

"Solomon is in position." Alfonso's voice came through, even, level. "Alfonso Castro, standing by."

"The Wraith of the Rose can still move." Don Juan's voice was next. "Don Juan Morales, standing by."

"The modified Divine Wrath III has its target locked." Valentina's voice, after. "Valentina Romanov, standing by."

Chu Shunhua said nothing. His Wraith-Warrior II, at the other end of the mountain road, raised its heavy steel tower-shield. The blade of the Kuilong-horn sword caught the dusk and threw it back as a cold white line.

Cesare looked at them.

"Cover me," he said.

He turned and began to run, in the direction of the dark passage that led down to the main root chamber of the World Tree. The Excalibur shard was in his hand, and along its edge the cinnabar traceries gave back a dull gold, like a length of branch that had not quite stopped burning.

Behind him, Augustus lifted the tower-shield and walked to meet Goulonoth.

"Come on, then." Quintian's voice came out in a roar, and he brought the shield down hard against the great blade.

Metal on metal went off on the mountain road with a sound like a depth charge — a great whale turning over, somewhere in the dark.

Goulonoth's raptor-class power core redlined above its design limit. Self-healing nerve-fibers inside the chassis grew at a frantic rate, patching the cracked joint systems back to working order. The great blade came down with annihilating force, and the Augustus shield caught it.

The mithril tower-shield made a low, mournful sound.

Five cross-forged layers of shadow-metal and hard gold twisted under the force. The lion's eyes split all the way through. The crack ran down through the lion's open mouth. But the shield did not break.

Quintian's greaves sank into the rock of the road. The whole frame was shoved back a half-step by the force. But his arms did not bend.

"Alfonso!" he roared.

"Already running." Alfonso's voice, perfectly level.

The breastplate of the Solomon chassis opened. Six little mechanical spiders were launched from the spider-nest wristlet, trailing fine cables through the night air in six arcing lines. Their abdomens were inset with high-purity cinnabar micro-crystals. In flight they made a small gear-on-gear sound, like six bronze little beasts tapping at a door.

Those six were the vanguard.

More came. They dropped out of the dark, came up out of the ground, crawled out of the brush — sharing a single mind, answering the resonance of the golden bushing at the back of Cesare's neck. Hundreds of bronze spiders converged on Goulonoth, each one carrying a cinnabar micro-crystal in its belly.

"Detonate," Alfonso said, under his breath.

At the same moment, hundreds of cinnabar micro-crystals went off inside hundreds of bronze spider bellies.

A broadband electromagnetic pulse bloomed out around Goulonoth in a perfect sphere, and for an instant the dark of the road went briefly, horribly blue. The pulse was tuned to Omega prototype nerve-bridging systems — to scramble the self-healing fibers, to confuse the rhythm of the cinnabar core. Leonardo's mechanical body shuddered once, hard, under the wave. The cinnabar chips in his joints gave out a high thin whine. He raised his right hand as if to catch something, and the fingers, under the interference, trembled out of his control.

"A petty trick." Leonardo's voice stayed level. He looked down at his own trembling mechanical arm. The chips in it pulsed, on and off, on and off, under the static.

"Yes," Alfonso said. "A petty trick. But a petty trick that will cost you three minutes to recover from."

"Three minutes will be enough," Cesare's voice said, on the line.

On the mountain road, the shape of him was already gone, into the dark mouth of the passage that led down to the main root chamber.

The Wraith of the Rose drew a pale line across the night, curving in toward Goulonoth's exposed cabling from the rear quarter.

"Cover the Chief!" Don Juan roared.

The mithril tower-shield caught the great blade a second time.

This time, the shield did not crack.

But somewhere in the Augustus chassis, a piece of metal gave out with a brittle, snapping sound — the bearing of the left shoulder joint, twisted straight through by the force. Gears came spitting out of the joint and went hissing into the air, trailing a few sparks.

Quintian did not step back.

He took the mithril shield in the one good arm that was left to him, and held it high, between Goulonoth and the dark mouth of the passage.

"Chief," he said, under his breath. "I still owe you for the wine."
