【中文】
第248章 假面下的陷阱

唐璜跑得很快。他没走大路。从墓园出来之后他就钻进了一片废弃的工人宿舍区，绕过三个巡逻岗哨，沿着一条他两年前踩过点的暗巷来到了城南区的主干道边缘。凌晨四点的翡冷翠城南依然有零星的蒸汽货车在跑，但让唐璜放慢脚步的不是货车——是一队人。十二个圣堂装甲师的制式军服，胸口银色双翼徽记，腰间制式短铳，走在最前面的那个人让唐璜几乎要骂出声。法比奥。假面骑士兄弟会的前任会长。

他没穿学生制服，一身圣堂装甲师中尉军服，肩章和袖口金线绣花，胸口别着假面骑士兄弟会的撕裂面具交叉长剑徽记。路灯下他的脸格外苍白，嘴角挂着唐璜认得不能再认得的假笑。他转过头对身边士兵说了句什么，风把声音送进巷子："——老师交代过，今晚要把那个叫碧儿的女人转移到叹息之墙去。格拉古大主教亲自下的命令。"脚步声消失在城南方向。唐璜蹲在阴影里，等了整整五分钟才直起身来。然后他转身，朝教堂墓园的方向飞奔。

据点在圣玛格丽特教堂地下。上校当年修建的旧锅炉房改造的密室，佛朗哥教授提前留下的安全屋。唐璜推开那扇伪装成储物柜的铁门时，西泽尔正坐在一张被油灯照亮的木桌前，面前铺着翡冷翠的城区地图。阿方索站在角落里擦他那副蜘蛛巢腕表，瓦莲京娜靠在墙边擦拭改装神怒Ⅲ型的备用蒸汽阀，昆提良抱着双臂靠着柱子假寐。

唐璜进来的时候带进了一股冷风和铁锈味。

"十二个。"他开口就报数，"法比奥带队，十二个假面骑士兄弟会的老成员，全穿着圣堂装甲师中尉军服，方向是坎特伯雷堡。"

昆提良猛地睁开眼睛。阿方索停下了擦腕表的动作。瓦莲京娜的目光从蒸汽阀上移过来，落在唐璜脸上。

西泽尔没抬头。他的手指按在地图上坎特伯雷堡的位置，指甲发白。

"他说了什么。"西泽尔的声音很平。

"格拉古大主教亲自下的命令，今夜转移碧儿去叹息之墙。"唐璜走到桌边，手指按在地图上坎特伯雷堡的南侧门，"他们刚从城南主干道过去，按脚程算，我追不上了。但如果他们要进堡提人再走，从坎特伯雷堡到叹息之墙怎么都要经过东城门外的碎石路……"

"不用追。"西泽尔终于抬起头来。

油灯把他的脸照得半明半暗，紫瞳在阴影中像两枚燃着冷焰的煤。

"你现在去坎特伯雷堡。"

唐璜怔了一下："碧儿已经在被转移了，我去堡里能做什么？"

"确认人还在不在堡里。"西泽尔说，"法比奥说要把碧儿转移到叹息之墙，但圣域条例规定——圣堂装甲师指挥官必须分兵去备用指挥所待命，莱希特伯爵不可能亲自带一个小队执行这种杂务。法比奥是中尉，不是指挥官，他没有权力单独押送A级人质进叹息之墙。"

"你的意思是——"唐璜眯起了眼睛。

"如果碧儿真的在法比奥手里，那法比奥背后不是格拉古大主教。"西泽尔说，"格拉古大主教要的是灭口，不会把一个A级人质交给十二个假面兄弟会的人。除非——"

"除非法比奥根本不是去接人，是去抢人。"唐璜接了下去，"抢在圣堂装甲师真正的人到之前，先把碧儿带走。"

西泽尔看了他一眼，没有确认也没有否认，只是说："去看看。"

唐璜点头，转身就走。

"等等。"瓦莲京娜从墙边走过来，从腰间解下一枚戒指丢给他。那是一枚暗银色的指环，内侧刻着叶尼塞忍冬花的花纹。"戴上，你那张脸在翡冷翠上城区被通缉。"

唐璜接住戒指，套在右手无名指上。暗银色的金属贴着他的皮肤微凉。"忍冬花。"他对着油灯看了看，苦笑，"瓦莲京娜公主殿下的求婚戒指我收了。"

"那不是求婚戒指。"瓦莲京娜面无表情，"是叶尼塞外交使团的临时通行证。戴上了遇到盘查就说自己是使团随员。"

"……"唐璜把戒指转了个面，"我就不能做两秒钟的美梦吗？"

他没等回答，拉开铁门消失在夜色中。

坎特伯雷堡在翡冷翠城东，是一座有着三百年历史的灰石建筑。唐璜用二十分钟绕到了堡的北面，蹲在一棵老橡树后面。堡门前的石阶上站着四个哨兵，圣堂装甲师的深灰制服，胸口银色双翼，但腰间挎的不是制式短铳——是一种更短更粗的东西，枪管上缠绕着细细的铜线圈。唐璜眯起眼看了几秒，认出来了。那是经过改装的短管雷霆牙，连射型，近距离能把人打成筛子。

不是普通哨兵的装备。

堡门口两侧的石柱上各嵌着一块拳头大小的灰白色金属板，金属板表面有细密的纹路在缓慢闪烁，像是某种感知装置。纹路的颜色每隔三秒变一次——暗红、暗金、暗红、暗金。欧米茄感应装置。唐璜的心猛地沉了一下。这种装置是圣堂装甲师专门用于侦测欧米茄级能量信号的，凡携带超过阈值红水银的人经过，装置就会亮起红色警报。

他没有红水银武器，蔷薇之鬼的甲胄还留在密涅瓦机关。但他的腰带里塞着四枚微型炸弹——蔷薇之鬼专用的那种，钉头大小，红水银填充量刚好够炸断一条成年人的腿。

唐璜从树后直起身来，整理了一下衣领。他现在穿的是一件从据点储藏室里翻出来的黑色燕尾礼服，剪裁得体，领口别着一枚铜质胸针——那是他前天在翡冷翠跳蚤市场花两枚银币买的，号称是美第奇家族十七世纪的传家徽章，实际上镀铜的破烂货，美杜莎的脸被磨得只剩一条蛇尾巴。但从三步远的地方看，足够唬人。

他右手无名指上的忍冬花戒指在月光下闪着暗银色的光。

他从橡树后走出来，沿着石阶慢慢往上走。脚步不急不缓，脸上挂着一种翡冷翠贵族少爷特有的、懒洋洋的倦怠。走到距堡门还有十步的时候，最近的哨兵转过了头。

"站住。"哨兵的声音很冷，"口令。"

唐璜在五步远的地方停下脚步，双手从口袋里抽出来，掌心朝上，展示着空空的手——这是翡冷翠街头惯用的"我没有武器"的手势。"晚上好。"他微微欠身，翡冷翠上流社会最标准的问候礼，"我是叶尼塞外交使团的随员，奉命来取一份落在坎特伯雷堡的行李——公主殿下的晚礼服，昨晚跳舞弄脏了没来得及带走。"

他说的是带有明显翡冷翠口音的意大利语，咬字精准，尾音上扬。这是他在翡冷翠上流社会混了三年的成果——每个音节都像是从贵族的沙龙里打磨出来的。

哨兵的眼睛从他的脸扫到他的燕尾服，又扫到领口的"美第奇家徽"胸针，再扫到他右手无名指上的忍冬花戒指。目光在戒指上停留了两秒。

"叶尼塞使团。"哨兵的语气微微松动，但枪口没有放下，"证件。"

唐璜从内袋里掏出一本深蓝色的小册子——那是瓦莲京娜临走前塞给他的，上面的叶尼塞皇室钢印是真的，只是名字是假的。他把册子递过去，同时用余光扫了一眼堡门两侧的感应装置。暗红。暗金。暗红。暗金。还在正常闪烁，没有因为他靠近而变色。

他身上没有红水银。

哨兵翻开册子看了看，又翻到最后一页看了看钢印，把册子还给他。"叶尼塞使团为什么凌晨四点来取行李？"

"因为公主殿下五点要换衣服。"唐璜说，"您知道她五点要出席枢机会的——"

"嗡——"

一声尖锐的高频啸叫突然从堡门左侧的感应装置中爆发出来。不是警报，是那种金属板过载时发出的尖啸。暗金色的纹路猛地变成了刺目的猩红。

哨兵的脸色瞬间变了。他的手按上了腰间改装雷霆牙的枪柄。

唐璜的心沉到了底。

不是因为他身上的红水银——他确信自己身上没有。是因为他刚才把瓦莲京娜给的那本册子递出去的时候，手指碰到了哨兵的手。哨兵的手套是普通的皮手套，不是绝缘的。

瓦莲京娜的册子上有叶尼塞皇室的钢印。钢印的墨水里掺了极微量的红水银防伪。

感应装置的过载阈值是S级——但哪怕是A级信号，它也会亮红灯。圣堂装甲师安装这种装置的目的就是不放过任何一丝红水银信号。瓦莲京娜的册子是一份外交证件，不是武器，但它足够触发感应装置的反应。

哨兵猛地后退一步，枪已经拔出来了。改装雷霆牙的枪口正对着唐璜的胸口。

"双手举起来！慢慢举！"

唐璜的脑子在零点三秒内转过了一百个念头。逃——不行，堡门前是开阔地，他跑不过子弹。解释——不行，叶尼塞使团的身份现在反而是罪证。硬闯——更不行，四个哨兵都是改装雷霆牙。

他选择了第三种。

"先生们，"他缓缓地举起了双手，掌心朝前，声音依然保持着贵族少爷的从容，"我想这里面有误会。我是叶尼塞使团的人，我的证件——"

堡门内传来沉重的脚步声。

铁门从里面被人推开了一条缝，一个人影从黑暗中走了出来。军靴踏在石阶上发出清脆的响声。

法比奥。

他又换了一套衣服——不，是同一套中尉军服，只是外面多披了一件黑色斗篷，斗篷的领子竖起来挡住了半张脸。但他胸口的撕裂面具交叉长剑徽记没有摘，在月光下反射出一道冷光。

他的右手无名指上戴着一枚戒指。不是圣堂装甲师的军戒——那是一枚唐璜认得的、刻着查理曼皇室百合花纹的金质戒指。查理曼皇室授勋的标志。法比奥是查理曼的人。或者说，他至少拿了查理曼皇室的好处。

法比奥看见唐璜的时候，那张假笑的脸上闪过一丝真实的表情——是意外。然后意外变成了冷笑。

"唐璜。"他的声音在夜风中显得格外清晰，"好久不见。"

唐璜在心底骂了一句，脸上却笑了。

"法比奥。"他微微欠身，"我以为你还在马斯顿被退学呢，没想到你混进了圣堂装甲师——了不起，什么时候的事？"

"上次你在马斯顿跟西泽尔跑了之后，格拉古大主教给了我一个机会。"法比奥走下石阶，停在距唐璜五步远的地方。他的军靴踩在石阶上，皮质斗篷的下摆随着动作轻轻摇摆。身后跟着六个人——也是圣堂装甲师军服，但腰间挎着一种更奇怪的武器。枪管极短，前端焊接了拇指大小的金属圆盘，圆盘上刻着细密的纹路。仿制炽天使级武器。不是真正的炽天使——真正的炽天使武器只有炽天骑士团才有——但仿制品也足以在三步之内把人打穿。

假面骑士兄弟会果然不简单。法比奥在这几年里不知道搭上了哪条线。

"叶尼塞使团的随员？"法比奥看着唐璜，笑容加深了，"有意思。西泽尔的狗换了一张皮，我就认不出来了？"

唐璜的笑容没有变。"法比奥，你这话说的，我们好歹在马斯顿同窗过——"

"我从来没跟你同窗过。"法比奥打断他，"你们这些下城区来的垃圾，从来不配跟我同窗。"

他抬起了右手。

不是挥手——是握拳。拳心里攥着一枚拳头大小的暗金色金属球，金属球表面有细密纹路在闪烁。唐璜认出来了——那是一枚浓缩红水银的信号弹。捏碎它就会爆发出超过A级阈值的红水银能量脉冲，足以触发方圆五十米内所有欧米茄感应装置发出最高级别警报。

如果他捏碎它，翡冷翠城防军和圣堂装甲师的主力都会在五分钟内赶到坎特伯雷堡。

"放下你的手。"法比奥对哨兵们说，然后他转向唐璜，"或者说，我捏碎这个，今晚你就别想走了。"

"……"唐璜的笑容终于消失了。

"西泽尔派你来侦察的，对吧？"法比奥偏了偏头，"他在哪？"

唐璜看着他，没说话。

"不说也没关系。"法比奥的假笑又浮了上来，"我知道他在翡冷翠。我也知道他迟早会来——因为碧儿·丹缇就在这座堡里。他不可能不来救她。"

碧儿还在堡里。

这个信息像一根针刺进了唐璜的太阳穴。法比奥说"就在这座堡里"——意味着碧儿没有被转移出去。法比奥在撒谎，或者——格拉古大主教的命令被法比奥截胡了。法比奥不是来执行转移命令的，他是来抢人的。

唐璜的手指无声地触碰到了腰带里那四枚微型炸弹的其中一枚。蔷薇之鬼专用，红水银填充量刚好够炸断一条成年人的腿——但在这种距离下，爆炸的冲击波也会伤到他自己。

"法比奥。"唐璜忽然笑了。

那是一种唐璜式的笑——嘴角上扬，眼睛里却没有笑意，像一把折叠刀在慢慢打开。

"你知道我以前在翡冷翠是干什么的吗？"

法比奥挑了挑眉。

"偷东西。"唐璜说，"偷贵族的怀表，偷贵妇人的珠宝，偷小姐们的心——"他的右手忽然动了。

快得像一道闪电。

四枚微型炸弹中的一枚被他用拇指弹出了腰带。炸弹在石阶上弹了一下——直接滚到了法比奥的脚下。法比奥的瞳孔骤然——不，不是骤然收缩——是终于意识到发生了什么。法比奥猛地往后跳，拳头猛地张开，暗金色的信号弹脱手飞了出去——

炸弹先响了。

红水银的爆炸不是火焰，而是一团暗红色的光芒，伴随着尖锐的气浪。法比奥的右腿膝盖下方被直接命中——不是炸断，是炸开。爆炸的冲击波带着红水银的碎片撕开了他的军裤和皮肉，血在月光下飞溅。法比奥惨叫着倒下去，信号弹从他手中飞出去落在三步远的石阶上，暗金色的光芒在石阶上滚动——

"开枪！"一个哨兵嘶吼。

四支改装雷霆牙同时开火。

唐璜已经在动了。他没有往上跑——他往堡门的方向扑去。法比奥倒下的位置正好在堡门台阶的边缘，哨兵们的射击角度被法比奥的身体挡住了一瞬。唐璜趁着这一瞬的空隙，翻过了法比奥的身体，肩膀撞开了半掩的堡门铁扇——

铁扇内部是一道长廊，灰色石壁，两侧各嵌着一面欧米茄感应装置。感应装置已经在他冲进来的瞬间同时变成了猩红色——他在外面引爆的那枚炸弹释放的红水银能量已经通过门缝渗了进来。

他没时间管这些。他从长廊的尽头撞开了另一扇门——厨房后门。厨房里还亮着灯，两个仆人正在洗碗，看见一个浑身是血的陌生男人冲进来，发出了一声尖叫。唐璜没理他们，从厨房后门翻出去，落在了一条狭窄的仆人通道里。通道的尽头是堡的后门——

后门是锁着的。

唐璜用了一秒——他用从厨房顺手抓来的一把切肉刀砍断了门闩，木头碎裂的声音在夜里格外响亮。门开了。他冲进了后巷。

巷子里停着一辆蒸汽货车——是坎特伯雷堡的杂货车。唐璜想都没想，爬上驾驶座，拉开节气阀。蒸汽机的轰鸣声在后巷里炸开，货车猛地冲了出去。巷子太窄，货车的右侧挡泥板撞在了墙上，金属和石头摩擦出一串火花。他没管。冲出巷口的时候，一个哨兵从正门追了过来，枪口对准了货车——

唐璜一打方向盘，货车的整个车头撞上了正门台阶的边缘。哨兵被撞飞了。货车冲上了主路。

他的身后，坎特伯雷堡的警报终于响了——不是欧米茄感应装置的警报，是更原始的铜钟声。铛、铛、铛。堡里所有的哨兵都会听到。

唐璜把节气阀拉到了底。货车在翡冷翠空旷的凌晨街道上咆哮着，车轮碾过石板路发出连续的震响。他的脑子里在高速运转——碧儿不在堡里。碧儿——不，法比奥说碧儿在堡里。但法比奥在那种情况下说谎没有意义。所以碧儿确实在堡里，只是还没有被带走。法比奥带着十二个假面兄弟会来——是为了赶在圣堂装甲师的真正押送队到达之前，把碧儿从格拉古大主教的手中截走。法比奥不是格拉古的人——法比奥是查理曼的人。

查理曼要碧儿做什么？

他想不通。但他把这个信息存进了脑子里。其他的——回去再说。

二十分钟后，他把货车丢在了城南的一个废弃仓库里。他步行回到了圣玛格丽特教堂。

推开铁门的时候，阿方索正在给蜘蛛巢腕表更换微型轴承。看见唐璜身上的血——不是他的血，是法比奥的血——阿方索的手停了一下。

"法比奥。"唐璜说。

西泽尔抬起头来。

"法比奥带着十二个假面兄弟会来，不是执行格拉古的转移命令——是来截胡的。"唐璜走到桌边，"他在堡门口拦住了我。他带着查理曼皇室的授勋戒指。"

昆提良站直了。"查理曼？"

"法比奥是查理曼的人。或者说至少是查理曼收买的。"唐璜说，"他用红水银信号弹威胁我，我用炸弹炸伤了他的右腿——"

"你暴露了。"西泽尔说。

"是。"唐璜承认，"但我得到了一个信息：碧儿还在堡里。"

房间里安静了一秒。

"阿黛尔呢？"昆提良问。

唐璜的嘴张了张，又闭上了。他不知道。他没法知道——他根本没进到堡的内部。

"我听到法比奥的命令只提到了碧儿。"他说，"但这也可能是法比奥故意说给我听的。真实情况——"

"我听到了。"阿方索忽然说。

所有人看向他。

阿方索从口袋里掏出了那台便携式神经电流读出器。那是从佛朗哥教授的遗物中取出的B-07档案库设备。阿方索在过去几天里对它进行了改装——加装了一根细长的接收天线，能够捕捉到方圆两百米内所有的神经电流信号。

"我刚才放在了你身上。"阿方索说，"在你袖口里。"

唐璜低头看了看自己的袖口——那里面确实有一粒米粒大小的金属片，他竟然完全没注意到。

阿方索按下了一个按钮。读出器上的小型投影屏亮了，显示出一条波形曲线。曲线上有两个明显的波峰——一个是唐璜自己的神经电流特征，另一个更强、更规律、带着一种特殊的低频震荡。

"我在你进入坎特伯雷堡的时候接收到了两组神经电流信号。"阿方索说，"一组是碧儿·丹缇的——我能确认，她的信号特征之前我在密涅瓦机关的数据库里见过。另一组——"

他停了一下。

"另一组是一个十五到十八岁的女性，神经电流特征与碧儿不同，带有明显的红水银残留波动。信号源位置——"阿方索指了指投影屏上的方位角，"在坎特伯雷堡的地下室。"

十五到十八岁的女性。红水银残留。

阿黛尔在西泽尔离开翡冷翠后接受过枢机会的"治疗"——那是枢机会为了获取西泽尔神经接驳数据而对阿黛尔进行的强制红水银浸泡实验。阿黛尔的神经系统里至今还残留着红水银的痕迹。

"碧儿和阿黛尔都在堡里。"西泽尔的声音很轻，像是确认一件他已经知道的事情。

他站起来。

"计划变了。今晚——"他看着地图上坎特伯雷堡的位置，然后手指慢慢划向了东北方向的维苏威火山，"法比奥是查理曼的人。他来截胡碧儿——不是为格拉古大主教。查理曼需要碧儿——或者说，需要碧儿身上携带的某种东西。"

"什么东西？"昆提良问。

"情报。"西泽尔说，"碧儿曾经是教皇厅的档案员。她手里有梵蒂冈档案室的访问权限——即使那个权限已经被撤销了，但她脑子里记住的东西不会消失。"

"查理曼要的是碧儿脑子里的情报。"阿方索说。

"迪迪埃国王。"唐璜脱口而出，"查理曼的迪迪埃国王。他想要——"

"教皇国对东方作战的全部计划。"西泽尔说，"《宗教秘密法》第四十七条的内容，教皇厅的绝密文件，以及——"

他停了一下。

"——以及关于我的全部档案。"

房间里的空气凝固了。

"你的档案里有什么？"昆提良问。

西泽尔没有回答。他从桌边拿起了一件黑色外套——那是瓦莲京娜之前给他的A级防火防爆服，外层是普通的黑色棉质夹克，内衬缝有影金属丝线。他把外套搭在肩上，扣子一颗一颗系好。

"唐璜。"他说。

"在。"

"你炸伤了法比奥的腿。假面兄弟会的人今晚会撤出坎特伯雷堡——法比奥需要治疗，他不可能带着一条断腿继续执行任务。"西泽尔说，"他们撤走的时候，堡里只剩下圣堂装甲师的常规哨兵——那些哨兵不是法比奥的人。"

"你要去救碧儿和阿黛尔。"唐璜说。

"是。"

"一个人？"

"我一个人。"

"老板——"唐璜的脸色变了。

"我们分兵四路。"西泽尔打断他，"不能把所有人都投入一个目标。昆提良去联络退役的炽天铁骑；阿方索跟薇若兰走备份通道进武器库解锁装备；瓦莲京娜去联络叶尼塞使团制造外交骚乱。我去坎特伯雷堡。"

他看着唐璜。

"你去维苏威火山。"

"维苏威火山？"唐璜愣住了。

"法比奥的人虽然会撤出坎特伯雷堡，但碧儿和阿黛尔不会留在堡里太久——圣堂装甲师的真正押送队很快会到。你需要先去维苏威火山确认一条路。"西泽尔说，"我救出她们两个之后，会带着她们从坎特伯雷堡撤出，沿着东城门外的碎石路往东北方向走——维苏威火山的北麓矿道入口。"

"那是——"阿方索的脸色微变，"你打算带她们进骷髅地？"

"不是骷髅地。是维苏威火山的外围矿道。"西泽尔说，"佛朗哥教授在遗物里留过一张维苏威火山内部结构图——达·芬奇三百年前亲手绘制的。矿道入口有两条路可以通往山体深处。如果碧儿和阿黛尔必须撤离到安全地带，那里是唯一不会被圣堂装甲师包围的地方。"

唐璜沉默了。

"老板，"他最后说，"你一个人去坎特伯雷堡——那里至少还有四个哨兵。"

"哨兵不是问题。"西泽尔说，"法比奥撤走之后，堡里的防守会从假面兄弟会的精锐变成普通哨兵。那些哨兵没有改装雷霆牙，也没有仿制炽天使武器。我有办法进去。"

他看了唐璜一眼。

"你负责维苏威火山。确认矿道入口有没有被人布置陷阱。带好你的工具——"他从桌边拿起了一个小布袋扔给唐璜，"这是佛朗哥教授留下的小型通讯器。频率我已经调到了最高级别的加密频段——全世界知道这个频率的人不超过三个。你到了矿道入口后跟我保持联系。"

唐璜接住布袋，掂了掂重量。

"老板。"他看着西泽尔，"你不会真打算一个人去吧？"

西泽尔系好了外套最后一颗扣子，抬眼看他。

"不会。"

他从桌子下面抽出了一个长条形的黑色布包。布包打开——里面是一把剑。剑身弯曲如蛇，窄而长，覆着淡绿色的铜锈，剑柄缠着褪色的绿绢。

青蛇剑。达·芬奇留给继承者的七把名剑之一。材质与初代炽天使武器同源，刚好适配西泽尔的手掌。

"蔷薇之鬼的甲胄留在密涅瓦机关，没法用。"西泽尔把剑别在腰后，外套的下摆刚好遮住剑柄，"青蛇剑不是炽天使级别的武器，但对付普通哨兵够用了。"

"老板……"唐璜的嘴动了动。

"还有什么要说的？"

"有。"唐璜认真地看着他，"活着回来。"

西泽尔看了他一眼。然后他转身走向了铁门。

他拉开门的时候，身后传来了一阵轻微的震动。不是地面——是李锡尼的腰间。

李锡尼从角落里走出来。他一直坐在那里没有说话，但他的左手一直按在腰间的什么东西上。现在他的脸色变了。

他按着的是一个拇指大小的黄铜圆筒，圆筒表面有一道细小的蜡封裂缝。蜡封的裂缝里正透出一丝微弱的金色光芒。

佛朗哥的蜡封密信提示器。

李锡尼把它从腰间取下来，圆筒的开口处正在发出持续的轻微震动。震动通过黄铜传到了李锡尼的指尖——也传到了房间里每一个人的耳膜。

"这是——"李锡尼的声音变了，"佛朗哥的临终密信。他死前把最后一份密信的提示器设成了'骷髅地封印状态'的监测触发——只有当骷髅地的封印出现重大异常时，提示器才会震动。"

他看着那个正在震动的黄铜圆筒。

圆筒开口处的金色光芒猛地亮了一下，然后在黄铜表面投射出了一行极其微小的、几乎需要贴近才能看清的文字：

"骷髅地封印已松动。"

房间里死一般安静。

西泽尔站在门口，一只手按在青蛇剑的剑柄上。月光从门外照进来，把他的脸照得一半明一半暗。

"碧儿和阿黛尔——"他说，"在骷髅地。"

【English】
Chapter 248 — The Trap Behind the Mask

Don Juan ran.

He did not take the avenue. From the cemetery he cut into the abandoned workers' tenements east of the wall, slipped three patrol points he had marked two winters ago, and worked his way down a back alley that smelled of coal tar and cat piss until the south artery of Florence opened up under his feet. It was a little past four. Steam-carts still ground past in ones and twos, their boilers huffing white plumes into the black air, but it was not the carts that slowed him. It was the column of men.

Twelve of them, in the slate-grey greatcoats of the Holy Chapel Armoured Division, the silver double-wing pinned at every breast, holstered short-barrels at every hip. The man at their head made Don Juan nearly spit. Fabio. Former president of the Masked Knight Brotherhood, expelled from Marston for conduct unbecoming, now dressed — God save the irony — in the lieutenant's uniform of that same Chapel Division, gold cord on the epaulettes, gold thread at the cuffs, and over his heart the torn mask crossed with the long sword, the sigil of his old brotherhood, worn like a private joke.

The lamplight washed his face to a chalky white. The smile on his mouth was the one Don Juan remembered best — that practiced, affable curve that never touched the eyes. He turned to the man beside him and said something low, and the wind, that traitor wind, carried the words straight down the alley.

"—the Archbishop Gracchus has given the order. Tonight, that woman — Bier — is to be moved to the Wall of Sighs."

Their boots faded south. Don Juan stayed in the shadow of the wall, crouched, and counted to three hundred before he straightened his legs. Then he turned and ran north, hard, toward the spire of St. Margaret's.

The safe house was where Franco had put it, in the dead boiler-room beneath the church that the old professor had bricked off ten years before. Don Juan shouldered the iron door — disguised as a broom cupboard — and let the cold and the rust in with him.

Cesare was at the oil lamp. He had pushed a city map of Florence flat on the deal table, his finger pressed against the position of a building, and his fingernail had gone white where he pressed. Alfonso stood at the corner polishing the bracelet of his Spider Nest watch. Valentina leaned against the wall, working a backup steam-valve for a modified Wrath of God III with a piece of chamois. Quintilian was asleep on his feet against the pillar, arms folded, head down.

The door brought in a draft that swayed the lamp.

"Twelve," Don Juan said. "Fabio at the head. All old Masked Brotherhood, all in Chapel Division lieutenant's kit. Heading toward Canterbury."

Quintilian's eyes opened. Alfonso's hand stopped moving. Valentina's gaze lifted from the valve and settled on Don Juan's face.

Cesare did not look up. His finger was still on the map.

"What did he say."

"Archbishop Gracchus's own order. Move Bier tonight, to the Wall of Sighs." Don Juan crossed to the table, laid his hand on the south gate of Canterbury. "They were already past the south artery. By their pace I could not catch them. But if they are taking her out of the castle, the only road to the Wall goes through the broken stone track east of the eastern gate —"

"You won't catch them," Cesare said. He looked up at last.

The lamplight split his face down the middle. The violet of his eyes was the violet of a slow coal burning in a dead hearth.

"You will go to Canterbury."

Don Juan blinked. "Bier is already being moved. What am I going to find in the castle?"

"Whether she is still in it." Cesare's voice stayed level. "The Holy Domain statutes require the Chapel Division's commanding officer to detach a secondary company to a reserve command post before any prisoner transfer. Count Reichert would not personally lead a dozen men on a menial errand like this. Fabio is a lieutenant, not a commander. He has no authority to march a Class-A prisoner into the Wall of Sighs."

"So you mean —"

"If Bier is really in Fabio's hands, then Fabio is not acting for Gracchus." Cesare's finger did not move. "Gracchus wants her silenced. He would not hand a Class-A prisoner to twelve Masked Brotherhood veterans. Unless —"

"Unless Fabio isn't going to receive her." Don Juan finished it. "He's going to take her. Take her before the real Chapel Division escort arrives."

Cesare looked at him. He neither confirmed nor denied. He only said, "Go see."

Don Juan nodded. He turned to leave.

"Wait." Valentina pushed off the wall. She unclipped a ring from her belt and tossed it. He caught it. Dark silver, with a fine honeysuckle pattern worked into the inside band. "Put it on. That face of yours is wanted in the upper city."

He slipped it on the fourth finger of his right hand. The metal was cool against his skin. "Honeysuckle," he said, holding it up to the lamp. "Princess Valentina's proposal ring. I'm keeping it."

"It is not a proposal ring. It is a temporary pass for the Yenisei diplomatic legation. Wear it, and if you are stopped, say you are legation staff."

"Can't I have two seconds of the dream?"

He didn't wait for an answer. The iron door closed behind him, and the night took him back.

Canterbury stood east of the city, three centuries of grey stone heaped into the shape of a keep. Don Juan took twenty minutes to circle to its north side and crouched behind an old oak. Four sentries on the front steps. Chapel Division slate, silver wings, but the weapons on their hips were not regulation short-barrels. The guns were shorter, thicker; the barrels were wrapped in a tight spiral of copper wire. He narrowed his eyes. Modified Thunderteeth. Full auto, close range. The kind of gun that turned a man into a sieve.

The two gate-pillars each had a plate of dull grey-white metal set into the stone, the size of a man's fist. The plates flickered. Slow. Three seconds red, three seconds gold, three seconds red, three seconds gold. Omega detectors. His stomach dropped a quarter inch. Those were the Chapel Division's instruments for catching any trace of red mercury above threshold. Anyone carrying more than a trace would set them screaming.

He himself had no red mercury. The Rose Ghost armour was back at the Minerva Bureau. But the small of his belt held four micro-bombs — Rose Ghost special, thumb-head sized, red mercury payload just sufficient to take a grown man's leg off at the knee.

Don Juan stood up from behind the oak and straightened his collar. He had on a black tailcoat pulled from the safe-house store: good cut, copper pin at the throat — a two-silver-piece brooch bought two days ago at the Florence flea market, advertised as a Medici heirloom, in fact a piece of cheap copper plating with a Medusa worn down to a single serpent's tail. From three paces it passed. He adjusted it, and started up the steps.

The pace of a Florentine gentleman. Slow. Slightly bored. The bored, lazy slouch of a young man born to a certain kind of life, who has never once had to wonder whether the next man up the street might shoot him.

The nearest sentry turned his head ten paces out.

"Halt. The word."

Don Juan stopped. He drew both hands from his pockets, palms up — the old street sign for I am not holding anything. "Good evening," he said, and gave the smallest inclination of the upper body, the Florentine salute of the better houses. "I am a member of the Yenisei diplomatic legation. I am here to retrieve a piece of luggage left behind in the castle — Her Highness's evening gown, ruined at last night's dance, too soiled to send through the official channels."

Italian, with the unmistakable Florence upper-city tang. Every vowel placed, every consonant chewed. Three years of dinners at the wrong tables, learning exactly how a Borgia cousin clears his throat.

The sentry's eyes went from the face to the tailcoat to the Medici pin, and stopped on the ring.

"Yenisei legation. Identification."

Don Juan drew the little navy booklet from his breast pocket — Valentina had pressed it on him at the door. The Yenisei royal seal was genuine. Only the name was not. He held it out, and as he did, he flicked his gaze to the detectors. Red. Gold. Red. Gold. Still cycling. Nothing on him.

The sentry opened the booklet, looked at it, turned to the back page, checked the seal, and gave it back. "Why does the Yenisei legation retrieve a gown at four in the morning?"

"Because Her Highness needs to change at five," Don Juan said. "You understand, she attends the —"

The whine.

A thin, high, metallic scream from the detector on the left-hand pillar. Not the alarm; the over-pitched shriek of a plate being driven past its current limit. The dull gold of the cycling pattern slammed, in a single pulse, into a red so bright it hurt to look at.

The sentry's face changed. His hand went to the butt of the modified Thunderteeth.

Don Juan's heart fell out of his chest.

Not him. He was clean. But — his fingers, when he had passed the booklet, had grazed the sentry's glove. The glove was plain leather. Not insulated.

The ink of the Yenisei royal seal was loaded with a trace of red mercury. The booklet was a diplomatic credential, not a weapon. But the threshold of the Omega detector was set to catch even a Class-A signal. The Chapel Division's brief was to fail closed.

The sentry stepped back. The Thunderteeth was out of the holster and pointing at Don Juan's breastbone.

"Hands up. Slowly. Both of them."

In the third of a second Don Juan ran through a hundred plans. Run — no, the steps are open ground, a bullet is faster. Explain — no, the Yenisei papers were now evidence, not alibi. Force — no, four modified Thunderteeth. He chose the third. He chose, that is, to talk.

"Gentlemen," he said, lifting his hands, palms out, the tone still that of a young man who has never been embarrassed in his life, "I think there is a confusion. I am legation staff, the credential —"

The boot-steps from inside the gate.

Iron groaned. The right-hand leaf of the gate swung open half a foot. A shape came out of the dark — boots on stone, deliberate, the small bright clicks a soldier's heel makes on worked granite.

Fabio.

Same lieutenant's uniform, but with a black cloak thrown over it now, the collar turned up to hide the lower half of his face. The torn-mask pin still at his breast caught the lamplight and threw a single cold spark. On the fourth finger of his right hand he wore a ring Don Juan recognised at once — a band of red gold, the fleur-de-lis of the Charlemagne court struck into the bezel. The ring of a Charlemagne decoration. Fabio was Charlemagne's man. Or at least, Fabio had eaten Charlemagne's bread.

When Fabio saw Don Juan, the practised smile on his face broke for a single honest instant — surprise. Then the surprise sealed itself over, and what came out the other side was the smile Don Juan had always known, only colder.

"Don Juan," he said, into the night air. "It has been a long time."

Don Juan, in his head, said something unprintable. On his face he put the same smile back.

"Fabio. I had thought you were still in Marston, finishing your expulsion. I did not know you had been — enlisted? Promoted? When did this happen?"

"After you and Cesare ran from Marston, Archbishop Gracchus was kind enough to give me a chance." Fabio came down the steps and stopped five paces off. His cloak moved against his shins. Six men had come out behind him, also in Chapel Division kit, also armed — but the weapons on their hips were stranger. The barrels were almost not barrels. At the muzzle end a thumb-sized disc of metal had been welded on, etched all over with a fine pattern. Imitations. Seraphim-class imitations. The real Seraphim weapons were the property of the Seraph Knights only. But the imitations would, at three paces, go through a man like a fist through paper.

The Masked Brotherhood had done well for itself. Somewhere along the line, Fabio had found friends with very deep pockets.

"Yenisei legation," Fabio said, reading the air, the smile widening. "How charming. A change of skin, and you think I won't know Cesare's dog?"

"Fabio. We were at school together —"

"We were not at school together." Fabio cut him off. "The sort who come up from the lower city were never at school with me."

He raised his right hand.

Not a wave. A fist. Clutched in the fist, the size of an apple, a ball of dark gold metal, and the surface of it was running with the same slow ripple of light as the Omega plates. A red mercury flare, Don Juan recognised, the kind that, crushed, would throw a Class-A pulse out across fifty paces. Every Omega detector in half a kilometre would light up. The whole of the Chapel Division's Florence garrison would be at Canterbury inside five minutes.

"Tell your men to lower their weapons," Fabio said to the sentries, without looking at them. Then to Don Juan: "Or I crush this, and you do not leave this street."

Don Juan's smile, finally, came off.

"Cesare sent you to scout. Where is he?"

Don Juan looked at him. He did not answer.

"It doesn't matter," Fabio said, after a moment. "I know he is in Florence. I know he will come. Because Bier is in this castle. And he will not leave her there."

Bier was in the castle.

The sentence went in like a nail. Fabio had said in this castle — not was, not had been. In. Present tense. Fabio had lied about the transfer order, or Gracchus's order had been cut off in flight. Either way, Bier had not left. Fabio was not running Gracchus's errand. Fabio was running Charlemagne's.

Don Juan's right hand, very slowly, very softly, found the smallest of the four bombs in his belt.

"Fabio," he said. "Do you know what I used to do, in Florence, before all this?"

Fabio raised an eyebrow.

"Steal things." Don Juan smiled again, and this time the smile was the one he had worn on the lower-city rooftops when the watch was a step behind and the goods were a step ahead. "Pocket watches off lords. Jewels off ladies. Hearts off the daughters of houses. It was good honest work, and I was good at it."

His right hand moved.

The first bomb left the belt on the flat of his thumb. It bounced once on the stone, rolled, and stopped against the toe of Fabio's boot. Fabio's pupils — for once, for the first time in Don Juan's memory — were slow. The brain behind them caught up half a beat after the eye. He jumped back. The fist with the flare flew open, and the dark-gold ball came out of his hand in a long spinning arc —

The bomb went off first.

Red mercury does not burn. It does not flame. It goes off as a cold red light, and a shockwave you feel in the marrow of your teeth. The blast caught Fabio's right leg below the knee — not severed, opened, the way you open a letter. The trouser and the boot and the flesh all came apart in a single wet line, and Fabio went down with a sound Don Juan had not heard him make since they were children.

"Fire!" a sentry screamed.

Four modified Thunderteeth, firing at once. Don Juan was already moving, and he was not running up the steps — he was throwing himself down them, through the gap where Fabio's body was still falling, into the half-open gate. The iron leaf took his shoulder at a bad angle and he felt something in it pop, but he was through, into a stone corridor lined on both sides with Omega plates that were screaming their flat red scream at him as he ran past. He did not look at them.

The far door. Kitchens. A woman washing dishes, a man beside her, a copper pot steaming over a low flame. They saw a stranger, blood on his coat, and screamed. He was already over the back of the work-table, through the scullery door, and into a passage so narrow he had to turn his shoulders. The far end: the rear gate. Locked. He grabbed the cleaver off the kitchen board on the way past, and on his knees in the dark of the passage he put the blade into the wood of the bolt and wrenched. The wood split. The gate screamed open. He was in the back lane.

A steam-cart was parked in the lane. The Castle's own delivery truck, by the look of the plates. Don Juan did not think. He climbed the driver's seat, threw the throttle, and the boiler came awake with a noise like a man being murdered. The cart leapt forward, the right-hand mudguard shrieking along the brick of the lane, sparks shaking out behind him like a long red tail. At the mouth of the lane a sentry came running round the corner, gun up — Don Juan wrenched the wheel. The front of the cart took the sentry at the hip and threw him sideways across the cobbles. The cart climbed the kerb onto the avenue.

Behind him, the alarm at last — not the Omega scream, the older alarm, the copper bell. DONG. DONG. DONG. Every sentry in Canterbury would have heard it. The whole city would hear it soon.

He ran the cart into a derelict warehouse in the south of the city, left it with the boiler still ticking, and walked the rest of the way to St. Margaret's on foot, with Fabio's blood drying on the cuff of his tailcoat.

He came through the iron door. Alfonso was at the table, fitting a new micro-bearing into the bracelet of his watch. He saw the blood, and his hand paused for a half-breath.

"Fabio," Don Juan said.

Cesare looked up from the map.

"It was not Gracchus's transfer. It was a snatch. Fabio is Charlemagne's. He had the Charlemagne decoration on his hand."

Quintilian straightened off the pillar. "Charlemagne."

"He tried to hold me with a red mercury flare. I dropped a bomb. Took his right leg off below the knee." Don Juan laid the whole thing on the table. "But I have one fact. Bier is still in the castle."

The room went still for the length of one breath.

"Adele?" Quintilian said.

Don Juan's mouth opened, and shut. "I did not get past the gate. I only heard Fabio's order, and it named Bier alone. But —"

"I heard," Alfonso said.

They all turned to him.

Alfonso set the watch down. He reached into his coat and brought out a small, battered box with a long thin aerial fixed to one side. The portable neural current reader. He had taken it from Franco's effects — out of the B-07 archive kit the old professor had left behind — and spent the last four days modifying it, adding the longer aerial, tuning it to pick up the faint neural current of a human body at two hundred metres.

"I had it on you," Alfonso said. "In the cuff of your coat."

Don Juan looked at his own cuff. A pinhead of dull metal, the size of a grain of rice, was sewn into the lining. He had not noticed.

Alfonso pressed a switch. The little projection screen at the top of the box woke, and threw a wavering line of light against the wall. The line had two crests. One he could pick out, faintly, as his own signal. The other was stronger, more regular, with a low undertone that throbbed through the rest of the pattern like a slow drum.

"Two signatures in the castle while you were at the gate," Alfonso said. "One is Bier. I have her pattern from the Minerva Bureau files. The other — a woman, fifteen to eighteen years old, neural current carrying a clear red mercury residue. Position —" he pointed at the bearing on the screen, "— the basement of Canterbury."

Fifteen to eighteen. Red mercury residue.

Adele.

After Cesare had left Florence, the Sacred College had taken Adele for what they had called a course of treatment. It had been a forced red mercury immersion, to draw out Cesare's neural jacking pattern from her nervous system. The residue was still in her.

"Bier and Adele are both in the castle," Cesare said, very quietly, the way a man says a thing he has already known and was waiting to hear confirmed.

He stood.

"The plan changes. Tonight." His hand was on the map, and his finger moved — off Canterbury, up the page, and rested on the long, slow shape of Mount Vesuvius. "Fabio is Charlemagne's man. He was sent to snatch Bier, not for Gracchus. Charlemagne wants her. Or rather, he wants what she carries."

"What does she carry?" Quintilian asked.

"Intelligence," Cesare said. "Bier was an archivist in the Papal Hall. The access to the Vatican archive has been revoked, but the contents of her memory have not. Charlemagne wants the Eastern war plan in its entirety. The forty-seventh clause of the Statute of Religious Secrets. The papal classified files. And —"

He paused.

"— and every file in the archive that bears my name."

The air in the cellar thickened.

"What is in your file?" Quintilian asked.

Cesare did not answer. He reached for the black coat slung over the back of the chair — the Class-A fireproofing jacket Valentina had brought him, plain black cotton outside, shadow-metal thread sewn into the lining. He swung it onto his shoulders and began to button it, one slow stud at a time.

"Don Juan."

"Here."

"You broke Fabio's leg. The Masked Brotherhood will pull out of Canterbury tonight — he cannot run a snatch with one leg under him. When they pull out, the castle reverts to the regular Chapel Division sentries. The sentries are not his."

"You mean to go in for Bier and Adele."

"I do."

"Alone."

"I will go alone."

"Chief —" Don Juan's face changed. "You cannot —"

"We split four ways. We do not put every body on the same target." Cesare's voice cut across his, flat and final. "Quintilian: find the retired Knights of the Iron Seraph. Alfonso: take Violaine through the back channel into the arsenal and unlock the stockpile. Valentina: stir up the Yenisei legation into making noise. I will go to Canterbury."

He looked at Don Juan.

"You will go to Vesuvius."

"Vesuvius," Don Juan said. The word did not make sense to him.

"Fabio's men will leave Canterbury. The real Chapel Division escort will arrive soon. When I have Bier and Adele out, I will go with them through the broken-stone track east of the eastern gate, north-east, to the north-flank mine entrance of Vesuvius."

Alfonso's face changed. "You mean to take them into Golgotha."

"Not into Golgotha. Into the outer workings of the Vesuvius mine." Cesare's hand did not move from the map. "Professor Franco left a plan of the interior of Vesuvius among his effects. Drawn by da Vinci's own hand, three centuries old. The mine has two routes that run into the deep chambers. If Bier and Adele have to disappear for any length of time, that is the only place in reach of Florence that the Chapel Division will not surround."

Don Juan was quiet a moment.

"Chief. You are going to Canterbury by yourself. There are four sentries at least."

"The sentries are not the problem. After Fabio pulls out, the castle's defence will be downgraded from the Masked Brotherhood's picked men to ordinary sentries. They have no modified Thunderteeth. They have no Seraphim imitations. I can get in." Cesare looked at him. "Your task is Vesuvius. Confirm the mine mouth is not trapped. Take this."

He took a small cloth bag off the table and tossed it. Don Juan caught it.

"A small transceiver. Franco's. I have tuned it to the highest level of the encrypted band. No more than three people in the world know that frequency. Once you are at the mine mouth, you will keep it open to me."

Don Juan weighed the bag in his hand. "Chief."

"What."

"You aren't really going in by yourself, are you."

Cesare did not answer at once. He reached under the table, and brought out a long, narrow bundle wrapped in black cloth. He unfolded the cloth. A sword. The blade was long and narrow, curved like a sleeping snake, the colour of verdigris, and the grip was bound in a green silk that had faded to the colour of old leaves.

The Green Serpent. One of the seven blades da Vinci had left to whoever came after him. The same ore as the first Seraphim weapons. The hilt fitted Cesare's hand as though it had been poured for him.

"The Rose Ghost armour is at the Minerva Bureau. I cannot wear it. The Green Serpent is not a Seraphim-class weapon. It is enough for ordinary sentries." He slid the blade behind his back. The tail of the coat fell over the hilt and hid it. "Anything else?"

Don Juan looked at him. "Yes. Come back alive."

Cesare looked at him once. Then he turned to the door.

He had his hand on the iron when a small vibration ran through the room. Not the floor. The belt of Licinius, who had been sitting in the corner, silent, the whole time. His left hand was at his waist. The colour had gone out of his face.

He drew out, between two fingers, a brass cylinder the length of a thumb. A hairline crack ran along the wax that sealed the cap. Through the crack a thin gold light pulsed, very faintly.

Franco's wax-sealed letter indicator. The one the old professor had set, on the night he died, to trigger on a single condition. Only when the seal of Golgotha showed a serious disturbance would the thing begin to shake.

Licinius took it from his belt. The cylinder hummed against his fingertips. The hum, very small, very low, ran through the brass and into the air, and every man in the cellar heard it.

The crack in the wax widened a hair. The gold light brightened, and the brass threw, on the wall behind Cesare's head, a line of text so small you had to step forward to read it.

THE SEAL OF GOLGOTHA HAS LOOSENED.

The cellar went silent.

Cesare stood at the open door. The night air, cold, came in off the churchyard. One hand on the hilt of the Green Serpent at his back. The lamp threw half his face into the light, and left the other half in a darkness that moved.

"Bier," he said. "And Adele. They are in Golgotha."

【中文】
第249章 骷髅地的异动

　　"计划变了。"

　　西泽尔站在铁门前，月光把他的影子拉得很长。他没有回头看任何人，声音平静得像在念一行没有感情的文字："外交骚乱取消。我们直接去维苏威火山。"

　　"老板，密涅瓦武器库的装备——"阿方索率先开口。

　　"来不及了。"西泽尔说，"碧儿和阿黛尔在骷髅地。格拉古大主教把她们转移到那里，说明他知道那里有什么。封印松动，里面那些东西正在醒过来。"

　　房间里没有一个人再说话。

　　李锡尼把那个还在震动的黄铜圆筒攥在掌心，金色微光从指缝间渗出来，照亮了他脸上纵横的旧伤疤。他沉默了几秒，然后说："我有朗基努斯碎片。"

　　这句话说出来的分量不亚于一颗炸弹。所有人看向他。

　　"佛朗哥留给我的。"李锡尼的声音低而哑，"打磨完成的那个版本。"

　　西泽尔终于转过身来。他看了李锡尼几秒钟，点了点头。就只是点头。

　　"走。"他说。

　　薇若兰已经在圣玛格丽特教堂的后院准备好了矿车。说是矿车，其实是密涅瓦机关库存里的标准装甲运输车——四米长的铁壳车厢，履带式底盘，双蒸汽核心驱动，悬挂减震做过特殊处理以适应维苏威火山矿道里高低不平的碎石路面。外面用生锈的铁皮和煤灰做旧，蒸汽排气管被改成了矿车通用的样式，乍看之下和翡冷翠周边矿区里跑了几十年的老旧运煤车没什么区别。

　　"原本是给万国盛典运送甲胄零件的备用通道。"薇若兰说，她的声音在凌晨的冷空气里格外清晰，"从翡冷翠东郊的废弃伐木场出发，穿过七号矿道直通维苏威火山北麓入口，全程四十分钟。路不好走，但不会被任何关卡拦住。"

　　七个人。瓦莲京娜最后一个上车。她把改装神怒Ⅲ型的甲胄留在了翡冷翠，随身的只有那柄从冰原带出来的战斧和一柄短刀。她跳进车厢的时候金发在蒸汽灯光下扬起，昆提良下意识地伸手接了她一下，被她一个眼神挡了回去。

　　矿车启动。蒸汽阀门开合之间发出沉重的喘息声，车厢在碎石路面上颠簸着驶出废弃伐木场，驶向黑暗的矿道入口。

　　唐璜趴在车厢后部的观察窗前，眼睛盯着逐渐远去的翡冷翠城廓。城里的灯火在凌晨的薄雾中像一捧碎金。他低声说："亚历山大撑不了太久。"

　　"他能撑。"西泽尔说，"格里高利家族是西方红水银的命脉。枢机会不敢动他。"

　　"我是说我们不在的时候。"唐璜说，"等他知道我们不是去制造外交骚乱而是去维苏威火山，大概会气得把那把折扇摔了。"

　　没有人笑。

　　矿车驶入矿道后，外面的世界彻底消失了。蒸汽灯被拧到最低档，昏黄的光勉强照亮前方三五米的路面。两侧的岩壁向内收紧，越往深处走空气越潮湿，带着一股被时间封存了数十年的霉味和铁锈味。

　　李锡尼坐在车厢最里面的角落，闭着眼，左手按在腰间那个打磨得光滑的朗基努斯碎片上。他已经三天没有正经睡过了，但此刻他的呼吸比任何人都平稳——这是个上过战场的人才有的本事，能在铁壳车厢里闭眼休息，不是因为安全，是因为他必须在最短的时间里把自己的状态调到最好。

　　瓦莲京娜靠着车厢壁，战斧横放在膝上。她忽然开口："西泽尔。"

　　"嗯。"

　　"骷髅地里的东西，你能控制？"

　　沉默。

　　"我不确定。"西泽尔说，"但那些东西——如果真的是从封印里出来的——它们认得锡兰的血。"

　　"所以你打算用血。"

　　"我打算先看清楚。"

　　瓦莲京娜没有再问。她把战斧竖起来靠在肩头，冰原寒玉的寒气透过斧柄传到掌心，让她的手指保持着必要的清醒。

　　矿车在黑暗中行进了大约三十分钟。

　　阿方索一直蹲在车厢后部，蜘蛛巢腕表上的八只微型蜘蛛被他释放了六只出去，在矿道前方的黑暗中探路。信号反馈回来的画面显示在腕表的小型投影屏上——矿道结构完好，没有坍塌，没有人为设置的障碍物。

　　"前方一公里就是维苏威火山北麓废弃矿井的主入口。"阿方索说，"矿道在最后五百米分岔，左边通向旧采石场，右边才是直通火山内部的——"

　　他的话忽然断了。

　　投影屏上，六只微型蜘蛛的视野同时出现了变化。蜘蛛是机械造的，不可能有情绪，但阿方索的指尖在腕表上按紧了——那种变化像是整条矿道的空气被突然抽走了一截。

　　光。

　　矿道深处，从火山方向，涌出来一片金色。

　　不是火光。也不是蒸汽灯的暖黄色。那是一种极纯的、几乎刺目的金色，像正午的太阳被硬塞进了一条窄窄的矿道里——但矿道里并没有太阳。那片光从更深处来，从地下来，从岩层的缝隙里渗出来，一寸一寸地淹没了蜘蛛的视野。

　　"红水银。"阿方索的声音变了，"这个能量等级——S级——"

　　同一秒，李锡尼猛地睁开了眼。他按着朗基努斯碎片的手骤然收紧，指节发白。碎片在他掌心剧烈地跳动起来，发出金属和金属碰撞的尖锐声响，像被什么东西远程唤醒了一样。

　　"来了。"李锡尼说。

　　矿道里传来一种声音。

　　不是蒸汽喷发，不是岩层崩裂。那是一种更深沉的、像指甲划过铁板的金属摩擦声。连续的，叠加的，不止一个声源。声音从矿道深处向他们的方向蔓延开来，和那片金色光芒同步——光到哪里，声音就跟到哪里。

　　"停车。"西泽尔说。

　　矿车在制动蒸汽的尖叫声中停下。车厢里七个人的呼吸在那一瞬间都轻了半拍。

　　从矿道前方的分岔口右侧——直通火山内部的通道——金色的光变得更亮了。紧接着，岩壁开始震动。不是地震那种横向的晃，是一种纵向的、从下往上传来的冲击，像是有什么极其沉重的东西正从火山内部往上爬。每一次冲击都在矿道的岩壁上留下裂纹，石粉簌簌地落。

　　然后，第一台甲胄从光芒中走了出来。

　　它的样子让昆提良倒抽了一口气。

　　那是一台至少有四十年历史的老式炽天使甲胄。通体暗金色的装甲板上满是岁月的痕迹——刮擦、凹陷、锈蚀，以及某种像植物根须一样攀附在装甲缝隙中的暗红色纹路。甲胄的头部是六翼天使的面甲造型，双眼处不是灯组而是两个空洞的凹槽——里面什么都没有，骑士舱是空的。

　　但它在走。

　　没有骑士。没有驾驶者。一台空的、四十年没人碰过的炽天使甲胄，正沿着矿道朝他们走来。每一步都带起沉重的金属碰撞声，蒸汽从它胸甲的排气口喷出，灼热的白气在金色的光芒中翻滚。

　　第一台之后是第二台。第二台之后是第三台。

　　三台自律炽天使。

　　从矿道裂缝和岩壁的接缝处，又爬出了更多。有的已经残破，只剩半截躯体在地面上拖行，金属关节在石头上刮出尖锐的声响；有的相对完整，但动作迟缓僵硬，像刚学会走路的婴儿。它们的数量看不清——金色的光太亮了，岩壁的阴影里全是晃动的暗金色轮廓。

　　"自律炽天使。"李锡尼的声音哑得几乎听不见，"骷髅地封存四十年的残骸——前任总长把所有出现过自行活动异象的甲胄都封在了里面——它们出来了。"

　　最前方那台完整的自律炽天使停下了。它的空洞面甲对着矿车，金属关节发出一连串咔嚓声——像是在调整角度，像是在审视。它没有武器，骑士舱是空的，但它胸腔的位置发出了一声低沉的、像心跳一样的闷响。

　　砰。砰。砰。

　　红水银核心在跳动。

　　那声音和西泽尔体内黄金套管的震动频率完全吻合。嗡的一声，套管在发烫。后颈像是被人按了一块烧红的烙铁，热度沿着脊椎向上蔓延。他的紫瞳在黑暗中亮起来——不是被光照亮的，是自己亮的——瞳孔深处有金红色的纹路在游动，像岩浆在地底裂隙中流淌。

　　"别动。"西泽尔对车厢里所有人说。

　　他推开车门。

　　冷风从矿道里灌进来，带着浓重的铁锈味和一丝甜腻到不正常的花香气——那不是矿道该有的味道。那是莲花的味道。

　　西泽尔站在矿车前面，面对着三台自律炽天使。

　　他的右手伸进领口，慢慢地扯出一条细链。链子的末端挂着一枚银莲花形状的合金坠子——琳琅夫人的遗物。他一直戴着，从翡冷翠到马斯顿，从马斯顿到东方，从王屋山的爆炸中活下来之后也一直戴着。

　　但他从未翻过来看过坠子的背面。

　　他翻了过来。

　　坠子背面，刻着一行极细的纹路。不是西方文字，不是拉丁文，也不是希腊文。是某种弯曲蛇形符号组成的古文——锡兰文字。文字中间，嵌着一枚齿轮徽记。齿轮中心一颗五芒星，五芒星的五个角末端各连接一圈更小的齿轮。

　　机械神教徽记。达·芬奇版本。

　　坠子在西泽尔的指尖发出极轻的嗡鸣。和他后颈的黄金套管同频共振。

　　那台最前方的自律炽天使停了。

　　它胸腔里红水银核心的跳动声忽然变了——从沉重的"砰——砰——砰——"变成了短促的"砰砰砰砰"——像一颗心脏骤然加速。它的金属关节不再咔嚓作响。空洞的面甲对着西泽尔手中的坠子，那两个没有灯组的眼窝里，渗出了一线极细的金色光芒。

　　然后是第二台。也停了。

　　第三台。那些从裂缝里爬出来的残骸们——动作全部凝固了。

　　整个矿道陷入了一种诡异的安静。只剩下蒸汽从甲胄排气口喷出的白气声，和西泽尔手中坠子持续的嗡鸣。

　　"老板——"唐璜从车窗里探出半个头。

　　"别过来。"西泽尔说。

　　但他的声音刚落，那个"安静"就碎了。

　　最先停下的那台自律炽天使忽然仰头，发出了一声尖锐到撕裂耳膜的金属啸叫。那啸叫像是从红水银核心深处挤出来的，带着一种不属于机械的、近乎愤怒的频率。啸叫的同时，它胸甲的装甲板缝隙间，那条暗红色的根须状纹路忽然亮了起来——从暗红变成了炽白色，像被什么东西点燃了。

　　它动了。

　　不再是一步一步的僵硬行走。是一瞬间的爆发式冲锋。一台四十年没人驾驶的老式炽天使，在没有骑士的情况下爆发出远超设计极限的速度——蒸汽从它全身所有排气口同时喷出，白气在矿道中炸成一片雾幕。

　　第二台也动了。第三台也动了。

　　那些从裂缝里爬出来的残骸们也动了——有的在地面上拖行，有的只剩下半截躯壳的也用残存的手臂朝着矿车方向爬。金属刮擦石壁的声音重新充满了矿道。

　　它们冲着矿车来了。

　　"上车！走！"西泽尔退后一步，反手把青蛇剑从腰后抽了出来。剑身在金色光芒中泛着一层冷冽的绿光。

　　矿车的蒸汽核心重新嘶吼起来，履带在碎石上打滑——阿方索猛地拧了一把加速阀，车厢猛烈地一震，撞开了挡在前面的几块落石，朝矿道入口方向倒退了回去。

　　但自律炽天使太快了。第一台已经到了矿车车厢侧面，金属手掌扣住了车厢的边沿，整台矿车被那股力量拽得偏了一个角度，履带在石头上划出一道火星。

　　"左舷！"瓦莲京娜的战斧已经劈了出去。叶尼塞战斧的冰原寒玉斧刃撞上自律炽天使的手腕关节，冰与金属碰撞的声音在矿道中回荡了两次——第一下砍开了外层装甲，第二下嵌进了内部的硬金骨架。但甲胄的关节并没有断开。那条暗红色的根须状纹路在斧刃切入的位置亮起了白光，像是在自我修复。

　　"它在自己长回去！"瓦莲京娜骂了一声。

　　"有欧米茄的自愈纤维！"阿方索在驾驶座上吼了一声，方向盘被他打得死死的，"别砍——砍不死的——"

　　西泽尔从车厢后门跳了下去。青蛇剑在他手中弯出一道蛇形的弧线，剑尖精准地刺向那台扣住车厢的自律炽天使的面甲接缝处——那里是神经接驳系统最密集的位置。

　　剑尖刺入的瞬间，他后颈的黄金套管猛地烫了一下。

　　他的紫瞳在黑暗中炸开了金红色的光芒。

　　那光芒不是向外发射的，是从瞳孔内部涌出来的，像两种颜色的墨水在水中翻滚交织。金红纹路沿着他的眼眶向太阳穴蔓延，照亮了他苍白的脸——那种苍白在金红色光芒的映照下显得近乎透明，像是被光穿透了。

　　自律炽天使停了。

　　和之前坠子引发的停顿不同。这一次的停顿是彻底的——那台甲胄的关节不再发出任何声响，胸腔里红水银核心的跳动声骤降到了几乎听不见的频率。它空洞的面甲对着西泽尔的紫瞳，一动不动。

　　第二台也停了。第三台也停了。残骸们也停了。

　　整个矿道再一次安静了。

　　但西泽尔知道这不是结束。他能感觉到那些甲胄核心里残存的世界树意识碎片在挣扎——它们认出了他，又在抗拒他。两种力量在他和甲胄之间拉扯，像两个人在争夺同一根绳子的两端。

　　三秒。

　　他最多只能压制三秒。

　　"阿方索。"西泽尔的声音从牙缝里挤出来，平得听不出任何情绪。

　　"在。"

　　"入口。"

　　阿方索没有多问一个字。他从驾驶座上弹起来，蜘蛛巢腕表里最后两只机械蜘蛛被他同时释放了出去。两只拇指盖大小的青铜蜘蛛沿着矿道壁飞速爬向废弃矿井的入口——在矿车后方大约五十米的位置，那是通往外面的唯一通道。

　　两只蜘蛛的腹部各绑着一个微型装置——暴力增强型雷霆牙的弹头结构，被阿方索改成了延时爆破版。红水银注入量提高到原来三倍，微型蒸汽阀控制着引爆时机——最长可延时五秒。五秒之后红水银点燃，铳身三秒内解体爆炸。

　　两只蜘蛛到达入口位置时，恰好是西泽尔压制自律炽天使的第三秒。

　　那些甲胄醒了。

　　所有的。同时。像是收到了统一的指令。第一台的面甲猛地转向西泽尔，啸叫声比之前更尖锐。它的胸腔在膨胀——红水银核心在急速充能，准备进行某种近身爆破。

　　西泽尔后撤一步，青蛇剑在身前画了一个弧。

　　"炸。"

　　阿方索按下了引爆键。

　　两声闷响在矿道入口处几乎同时炸开。暴力增强型雷霆牙的弹头在半秒内释放了全部红水银能量——热量在一瞬间把入口处的玄武岩壁烧成了红色，蒸汽和碎石混合着向矿道内部喷涌。矿道入口上方一大段岩层失去了支撑，轰然坍塌。

　　数十吨的岩石和碎矿砸下来，把废弃矿井的入口封得严严实实。碎石仍在不断落下，扬起呛人的灰尘。

　　自律炽天使被坍塌挡住了。至少暂时被挡住了。

　　矿车趁着最后一秒的窗口从分岔口冲进了左侧的旧采石场通道——那条路绕得更远，但还能走。碎石在矿车后方追着他们砸了十几秒，直到矿车拐进了另一条支道才渐渐停歇。

　　车厢里一片死寂。

　　昆提良半个身子探出窗外盯着后方看了好一会儿。矿道被灰尘笼罩，什么都看不清了。他慢慢缩回来，咽了口唾沫，说："堵死了。"

　　"五分钟。"阿方索说，方向盘还在他手里，被他握得指节发白，"最多五分钟。那些东西会自己把路挖开。"

　　"够了。"西泽尔说。

　　他重新坐回了车厢里。青蛇剑横放在膝上，剑身上还沾着自律炽天使装甲板的碎屑。他的右手按在胸口——那枚银莲花坠子被他塞回了领口，但坠子背后的纹路在黑暗中仍然隐约可见：齿轮，五芒星，锡兰古文。

　　琳琅夫人从一开始就知道。她把梵天陨落的密钥刻在了坠子正面，而把另一个秘密——机械神教和锡兰星见之间的纽带——刻在了坠子背面。她没有告诉他。也许她想告诉他，但时间没有等到那一天。

　　车厢在矿道里颠簸着向前。空气里残留着爆炸的硫磺味和一种正在消散的莲花香气。

　　西泽尔闭上了眼。

　　他需要休息。哪怕只有几秒钟。

　　然后他听到了。

　　从矿道深处。从坍塌的碎石后面。从骷髅地的方向。从火山的最深处。

　　一个声音。

　　女孩的歌声。很轻，很远，像隔着一层水。旋律简单到只有几个音符反复——那是马斯顿仲夏夜庆典上孩子们会唱的歌谣，关于莲花和根脉。

　　"满池莲花在淤泥中根脉相连……"

　　阿黛尔的声音。

　　西泽尔睁开了眼。

【English】
Chapter 249 — The Stirring at Golgotha

"Plans have changed."

Cesare stood at the iron gate, the moon at his back stretching his shadow long across the flagstones. He did not turn. His voice had no temperature in it — the voice of a man reading a line of scripture he had stopped believing in. "The diversion is off. We go directly to Vesuvius."

"Boss, the Minerva loadout—" Alfonso was the first to speak.

"There is no time." Cesare said. "Beatrice and Adele are inside Golgotha. Archbishop Graccus moved them there on purpose. He knows what is buried under the seal. The seal is failing. Whatever is down there is waking."

No one in the room answered.

Licinius closed his hand around the brass cylinder he had been holding. It was still trembling against his palm. A thin gold light leaked between his fingers and laid bright lines down the old scars on his face. He was quiet for several seconds. Then he said, "I have the Longinus shard."

The sentence fell into the room with the weight of a small bomb. Everyone looked at him.

"Franco left it with me." Licinius's voice was low, hoarse at the edges. "The finished version. Polished and balanced."

Cesare finally turned. He looked at Licinius for a long moment. Then he nodded. That was all.

"Move," he said.

Violante had the cart ready in the rear yard of Saint Margaret's. A mine cart, she had called it, but it was in fact a standard Minerva armory armored transport — an iron-shelled wagon four meters long, treaded chassis, twin steam cores driving it, the suspension specially tuned for the broken stone of the Vesuvius mining roads. The outside had been treated with rust and coal-ash until it looked like any one of the battered coal-haulers that had been rattling around the quarries outside Florence for decades. The steam exhausts had been swapped for the standard mining-cart pattern.

"It was meant to be a backup route for moving mech parts during the Universal Congress," Violante said, her voice unusually clear in the pre-dawn cold. "Out of the abandoned lumber yard on the eastern edge of the city, through Mine Shaft Seven, straight to the northern foot of Vesuvius. Forty minutes. The road is poor, but no checkpoint will stop us."

Seven of them. Valentina was the last to climb aboard. She had left her modified Wrath-of-God III behind in Florence; all she carried was the battle axe she had brought out of the ice plains and a short blade at her hip. When she swung herself up into the wagon, her fair hair caught the steam light. Quintilian reached out, on instinct, to steady her. She stopped him with a look.

The cart began to move. The steam valves opened and closed in a labored wheeze. The wagon jolted over the broken ground of the lumber yard, then out into the dark mouth of the mine shaft.

Don Juan was leaning against the rear viewing slit, eyes on the silhouette of Florence falling away behind them. The city's lights in the pre-dawn mist looked like a handful of scattered gold. He said, in a low voice, "Alessandro cannot hold out for long."

"He can hold." Cesare said. "The Gregorio family is the lifeblood of the western red mercury trade. The Curia will not touch him."

"I mean, while we are not there." Don Juan said. "When he finds out we are not staging any diversion at all but have gone straight to Vesuvius, he will probably snap that folding fan of his across his knee."

No one laughed.

Once the cart entered the mine shaft, the world outside ceased to exist. The steam lamps were turned down to their lowest setting; the dim yellow light was enough to see three or four paces ahead, no more. The rock walls on either side closed inward as they went. The deeper they traveled, the damper the air grew, smelling of decades of sealed-in mold and iron.

Licinius sat in the innermost corner of the cart with his eyes closed and his left hand resting on the polished Longinus shard at his waist. He had not slept properly in three days, but his breathing was steadier than anyone else's — a trick of men who had been to war, who could close their eyes in an iron shell and rest, not because they were safe, but because they had to bring themselves to their best in the shortest possible time. His lips moved without sound. We are beset on every side, but not crushed. We are perplexed, but not in despair.

Valentina leaned against the wagon wall, the battle axe laid flat across her knees. After a while she spoke.

"Cesare."

"Yes."

"The things in Golgotha. Can you control them?"

A silence.

"I am not certain," Cesare said. "But those things — if they truly came out of the seal — they know the blood of Ceylon."

"So you mean to use your blood."

"I mean to look, first."

Valentina did not ask again. She set the axe upright against her shoulder. The chill of the ice jade in the haft bled through into her palm and kept her fingers as clear as they needed to be.

The cart traveled on through the dark for about thirty minutes.

Alfonso had been crouched in the back of the wagon, six of the eight micro-spiders from his Spider Nest watch released ahead of them into the dark. The feeds were playing on the watch's tiny projection screen — tunnel structure sound, no collapses, no obstacles set by human hands.

"About a kilometer to the main entrance of the abandoned mine at the northern foot of Vesuvius. The shaft forks in the last five hundred meters. Left is the old quarry. Right is the direct line into—"

He stopped.

On the projection, all six spider feeds changed at once. The spiders were mechanical, they could not feel, but Alfonso's fingertips pressed hard against the watch — the change was like the air in the tunnel being drawn out a notch.

Light.

Out of the depths, from the direction of the volcano, gold poured into the mine.

Not fire. Not the warm yellow of steam lamps. A gold so pure it was almost violent, like the noon sun had been shoved bodily into a narrow mine shaft — but there was no sun in the mine. The light came from deeper in, from below, seeping through the cracks in the rock, an inch at a time drowning the spiders' view.

"Red mercury." Alfonso's voice had changed. "This energy level — S-grade—"

In the same second, Licinius's eyes snapped open. His hand on the Longinus shard tightened, knuckles going bone-white. The shard jumped in his palm, metal on metal, as if it had been wakened by something far away.

"It's here," Licinius said.

A sound came from the shaft.

Not the venting of steam. Not the splitting of rock. Something deeper — like fingernails drawn across an iron plate. Continuous, layered, more than one source. It spread from the depths of the tunnel toward them, in step with the gold light. Wherever the light reached, the sound followed.

"Stop the cart," Cesare said.

The cart stopped with the screaming of steam brakes. For an instant, the seven of them all held their breath half a beat longer than usual.

From the right side of the fork — the path that ran straight into the volcano — the gold grew brighter. The walls of the mine began to shake. Not the horizontal shake of an earthquake. Vertical impacts, hammering up from below, as if something unimaginably heavy was climbing out of the heart of the mountain. Each impact left cracks in the rock face, and a whisper of stone dust fell.

Then the first Seraph walked out of the light.

It was an old Seraph, at least forty years out of date. Its dark gold armor was marked with every kind of weather — scratches, dents, rust, and climbing through every seam of the plates, dark red patterns like roots. The head was a six-winged angel faceplate in the old style, but where the eyes should have been there were two empty hollows. The knight's cabin was empty.

But it walked.

No rider. No driver. An empty Seraph, untouched in forty years, walking toward them down the mine. Each step rang with the heavy crash of metal on stone. Steam puffed from the chest vents, white vapor churning in the gold light.

The second followed. Then the third.

Three autonomous Seraphs.

From the cracks in the walls and the seams in the rock, more crawled out. Some were broken, half-bodies dragging themselves along the stone, metal joints screaming. Some were more whole, but slow, stiff, like infants learning to walk. Their numbers were impossible to count — the gold was too bright, the rock shadows full of moving dark gold silhouettes.

"Autonomous Seraphs," Licinius's voice was barely audible. "The remains sealed inside Golgotha for forty years. The previous Captain-General had every Seraph that ever showed signs of self-movement sealed inside. They are out."

The most intact one at the front stopped. Its empty faceplate faced the cart. Its joints clicked in a long, considering series of sounds, as if it were adjusting the angle of its attention. It carried no weapons. Its cabin was empty. But in the cavity of its chest, something made a low, slow sound, like a heartbeat.

Thump. Thump. Thump.

The red mercury core, beating.

The sound matched the vibration frequency of the golden cannula at the back of Cesare's neck exactly. Humming. The back of his neck felt as if someone had pressed a red-hot iron there. Heat climbed up his spine. His purple eyes lit in the dark — not lit by anything from outside, lit from within — gold-red patterns swimming in his pupils, like lava in the cracks of the earth.

"Don't move," Cesare told the others in the cart.

He pushed open the door.

Cold wind from the tunnel flooded in, carrying a heavy rust smell and, beneath it, a sweetness that did not belong in any mine.

Lotus.

Cesare stood in front of the cart, facing the three autonomous Seraphs.

His right hand went into his collar and drew out a thin chain. At the end of it hung a silver lotus-shaped alloy pendant — Lady Linlang's keepsake. He had always worn it. From Florence to Marston. From Marston to the East. Since the explosion at Mount Wangwu.

He had never turned it over to look at the back.

He turned it over.

The back of the pendant was etched with very fine lines. Not Western script. Not Latin. Not Greek. Curved, snake-like characters forming an old tongue — the script of Ceylon. In the middle of the script sat a gear sigil. A five-pointed star at the center of the gear, each point of the star connected to a smaller gear.

The sigil of the Machine God. The Da Vinci version.

The pendant began to hum faintly in Cesare's fingers. It was resonating with the cannula at the back of his neck.

The first autonomous Seraph stopped.

The beating of the red mercury core in its chest changed — from a slow thump... thump... thump... to a rapid thump thump thump thump — the sound of a heart suddenly racing. Its joints stopped clicking. The empty faceplate looked at the pendant in Cesare's hand. From the two lamp-less hollows of its eyes, a thin line of gold light leaked out.

The second stopped.

The third. The broken things dragging from the cracks — they all froze.

The whole tunnel fell into an eerie quiet. Only the steam hissing from the mech vents, and the continuous hum of the pendant in Cesare's hand.

"Boss—" Don Juan leaned half his head out the cart window.

"Don't come closer," Cesare said.

But the moment his voice fell, the quiet shattered.

The first autonomous Seraph threw its head back and screamed. Not a mechanical sound — a sharp, ear-tearing shriek that seemed to be forced out from the deepest part of its red mercury core, carrying a frequency that was almost angry. At the same time, the dark red root patterns in the seams of its armor lit up — from dark red to incandescent white, as if something had been set on fire inside them.

It moved.

Not the slow, stiff walk anymore. A sudden, explosive charge. A forty-year-old Seraph, with no knight, bursting forward at a speed well past its design limit — steam blasted from every vent on its body at once, white vapor exploding into a wall of fog in the shaft.

The second moved. The third moved.

The broken things in the cracks — some dragging, some with only half a torso — crawled toward the cart with whatever arms they had left. The sound of metal scraping on stone filled the tunnel again.

They were coming for the cart.

"Get on! Go!" Cesare stepped back, drawing the Green Snake sword from behind his waist. In the gold light the blade wore a cold green edge.

The cart's steam core roared again, treads slipping on the gravel — Alfonso wrenched the accelerator, the wagon lurched hard, knocked aside a few fallen stones, and began reversing toward the tunnel entrance.

But the autonomous Seraphs were too fast. The first was already at the cart's side, its metal hand gripping the edge of the wagon, the whole cart hauled off course by the force, treads scraping sparks off the stone.

"Port side!" Valentina's axe was already swinging. The ice jade edge of the Yenisei battle axe met the Seraph's wrist joint. The sound of ice striking metal echoed twice in the shaft — the first strike opened the outer armor, the second buried the blade in the inner hard-gold skeleton. But the joint did not give. The dark red root pattern around the cut lit up white, beginning to seal itself.

"It's growing back!" Valentina swore.

"It carries Omega self-healing fibers!" Alfonso shouted from the driver's seat, the steering wheel white-knuckled in his hands. "Don't cut — you cannot kill it that way—"

Cesare dropped from the back door of the cart. The Green Snake sword drew a snake-arc in his hand, the tip aimed with precision at the seam of the faceplate on the Seraph gripping the wagon — the densest part of its neural interface.

The instant the tip went in, the golden cannula at the back of his neck burned hot.

His purple eyes in the dark exploded with gold-red light.

The light did not project outward. It poured out from inside the pupils, like two colors of ink tumbling and weaving through water. The gold-red patterns spread from his eye sockets along his temples, lighting his pale face — that pallor under the gold-red light looked almost translucent, as if the light had gone straight through him.

The Seraph stopped.

Different from the pendant-induced stop. This one was complete — the mech's joints made no sound at all, the red mercury core in its chest dropped to a frequency almost below hearing. Its empty faceplate looked into Cesare's purple eyes, motionless.

The second stopped. The third stopped. The broken ones stopped.

The tunnel was silent again.

But Cesare knew this was not the end. He could feel the remnants of the World Tree consciousness in the mech cores struggling — they recognized him, and they were fighting him. Two forces pulling at him and the mechs, like two men fighting for the ends of the same rope.

Three seconds.

He could hold them for three seconds at the most.

"Alfonso," Cesare's voice came out from between his teeth, level, showing nothing.

"Here."

"The entrance."

Alfonso did not ask a single extra question. He jumped up from the driver's seat and released the last two mechanical spiders from the Spider Nest watch. Two thumb-sized bronze spiders scuttled along the walls of the shaft toward the abandoned mine entrance — some fifty meters behind the cart, the only way out.

Each spider carried a micro device on its belly — the warhead structure of a violence-enhanced Thunder Fang, modified by Alfonso into a delayed-detonation version. The red mercury charge had been tripled. A micro steam valve controlled the ignition timing — maximum five-second delay. Five seconds later, the red mercury would ignite, the body would come apart and explode within three seconds.

When the two spiders reached the entrance, it was the third second of Cesare's suppression.

The mechs woke up.

All of them. At the same instant. As if they had received a single command. The first one's faceplate whipped around to face Cesare, the shriek sharper than before. The cavity of its chest was expanding — the red mercury core rapidly charging, preparing for some kind of close-range detonation.

Cesare stepped back, the Green Snake sword drawing an arc in front of him.

"Blow it."

Alfonso pressed the detonator.

Two muffled explosions went off at the entrance almost simultaneously. The violence-enhanced Thunder Fang warheads released all their red mercury energy in half a second — the heat turned the basalt walls at the entrance red in an instant, steam and rock fragments mixed and blasted into the tunnel. The rock above the entrance lost its support and came down in a roar.

Dozens of tons of rock and broken ore crashed down, sealing the abandoned mine entrance completely. Debris kept falling, raising choking dust.

The autonomous Seraphs were blocked by the collapse. For the moment, at least.

The cart took the last second of the window to rush from the fork into the old quarry tunnel on the left — the longer way, but it still went. Debris chased them for another dozen seconds, until the cart turned into another branch and gradually stopped.

Inside the cart, a dead silence.

Quintilian leaned half his body out the window and stared at the rear for a long while. The tunnel was thick with dust, nothing to see. He slowly drew back, swallowed, and said: "Buried."

"Five minutes." Alfonso said, the steering wheel still in his hands, knuckles bone-white. "Five minutes at the most. Those things will dig themselves a way out."

"That is enough," Cesare said.

He sat back down inside the wagon. The Green Snake sword across his knees, the blade still carrying chips from the Seraph's armor. His right hand rested against his chest
