【中文】
第252章 维苏威火山的心脏

暗金色的光点从矿道深处缓缓升高，不是眼睛，是一盏悬挂在穹顶上的矿灯，三百年前的铜灯罩上铸着昂格里亚家族的鹰锤纹章，灯芯里流淌的不是油，是缓慢跳动的红水银。光点每跳一下，矿道两侧的岩壁就亮一瞬，映出大片黄铜色的齿轮浮雕。

齿轮浮雕刻满了整条矿道，齿牙紧密咬合，一直延伸到视线尽头。

西泽尔没有回头看身后的人。他继续向前走，脚步声在矿道里回荡，和红水银灯芯跳动的嗡鸣混在一起。

"老板。"阿方索在身后低声说。

"我听到了。"西泽尔说。

他的声音很平静，但后颈的黄金套管忽然发烫，烫得他肩膀微微一僵。他伸手按住了脖颈，指尖触到金属表面时感到细密的震动，像是有什么东西正试图从套管深处醒来。

"所有人穿战斗服。"西泽尔说。

阿方索点了点头，从随身的密封背包里取出叠好的银灰色防护服，抖开来是一套贴身的连体衣，内衬缝着密密麻麻的影金属丝线，摸上去冰凉而沉重。他把第一套递给西泽尔，然后是瓦莲京娜、唐璜、昆提良，最后才给自己套上。

这是密涅瓦机关A级防火防爆服，扛得住八百度高温持续三十分钟，原本是给进入熔岩之心作业的工程师准备的。

矿道渐渐变宽。

三百年前昂格里亚家族的矿工用铁镐在玄武岩上一锤一锤凿出这条通道，岩壁粗粝不平，每隔十五米就有一个壁龛，壁龛里原本放着油灯，现在被红水银灯芯取代，光芒昏黄而温暖，像是三百年前那些矿工的灵魂还没有走。

"前面有分岔。"李锡尼走上前，手中举着佛朗哥留下的维苏威火山第三版内部勘测图，图纸已经被汗浸透了边角，但上面的线条依然清晰。

他指向左侧一条更窄的支巷，巷道口用红漆写着"7-A"。

"走7-A。"李锡尼说，"这是直达熔岩之心外围平台的旧通道，三百年前用来运输硬金矿石。"

他顿了一下，又补了一句。

"老图纸上标注，从这里开始温度会持续上升。"

没有人说话。他们继续前进。

走了大约二十分钟，温度明显升高了，防护服内衬的影金属丝线开始发挥作用，把热量隔绝在身体之外，但呼吸依然变得困难，空气干燥而滚烫，每吸一口都像在吞咽烧红的铁屑。

然后他们听到了轰鸣声。

低沉的、持续的、像一颗巨大的心脏在跳动的轰鸣声，从脚底传上来，穿过靴底，穿过骨骼，一直钻进颅腔深处。

"火山。"唐璜说。

他的声音被轰鸣声压得有些发颤，但没有人笑话他。

矿道尽头是一扇铁门。

铁门已经被锈蚀得面目全非，门板上用红漆写着一个巨大的字母"A"，漆面起泡剥落，露出底下的铸铁纹理。阿方索上前检查了一遍门框，确认没有机关或警报，才伸手用力推。

门轴发出一声尖锐的哀鸣，铁门缓缓向内打开。

热浪扑面而来。

不是温热，是真正的、足以让裸露皮肤瞬间起泡的灼热气流。防护服内衬的影金属丝线在热浪中嗡了一声，自动激活了冷却循环。

门后面是一片巨大的圆形平台。

平台悬在熔岩之心的边缘，直径超过两百米，边缘没有栏杆，只有一圈矮矮的铁制安全链，链条已经被高温烤成了暗红色。平台的另一端是深不见底的熔岩池，岩浆缓慢翻涌，橘红色和暗金色交替闪烁，像是大地深处敞开的一只巨大伤口。

整个空间被岩浆的光芒照得通明，岩石穹顶高悬在头顶至少五十米以上，穹顶表面镶嵌着数以千计的黄铜齿轮，齿轮的排列方式和矿道中的一样紧密，但尺寸大了十倍不止。每一颗齿轮都在缓慢转动，发出低沉的共鸣声。

红水银蒸汽从熔岩池中升起，在穹顶下方形成淡红色的雾气，像是给这个空间蒙上了一层血色的纱。

"这就是熔岩之心。"李锡尼低声说。

西泽尔站在平台边缘，俯瞰脚下翻涌的岩浆。

红水银蒸汽扑面而来，温热而腥甜，像是某种巨大生物的呼吸。他能感觉到后颈的黄金套管在发烫，温度比刚才更高了，烫得他头皮发麻。

他抬起头。

平台的正中央，竖着一座十字架。

十字架是铁制的，高约五米，横臂上焊着粗糙的铁环，铁环上挂着铁链。铁链的另一端绑着一个人。

碧儿·丹缇。

她被铁链缚住双臂，整个人悬挂在十字架上，双脚离地约一尺。黑色的长发散落下来，遮住了半张脸。她的教廷档案员制服已经被烧焦了大半，露出底下一件单薄的白色内衫，内衫被汗水浸透，贴在身上。

她还活着。

她的头微微低着，但胸腔还在起伏，每一次呼吸都带出细微的喘息声。

"碧儿！"唐璜向前冲了一步。

"别动。"西泽尔说。

他的声音不大，但唐璜的脚步硬生生停住了。

西泽尔的目光没有看碧儿，而是看着碧儿脚下的平台地面。

那里画着一个圈。圆圈用红水银画成，直径约十米，圈内的岩层呈现出一种不自然的暗红色，像是有什么东西在岩石下面涌动。圈外刻着密密麻麻的梵文，和矿道壁上的齿轮浮雕风格一致。

"是触发阵。"阿方索皱眉，"红水银触发阵，碧儿一旦被移出那个圈，圈内的红水银就会引爆。"

"引爆炸这个平台？"瓦莲京娜问。

"不，炸她。"阿方索说，"红水银会沿铁链上行，把她烧成灰。"

唐璜的手指无声扣紧了蔷薇之鬼的臂甲，指节发白。

"还有别的办法吗？"昆提良问。

阿方索沉默了两秒。

"需要有人从外部解除触发阵。红水银触发阵的解除条件是'等价替换'——用同等质量的活体物质替代圈内的人质。但问题是，"他看了一眼碧儿脚下的圆圈，"这个圈太大了，我计算不出需要多少活体物质。"

"你不用计算。"西泽尔说。

他走向十字架，每一步都踩在红水银蒸汽里，防护服的靴底发出轻微的嘶嘶声。他在距离碧儿约五米的地方停下来，仰头看着她。

碧儿缓缓抬起头。

她的脸上有烧伤的痕迹，右侧颧骨到耳根的皮肤被高温烫出一片水泡，但她的眼睛还是清醒的，瞳孔里映着熔岩的橘红色光芒。

"西泽尔大人。"她的声音沙哑，像是被烟呛了很久，"对不起，我又给您添麻烦了。"

"你做得对。"西泽尔说，"是我让你去梵蒂冈档案室的。"

碧儿的嘴角微微牵动了一下，像是想笑，但烧伤的皮肤扯得她皱眉。

"阿黛尔小姐……"她开口。

西泽尔抬手制止了她。

"我知道。"

他转过身，背对着十字架，目光扫过平台的另一端。

那里是熔岩池的边缘，橘红色的岩浆缓慢翻涌，热浪从池面升起，让整个平台都笼罩在一种扭曲的透明波动中。透过热浪，他看到熔岩池上方的岩壁上嵌着一扇门。

门是黑铁铸成的，高度超过十米，门面上刻着巨大的卡巴拉之树图案——树干是暗金色的金属，枝桠向四面八方伸展，每一片叶子的位置都嵌着一颗缓缓转动的齿轮。树根向下延伸，消失在岩壁深处。

那就是黑铁巨门。

通往世界树残枝所在圆形大厅的入口。

门是关着的。

"您来得比我预想的要快。"

一个声音从平台边缘传来，不急不缓，带着一种少年人故作老成的腔调。

西泽尔循声看去。

平台的左侧边缘，红水银蒸汽最浓的地方，一个巨大的轮廓正在缓缓浮现。先是头部的夔龙面甲，然后是宽阔到几乎填满整个矿道的双肩，接着是粗壮的手臂，手臂末端握着一柄六米长的巨型反曲锯齿巨刃。

第三代普罗米修斯·古洛诺斯Ⅱ。

原型机。

比胡安之前驾驶的古洛诺斯还要大一号，全身覆盖着暗金色的重型装甲板，每一块装甲板边缘都刻着世界树神经祈祷文。背部搭载着四门蒸汽加农炮，炮管粗得像成年人的腰，炮口正对着平台中央。胸腔里嵌着一颗暴龙级红水银动力核心，核心每跳动一次，周围的空气就震颤一次。

骑士舱打开。

一个十五岁的少年从舱口探出身来。

他穿着密涅瓦机关核心骑士制式军服，但外面套了一件博尔吉亚家族的金线刺绣披风，披风上绣着双头鹰和蛇发女妖的纹章。他的脸还带着少年的稚气，下颌线条却已经变得硬朗，一双眼睛——浅灰色的、冰冷的眼睛——正死死地盯着西泽尔。

胡安·博尔吉亚。

教皇和合法夫人所生的次子，西泽尔同父异母的弟弟。

"西泽尔哥哥。"胡安的声音在蒸汽中回荡，"还是该叫你红龙？"

西泽尔没有回答。

"你知道我等这一天等了多久吗？"胡安从骑士舱中站起来，披风在热浪中翻飞，"从你被当成异端烧死的那天起，我就在等。我以为你死了，我以为我终于可以把博尔吉亚家族的一切都握在手里了——圣殿骑士的封号，炽天骑士团的继承权，父亲的认可。"

他的声音在升高。

"然后你回来了。你不仅回来了，你还成了父亲的小黑山羊，成了密涅瓦机关的红龙，成了万国盛典上打败了腓特烈的英雄！"胡安的手在古洛诺斯Ⅱ的控制杆上捏得咯咯作响，"而我呢？我连在你身边当个跟班都不配！"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的暴龙级核心发出一声低沉的轰鸣，像是回应着主人的愤怒。

"你知道我在原罪机关是怎么过来的吗？"胡安的声音忽然冷了下来，"每天穿着这身铁皮训练到吐血，每一天都在想，怎么才能让西泽尔·博尔吉亚跪在我面前。"

他伸手向平台中央一指。

碧儿·丹缇悬挂在十字架上，铁链在她身上叮当作响。

"她是个诱饵。"胡安说，"格拉古大主教把她绑在这里，就是等着你跳进来。那个触发阵不是用来杀她的，是用来消耗你的。"

西泽尔没有动。

"阿黛尔在哪里？"他问。

胡安笑了。

少年的笑容在红水银蒸汽中显得有些扭曲，像是被人用手指硬掰出来的。

"你想知道她在哪里？"胡安说，"我可以告诉你。"

他伸手指向那扇黑铁巨门。

"在那扇门后面。在熔岩之心的最深处。"

他的手指在黑铁巨门上停留了一秒，然后收回来。

"但你过不去。那扇门有三重封印，没有钥匙，你连碰都碰不了。"

西泽尔的目光越过胡安，落在那扇黑铁巨门上。

门面上的卡巴拉之树图案在熔岩的光芒中缓缓旋转，每一片叶子的齿轮都在以不同的速度转动，整个图案看上去像是一幅活的画。树根的末端消失在岩壁中，但在他紫瞳的视野里，树根的尽头隐约透出一点淡金色的光，像是有什么东西在门的另一侧等待。

"你们有钥匙吗？"西泽尔问。

"我们不需要钥匙。"胡安说，"我们只需要你。"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的六管转轮机枪从手臂甲下方展开，枪管开始旋转，发出刺耳的机械摩擦声。

"父亲把你当工具，格拉古大主教把你当工具，密涅瓦机关把你当工具。"胡安的声音从蒸汽中传来，带着一种奇异的平静，"现在轮到我了。"

"我也要用你。"

他按下控制杆。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的背部四门蒸汽加农炮同时开火。

不是实弹，是红水银填充的薄壳榴弹，四发炮弹呈扇形射出，拖着暗红色的尾焰，在空中划出四道弧线，精准地覆盖了平台中央的每一寸地面。

"散开！"西泽尔低喝。

唐璜、昆提良、阿方索、瓦莲京娜同时向四个方向扑出。唐璜的身影在蒸汽中一闪，蔷薇之鬼甲胄的关节发出一连串金属咔嗒声，超轻型的刺客机体让他在不到一秒内就滑出了十五米。

昆提良的奥古斯都沉重地落地，强化装甲和秘银重盾同时展开，他举起五层交错锻造的秘银重盾，闭眼狮头纹章正对着弹道，重盾表面的影金属在高温中泛着暗蓝色的光。

阿方索的所罗门王没有动，他只是轻轻按下蜘蛛巢腕表上的一个按钮，八只微型机械蜘蛛从腕表中鱼贯而出，向四面八方散开。

瓦莲京娜的改装神怒Ⅲ型在平台上滑行，背部的蒸汽喷射推进器喷出一股青蓝色气流，把她连人带甲胄送到了平台的另一侧，落地时冰原寒玉在关节处发出清脆的碎裂声。

第一发榴弹在碧儿脚下的触发阵边缘爆炸。

红水银蒸汽和岩石碎屑一起飞溅，但触发阵没有引爆——胡安用的是薄壳弹，威力不足以触发红水银连锁反应。

但爆炸的冲击波让十字架剧烈摇晃，碧儿的身体被铁链拽得在空中打转，一声闷哼从她嘴里逸出。

"你疯了吗？"唐璜的声音从蒸汽中传来，"她会死的！"

"她死不死跟我有什么关系？"胡安的声音毫无波动，"诱饵就是用来消耗的。"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的六管转轮机枪开始扫射。

子弹像暴雨一样倾泻在平台上，每一颗都拖着暗红色的尾焰，撞击在岩石上炸出一朵朵橘红色的火花。阿方索的六只微型机械蜘蛛已经就位，它们钻进岩石缝隙中，开启信号干扰模式，释放出宽频电磁脉冲，试图让古洛诺斯Ⅱ的火控系统失灵。

电磁脉冲在空气中扩散，古洛诺斯Ⅱ的瞄准系统屏幕上开始出现雪花。

胡安皱了下眉。

"阿方索的蜘蛛。"他冷笑一声，"你以为这套把戏能对我用几次？"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ胸腔里的暴龙级核心骤然加速运转，核心表面的红水银纹路亮了起来，一股肉眼可见的暗金色能量波从核心向外扩散。波纹扫过平台，所过之处，阿方索释放的六只微型机械蜘蛛的腹部红水银微晶同时过载，蜘蛛的身体在瞬间烧成了一缕青烟。

"欧米茄自愈神经纤维。"阿方索低声说，"他在原型机里也装了。"

"不只是原型机。"李锡尼的声音从平台边缘传来，他一直没有动，蹲在一个矿道壁龛的阴影里，用佛朗哥的神经电流读出器扫描着古洛诺斯Ⅱ的结构，"这台古洛诺斯Ⅱ的神经接驳系统是全新的——骑士的脊髓信号直接被欧米茄自愈神经纤维读取，跳过了所有机械传导延迟。"

"反应速度呢？"西泽尔问。

"比之前的古洛诺斯快了至少一倍。"

西泽尔没有说话。

他站在平台中央，背后是绑着碧儿的十字架，面前是正在逼近的古洛诺斯Ⅱ。红水银蒸汽在他周围翻涌，热浪让他的头发和衣服都在轻微飘动。他的紫瞳在蒸汽中泛着淡淡的光，像是两颗被火焰包裹的宝石。

"穿上甲胄。"他对身后的同伴说。

阿方索没有犹豫。所罗门王的神经接驳系统启动，背部装甲板向两侧展开，露出内部骑士舱。阿方索转身进入舱室，装甲板合拢，神经接驳针刺入他的脊椎。同一时刻，昆提良也登上了奥古斯都——沉重的装甲在他身上合拢时发出低沉的金属碰撞声，秘银重盾被他单手举起，闭眼狮头纹章正对着古洛诺斯Ⅱ。

唐璜的蔷薇之鬼没有装甲板展开的过程，超轻型机体直接套在他身上，关节处发出细密的咔嗒声，像是一只蜷缩的金属蜘蛛。

瓦莲京娜也动了。改装神怒Ⅲ型在她身上合拢时，冰原寒玉在脊椎接口处碎裂成粉末，叶尼塞王妃的红水银晶块核心在胸腔中跳动起来，释放出比普通核心强一倍的能量脉冲。

"你去救碧儿。"西泽尔对李锡尼说。

李锡尼点头。他从腰后取下黑色十字纹蜂巢手铳，和塔拉夏一起贴着平台边缘向十字架方向迂回。

"那我们呢？"唐璜问。

"你们负责古洛诺斯Ⅱ的附属机械兵。"西泽尔说，"等它们出来。"

"附属机械兵？"阿方索皱眉。

他的话音未落，平台边缘的矿道入口处传来了密集的脚步声。

不是人类的脚步，是金属踏在岩石上的沉重撞击声。

三台。

从矿道中鱼贯而出的，是三台第一代普罗米修斯量产型甲胄。每一台都有四米高，全身哑光黑色轻型装甲，关节处刻着世界树神经祈祷文。它们的指尖泛着暗金色的热能丝光芒，六管转轮机枪从手臂甲下方展开。

"这才是诱饵。"胡安的声音从古洛诺斯Ⅱ的扩音器中传出，"碧儿·丹缇只是开胃菜，这三台才是正餐。"

三台普罗米修斯量产型一字排开，六管转轮机枪同时开始旋转，枪管转动的嗡嗡声和古洛诺斯Ⅱ的暴龙级核心轰鸣声混在一起，让整个平台都在震颤。

"唐璜、昆提良、阿方索。"西泽尔说。

"在。"

"那三台是你们的。"

"明白。"

三台试制型炽天使甲胄同时冲了出去。

昆提良的奥古斯都冲在最前面，五层交错锻造的秘银重盾挡在身前，第一台普罗米修斯的六管转轮机枪全部火力倾泻在重盾上，子弹撞击在影金属和硬金交替排列的盾面上，发出密集的金属碰撞声。秘银重盾纹丝不动，闭眼狮头纹章在火光中像是一头沉默的雄狮。

"来啊！"昆提良低吼。

阿方索的所罗门王在昆提良身后停下，他从背后取下一杆长管狙击铳，枪管比普通狙击铳粗了一倍，铳口泛着暗红色的光——那是暴力增强型雷霆牙的弹头结构，红水银注入量提高到原来的三倍，用微型蒸汽阀控制引爆时机。

他没有立刻开枪。他在等。

唐璜的蔷薇之鬼在蒸汽中消失了。

超轻型机体的优势在这种环境中被发挥到了极致——蔷薇之鬼的重量只有奥古斯都的三分之一，关节灵活度却是后者的两倍。唐璜借助红水银蒸汽的掩护，绕到了第一台普罗米修斯的侧后方，那里是量产型甲胄最薄弱的环节——连接胸腔动力核心和四肢的能量管线。

管线暴露在装甲板的缝隙间，像是一根根暗红色的血管。

唐璜抽出青蛇剑。

剑身弯曲如蛇窄而长，覆着淡绿色的铜锈。这柄剑是达·芬奇留给继承者的七把名剑之一，材质与初代炽天使武器同源，刚好适配他的手掌。

他挥剑。

青蛇剑从侧后方切入，精准地斩断了第一台普罗米修斯的右臂能量管线。管线断裂的瞬间，高压蒸汽从断口喷出，普罗米修斯的右臂痉挛了一下，六管转轮机枪停止了转动。

唐璜没有停。他借着斩击的反作用力，在空中翻了个身，落在普罗米修斯的肩甲上，又一剑切断了左臂的管线。

双臂同时失去动力的普罗米修斯轰然倒地，砸在岩石地面上，溅起大片碎石。

"第一台，倒了。"唐璜的声音从通讯频道中传来。

"漂亮。"阿方索说。

他的狙击铳终于开火了。

暴力增强型雷霆牙的弹头穿透了第二台普罗米修斯的胸腔装甲，弹头在动力核心内部爆炸，红水银点燃了核心的能量循环，三秒之内，第二台普罗米修斯的胸腔被炸成了一团橘红色的火球。

"第二台。"阿方索说。

第三台普罗米修斯试图向唐璜和阿方索开火，但昆提良已经冲到了它面前。奥古斯都的秘银重盾直接拍在普罗米修斯的胸甲上，五层交错锻造的盾面在撞击的瞬间收缩了一下——冰原寒玉的低温让金属微收缩形成二次缓冲——然后重盾的力量透过去，把普罗米修斯拍得连连后退。

"让开！"唐璜从昆提良肩头跃过，青蛇剑精准地刺入了第三台普罗米修斯的面甲缝隙，剑尖贯穿了内部的骑士舱。

金属断裂声。蒸汽泄漏声。骑士的惨叫。

第三台普罗米修斯缓缓倒下。

"清场完毕。"昆提良说。

但古洛诺斯Ⅱ已经动了。

胡安没有给他们喘息的时间。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ迈出第一步的时候，整个平台都在震颤。原型机比量产型大了不止一倍，每一步落地都在岩石上踩出蛛网状的裂纹。它手中的六米长巨型反曲锯齿巨刃从侧面横扫过来，锯齿在空气中发出尖锐的啸叫，像是一头正在咆哮的巨兽。

"散开！"

瓦莲京娜的改装神怒Ⅲ型在蒸汽中跃起，冰原寒玉研磨的叶尼塞战斧从空中劈下，斧刃撞上古洛诺斯Ⅱ的巨刃。两件巨型武器碰撞的瞬间，冲击波把方圆十米的红水银蒸汽都吹散了。

瓦莲京娜被巨力震得倒飞出去，落地时在岩石上滑出了五六米远，冰原寒玉在关节处再次碎裂。

"好重……"她低声说。

"让开，公主殿下。"西泽尔说。

他的声音很平静。

瓦莲京娜没有逞强，她操控改装神怒Ⅲ型退到了平台边缘，把正面让给了西泽尔。

平台中央只剩下西泽尔和古洛诺斯Ⅱ。

热浪从熔岩池中升起，把两个人的影子都拉得很长。影子在岩石地面上交叠在一起，像是两个即将搏杀的巨人。

新型红龙甲胄就停放在平台的角落里。

密涅瓦机关为西泽尔打造的强化版炽天使机动甲胄，保留着超重武装和剑舞者双形态，武器系统做了全面强化。甲胄静静地伫立在红水银蒸汽中，胸口的暗红色能量纹路像是一颗正在跳动的心脏，左肩上用东方文字刻着"红龙"两个字。

西泽尔走向甲胄。

他的脚步不快，但每一步都很稳。他伸手按上甲胄的胸甲，指尖触到金属表面的瞬间，后颈的黄金套管剧烈发烫，烫得他手指不自觉地抖了一下。

甲胄的神经接驳系统启动。

超重武装的外挂装甲板向两侧展开，露出内部骑士舱。舱内亮起淡金色的光，照亮了西泽尔苍白的面孔。他的紫瞳在光芒中泛着深邃的紫色，像是被火焰包裹的两颗黑曜石。

他进入舱室。

装甲板合拢。

神经接驳针刺入他的脊椎。

新红龙试制版炽天使甲胄的神经接驳系统和西泽尔后颈的黄金套管完美匹配，耦合度在启动的瞬间就攀升到了百分之九十七。甲胄的每一块装甲板、每一个关节、每一根能量管线，都像是变成了他身体的延伸。

他抬起右手。

新红龙的右手和西泽尔的右手同步握拳，金属指节发出一连串清脆的咔嗒声。

"红龙。"

胡安的声音从古洛诺斯Ⅱ的扩音器中传出。

"来吧。让我看看密涅瓦机关花了多少钱打造的玩具，到底能不能打得过第三代普罗米修斯。"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的暴龙级核心轰鸣着，迈开大步冲了过来。巨型反曲锯齿巨刃从上方劈下，刃口的锯齿在空气中划出一道暗红色的弧光，像是死神的镰刀从天空中砸下来。

西泽尔举起龙牙剑。

剑身是断茬拼接的——断茬处嵌着圣剑装具·Excalibur的碎片，那是龙德施泰特从莲花作战带回来的。断茬与碎片拼接的接缝处泛着微弱的白光，像是两种不同的金属在互相排斥又互相吸引。

剑与巨刃在空中相撞。

冲击波从碰撞点向四面八方扩散，岩石地面被震出蛛网状的裂纹，红水银蒸汽被冲击波吹成一个环形，向外扩散出去。

西泽尔的手臂在龙牙剑传来的巨力中发麻。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的输出功率远超他的预期。暴龙级核心的能量在原型机中咆哮着，每一次脉动都给胡安的手提供更多的力量。

"不行啊，哥哥。"胡安的声音从扩音器中传出，带着一种压抑已久的快意，"就这点力气？"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的巨刃继续压下来，锯齿在龙牙剑的剑身上摩擦，发出刺耳的金属嘶鸣。火花从剑刃与锯齿的接触点飞溅出来，像是流星雨。

西泽尔后退了一步。

"你的剑在抖。"胡安说，"看，你的整条手臂都在抖。"

他说的没错。神经电流读出器如果还在运转的话，会显示西泽尔的神经接驳系统正在承受巨大的负荷——古洛诺斯Ⅱ的力量透过龙牙剑传到甲胄，再从甲胄传到他的脊椎，每一秒都在啃噬他的神经通路。

西泽尔没有说话。

他用左手摸向后腰。

那里别着一柄剑。

青蛇剑。

不，那不是青蛇剑。那是一柄更古老的剑，剑身上没有铜锈，只有黑色的金属纹理，剑柄缠着褪色的绿绢，剑格处铸着一个已经模糊不清的博尔吉亚家族徽记。

初代断剑。

三百年前第一任断剑骑士冈扎罗·博尔吉亚的佩剑。莲生在达·芬奇的备件库中把它交给了西泽尔。能斩断所有机械神国的造物，包括欧米茄原型体。

西泽尔没有用这柄剑。

不是现在。

他用龙牙剑硬接胡安的巨刃，左手则按下了甲胄左肩的一个隐藏按钮。

新红龙试制版甲胄的肩部辅助喷射口喷出了高速蒸汽。

蒸汽被熔岩的红光染成金红色，在西泽尔背后展开成两扇扇形的光翼。高温高压的气幕在甲胄周围形成了一道屏障，挡住了巨刃压下来的部分力量。

西泽尔趁此机会抽身后退，拉开了和古洛诺斯Ⅱ的距离。

"跑什么？"胡安追上来。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的速度比西泽尔预想的更快。原型机的腿部关节经过了特殊改装，每一步的跨度都超过五米，三步就追到了西泽尔面前。巨刃再次从上方劈下，这一次胡安用上了全力，暴龙级核心的能量灌注到巨刃中，刃口的锯齿在空气中燃烧起来，像是裹着一层橘红色的火焰。

西泽尔举起龙牙剑格挡。

两柄武器再次碰撞。

但这一次古洛诺斯Ⅱ的力量比刚才大了一倍。

西泽尔的膝盖弯曲了。新红龙甲胄的膝关节发出一声不堪重负的金属呻吟，膝盖下方的岩石地面被踩出两个深坑。他的手臂在龙牙剑的握柄上滑了一下，指关节的白手套被磨出了血痕。

"跪下。"胡安说。

他的声音不再愤怒，反而变得平静。

"跪下，西泽尔。跪在我面前，承认你不如我。承认你只是一个私生子，一个被父亲捡回来的工具，一个本该在翡冷翠贫民窟里烂掉的可怜虫。"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的巨刃继续压下来。

西泽尔的脊椎在神经接驳系统传来的巨力下发出细微的咯吱声。他的视野开始模糊，红水银蒸汽让一切都变得不真实。

但他的紫瞳没有变。

没有变成金红色，没有出现金色的纹路。后颈的黄金套管在发烫，但还没有到启动不朽之王系统的阈值。

他还在撑。

"我不会跪。"西泽尔说。

他的声音很轻，被巨刃和甲胄的碰撞声压得几乎听不见。但胡安听到了。

"你说什么？"

"我说，"西泽尔的紫瞳中映着巨刃燃烧的火焰，"我不会跪。"

他用龙牙剑的断茬——嵌着圣剑碎片的那一截——精准地切入了巨刃锯齿的缝隙间。

接缝处的白光骤然亮起。

龙牙剑断茬与Excalibur碎片的接缝爆发出刺眼的白光，那是两种不同金属在互相排斥时产生的能量脉冲。脉冲沿着巨刃的锯齿传导出去，所过之处，锯齿表面出现了一道道细微的裂纹。

胡安的表情变了。

"这是什么——"

他的话没说完。

西泽尔已经借着巨刃被脉冲震开的那一瞬间，操控新红龙甲胄后退了三步。

但古洛诺斯Ⅱ的反应速度超出了他的预期。欧米茄自愈神经纤维让胡安的指令传导延迟降到了零，原型机几乎是本能地追了上来，巨刃从侧面横扫过来。

这一次西泽尔没能躲开。

巨刃的锯齿擦过了新红龙甲胄的右肩甲。

不是正面命中，是擦过。但即便如此，锯齿也在肩甲上留下了一道深可见骨的切口。切口处的装甲板向内翻卷，露出了内部精密的神经接驳线路，有几根线路被锯齿切断，电火花从断口处飞溅出来。

西泽尔的右肩传来一阵剧痛——神经接驳系统的反馈信号告诉他，甲胄的右肩关节受损了，至少三个电机失灵，右臂的活动范围下降了百分之四十。

他操控新红龙甲胄后退，单手举着龙牙剑，面对着继续逼近的古洛诺斯Ⅱ。

"哥哥，你的甲胄坏了。"胡安说，"还要打吗？"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的巨刃再次举起。

这一次的姿态和之前不同——巨刃没有从上方劈下，也没有从侧面横扫，而是直直地指向了新红龙甲胄的骑士舱位置。

要一击刺穿。

西泽尔的紫瞳盯着那柄正在逼近的巨刃。

热浪让他的视野开始扭曲，红水银蒸汽在巨刃周围形成了一层橘红色的光晕。巨刃的锯齿在高温中燃烧，像是裹着一层地狱的火焰。

他举起龙牙剑格挡。

但右肩的损伤让他的动作慢了半拍。

巨刃突破了龙牙剑的防御，刃尖直直地刺向新红龙甲胄的骑士舱位置。刃尖距离舱壁还有不到一米。

半米。

三十厘米。

西泽尔的紫瞳在巨刃的阴影中骤然变亮。

不是紫，是金红色。

像是被火焰点燃的宝石，像是黎明前东方天际的第一缕光。

后颈的黄金套管开始剧烈发烫。

不朽之王系统正在启动。

【English】
Chapter 252 — The Heart of Mount Vesuvius

A point of dark gold light rose slowly out of the deep of the mine. Not an eye. A miner's lamp, hung from the vault of the tunnel on a chain that had been blackened by three centuries of heat, the copper shade still bearing the eagle-and-hammer crest of the Anglia family cast into the metal. The wick that burned inside it was not oil. It was a slow, thick pulse of red quicksilver, and each time the pulse jumped, the rock on either side of the passage was lit for one heartbeat, revealing long stretches of bas-relief gears carved into the basalt — a thousand cogs, teeth biting teeth, running the full length of the corridor out of sight.

Cesare did not look back at the men behind him. He kept walking. His footsteps went down the mine and came back to him in echoes that braided themselves with the hum of the quicksilver wick, as if something deeper in the mountain were breathing in time.

"Captain," Alfonso murmured from behind.

"I hear it," Cesare said.

His voice was level. The golden cannula set into the nape of his neck had begun to burn — not painfully, not yet, but with that quick, alert heat he had learned to obey. He lifted a hand and pressed two fingers to the metal through the back of his collar. The surface was vibrating under his touch, a fine, close tremor, as though something inside the sleeve were stirring in its sleep.

"All of you, combat dress," he said.

Alfonso nodded. From the sealed pack at his hip he took out a stack of folded silver-grey suits, each one a single close-fitting garment whose inner lining had been quilted with thousands of fine threads of shadow-metal — cold to the touch, heavy in the hand, and worth, by Minerva Bureau accounting, more than most country houses. He shook the first one out and passed it to Cesare, then to Valentyna, then to Don Juan, then to Quintilian, and only at the end pulled one on for himself.

These were Minerva Bureau Class A thermal-and-blast suits, rated to keep a man alive at eight hundred degrees for half an hour. They had been made for engineers who had to go down into the Heart.

The passage widened.

The Anglia miners, three hundred years dead, had cut this corridor out of the basalt one chisel-blow at a time, and the walls were still rough under the quicksilver light. Every fifteen paces, a niche had been hollowed out of the rock. They had been made for oil lamps; the oil was long gone, and the quicksilver wicks had taken their place, throwing out a low amber warmth that made the niches look, in the moving shadows, like the still-open mouths of the men who had lit them.

"Branch ahead," Licinius said, and came forward. He held the third-edition interior survey of Vesuvius that Franco had left behind. The edges of the paper had gone soft with sweat, but the lines of the drawing were clean.

He pointed down the narrower of the two side-passages. A number had been painted at its mouth in flaking red lacquer: 7-A.

"We take 7-A," Licinius said. "Old haulage, straight through to the outer platform of the Heart. They used to run the hard-gold ore down it."

He paused.

"The old plans mark a continuous temperature rise from here on," he said.

No one answered. They went on.

Twenty minutes in, the air began to work at the lungs. The shadow-metal lining of the suits took the worst of the heat and held it away from the body, but the breath a man could draw in was still dry and seemed to scald the throat on the way down, as though he were swallowing red-hot filings.

Then they heard the roaring.

It was not a sound made in the world above. It was a sound made under the world, low and unending, as if some enormous heart, buried too deep in the earth, had been beating since before there were ears to hear it. It came up through the soles of their boots, through the bones of their feet, and went on rising into the skull.

"Vesuvius," Don Juan said.

His voice was thin against the noise, and no one laughed at him.

The end of the mine was a door of iron.

The iron had rusted until it was no longer iron, only a brown ghost of a door, and across it in flaking red lacquer was painted one large capital: A. Alfonso ran his hands around the frame, checking for tripwire, for pressure plate, for the small telltale tremor of a galvanic alarm, and finding none, set his shoulder against the metal and pushed.

The hinges screamed. The door swung slowly inward.

The heat came in like a wall.

Not warmth. Heat — the kind of heat that would raise a blister on bare skin in the time it took to blink. The shadow-metal lining in their suits gave a single sharp hum as the cooling cycle came up, and the temperature inside the suit dropped a few degrees from lethal to merely murderous.

Beyond the door was a platform.

It was round, and it was vast — two hundred metres across, more or less, and it hung over the edge of the Heart itself. There was no railing. There was only a low chain of wrought iron set into the rock at the lip, and the chain had been cooked over centuries to the colour of old blood. At the far side of the platform the rock ended, and beyond that ending was the pit. The pit went down and down, and what was at the bottom of it was a slow, slow welling of molten stone — orange and dark gold alternating in slow, swallowing gulps, the way a wound in a body might be seen to heave if one watched it long enough.

The whole of the great chamber was lit by that light. The vault above them rose a full fifty metres, perhaps more, and into that vault had been set, by hands no one now living could name, thousands of cogs of brass. The cogs were the same pattern as the ones in the corridor below, but ten times the size, and they were all turning, very slowly, in a low common harmony that could be felt in the back teeth.

From the pit, the vapour of red quicksilver rose in a slow reddish fog that hung below the vault, and through that fog the chamber looked as if it had been curtained in blood.

"This is it," Licinius said, low. "The Heart."

Cesare walked to the edge of the platform. Below him, the lake heaved.

The quicksilver vapour came up into his face. It was warm, and faintly sweet in a way that was not sweet at all, like the breath of some great sleeping animal at the back of a cave. The golden cannula in his neck was burning now, harder than before, hot enough that the skin of his scalp began to prickle under it.

He looked up.

In the middle of the platform, set on a square of bare stone, stood a cross.

The cross was of iron. It was perhaps five metres tall. Welded to the cross-arm were two rough iron rings, and from the rings hung iron chains, and at the end of the chains was a woman.

Belle Dantie.

Her arms were shackled above her head and her whole body hung a foot or so clear of the platform. Her black hair had fallen forward and half hid her face. What was left of the Vatican archivist's uniform she had been wearing had been charred to rags, and under it, where it had not been burned away, the thin white shift beneath was soaked through with sweat and clung to her.

She was alive.

Her head was bowed, but her chest rose and fell. Each breath came out of her as a small, broken sound, the kind of sound the throat makes when it has been coughing smoke for hours.

"Belle!" Don Juan was moving before anyone could speak. He took a step forward.

"Stop," Cesare said.

His voice was not loud. Don Juan's boot stopped in the air and set down where it had been.

Cesare was not looking at Belle.

He was looking at the ground under her feet.

Someone had drawn a circle there. It was ten metres across, and it had been laid down in red quicksilver, thick as a man's thumb, and inside the circle the rock of the platform had taken on a colour that was not its own — a dark, sore red, the colour of something moving under the stone, as if the rock were bruised. Inside the ring, around the inner edge, a dense border of Hebrew letters had been incised into the floor, in the same style as the gear-reliefs in the mine.

"A trigger," Alfonso said, frowning. "A red-quicksilver trigger. If Belle is taken out of that circle, the quicksilver in the ring goes up."

"Up as in detonate the platform?" Valentyna asked.

"No," Alfonso said. "Up as in detonate her. The quicksilver will run the chains, the way fire runs a fuse. There will be nothing left of her to bury."

Don Juan's fingers closed slowly around the vambrace of the Rose Ghost. The knuckles of his hand went white under the suit.

"Is there another way?" Quintilian asked.

Alfonso was quiet for two seconds.

"Someone on the outside could break the trigger. The deactivation condition is *equal substitution* — a living body, of equal mass, in the circle in her place. The trouble is —" he looked again at the ten-metre circle under Belle's feet, " — I cannot tell you how much living matter that ring wants. The numbers are not on our side."

"You don't need to do the maths," Cesare said.

He walked toward the cross. Each step he took was through a thin layer of red-quicksilver vapour, and the soles of his boots gave a small hiss on the hot stone. He stopped about five metres from the hanging woman and stood there, looking up at her.

Belle raised her head.

There were burns on the right side of her face, a field of blisters from her cheekbone to the lobe of her ear, but the eye he could see was awake. The pupil of it was lit from below by the orange of the pit, and that colour burned there as if it had been painted in.

"Sir Cesare," she said. Her voice was hoarse, the voice of a person who had been breathing smoke for a long time. "I'm sorry. I've made trouble for you again."

"You did what you were told," Cesare said. "I sent you to the Vatican archive."

The corner of her mouth moved, as if she had meant to smile, but the burned skin of her cheek pulled at it and the smile became a wince.

"Miss Adele —" she began.

Cesare held up a hand, very slightly, and she stopped.

"I know," he said.

He turned his back to the cross and looked out across the platform.

At the far edge of the platform, on the other side of the pit, the rock wall of the chamber rose, and set into that wall was a door.

The door was of black iron. It was more than ten metres tall. Across its face had been engraved a single vast design — the Kabbalistic Tree, the tree of life. The trunk of it was a panel of dark gold metal. From the trunk, branches went out in every direction, and where the leaves of the branches would have been, a cog had been set, and each cog was turning at its own speed, so that the whole picture moved in the wall like a slow breathing thing. The roots of the tree ran down the door and on, into the rock beyond it, and disappeared.

The Black Iron Gate. The way in to the round hall where the bough of the World Tree was kept.

The gate was shut.

"I had not thought you would come quite so quickly."

A voice came from the edge of the platform. It was unhurried, and it had in it the particular affectation of a young man trying to sound older than he was.

Cesare looked.

Out of the thickest of the red-quicksilver vapour, on the left of the platform, a shape was assembling itself out of the red air. The face-plate of it came first, a mask worked into the likeness of a kui-long, the horned dragon of the old eastern bestiaries. Then the shoulders, broader than the door-frame they were passing through. Then the arms, long and thick, ending in a hand that held, the way a man might hold a child's stick, a blade six metres long — a great recurved saw-tooth sword.

Third-generation Prometheus. Gurnos II.

The prototype.

It was a full size larger than the Gurnos that Juan had piloted before, and it was plated, head to foot, in dark-gold heavy armour, the edge of every plate incised with the prayers of the World Tree's nervous system. On its back rode four steam-cannons, each one with a barrel as thick as a man's waist, and all four of them were trained on the centre of the platform. In its chest, a Tyrannosaurus-class red-quicksilver core beat like a second heart, and each beat shook the air.

The cockpit hatch opened.

A boy of fifteen leaned out of it.

Under the cockpit, he was wearing the standard Minerva Bureau core-knight dress uniform, but over it he had thrown a cloak embroidered in gold thread — the cloak of the Borgia house, with the double-headed eagle and the Gorgon worked into the cloth. His face still had the softness of a child about it, but the line of the jaw had begun, already, to harden. The eyes that looked out from under it were pale grey, and very cold.

Juan Borgia.

The second son of His Holiness the Pope and of his lawful wife. Cesare's half-brother.

"Brother Cesare," Juan said. His voice came back to them in echoes off the vault. "Or should I call you the Red Dragon?"

Cesare did not answer.

"Do you know how long I have been waiting for this?" Juan said, and he stood up in the cockpit so that the cloak could billow out behind him in the hot air from the pit. "From the day they burned you for a heretic. I have been waiting. I thought you were dead. I thought, finally, that the whole of the Borgia inheritance could be put into my hands — the Templar titles, the succession of the Order of the Burning Heaven, my father's good opinion."

His voice climbed as he spoke.

"And then you came back. You came back, and you were Father's little black goat, you were the Red Dragon of the Minerva Bureau, you were the hero of the Universal Festival who broke Frederick on the field. And I — I was not even fit to walk at your heel."

The Tyrannosaurus core of the Gurnos II gave a low snarl of a sound, as if it were answering the anger of its rider.

"Do you know what the years in the Original Sin Bureau were like for me?" Juan said, and his voice went cold. "Every day in that iron skin, training until I vomited blood. Every day, working out how to make Cesare Borgia kneel to me."

He pointed across the platform at the cross.

Belle hung in her chains. The chains made a small, dead sound against the iron of the cross.

"She is a lure," Juan said. "Archbishop Graccus had her bound here for you to come and find. The trigger-ring is not meant to kill her. It is meant to cost you."

Cesare had not moved.

"Where is Adele?" he said.

Juan smiled.

The smile of a fifteen-year-old, in red vapour, looked as if it had been worked into place by a hand that did not care whether the result was convincing.

"You want to know where she is," he said. "I can tell you that."

He pointed at the Black Iron Gate.

"Behind that door. At the bottom of the Heart."

He let his hand rest on the door for a second, then drew it back.

"But you cannot reach her. The door has three seals. Without the key, you cannot even touch it."

Cesare's gaze passed over Juan and came to rest on the Black Iron Gate. The Kabbalistic Tree turned slowly on the face of it, leaf by leaf, and in the depth of his purple eyes, the ends of the roots — down past the lower panel, down into the rock — gave back a faint answering gold, as if something on the far side of the door were looking back.

"Do you have the key?" Cesare asked.

"We don't need a key," Juan said. "We need you."

The Gurnos II's arm opened along the seam below the wrist-plate, and a six-barrel rotary gun slid out of the forearm. The barrels began to turn, with a small hard mechanical screaming.

"Father uses you as a tool," Juan said. "Archbishop Graccus uses you as a tool. The Minerva Bureau uses you as a tool. Now it is my turn."

"I am going to use you too."

He pulled the control stick.

The four steam-cannons on the Gurnos II's back fired together.

They did not fire solid shot. They fired thin-cased shells packed with red quicksilver, and the four of them went out in a fan, trailing dark-red tails, and covered the centre of the platform in a single overlapping arc of fire.

"Move!" Cesare said.

Don Juan, Quintilian, Alfonso, and Valentyna went four ways at once. Don Juan's Rose Ghost let off a long string of metallic clacks as the joints of the ultra-light assassin frame folded him, in under a second, fifteen metres sideways. Quintilian's Augustus came down on its feet with a deep boom, the reinforced plate and the five-layered mithril great shield coming up together, the closed-eyed lion on the face of the shield looking into the fire-line. Alfonso, in the Solomon King, did not move at all; he pressed a button on the spider-nest at his wrist, and eight tiny mechanical spiders ran out of the watch and scattered across the stone. Valentyna's modified Wrath III slid across the platform, the steam jets at its back spitting a pale blue exhaust that dumped her, suit and all, on the far side of the platform in a single move; the permafrost jade in the joints of the frame cracked as she landed.

The first shell went off at the edge of the trigger-ring under Belle.

Red vapour and rock splinters went up together. The trigger did not fire. The shells were thin-cased, and the blast was not enough to set off a quicksilver chain. But the shockwave took the cross by the base of it and shook it, and Belle's body swung in her chains like the body of a struck bell, and a small, broken sound came out of her mouth.

"Are you mad?" Don Juan's voice came out of the vapour. "She will die."

"What she does or does not do is nothing to me," Juan said, without inflection. "A lure is a thing to be spent."

The Gurnos II's six-barrel rotary began to fire in earnest.

The bullets came down on the platform like a red rain. Each one dragged a dark tail of vapour behind it; each one threw up a small orange flower of fire when it hit stone. The six of Alfonso's spiders were already in the cracks of the rock, broadcasting a wide-band electromagnetic pulse, and the Gurnos II's fire-control screen was going to snow.

Juan frowned.

"Alfonso's spiders," he said. "How many times do you think I have watched that trick?"

The Tyrannosaurus core in the chest of the prototype spun up. The quicksilver channels on the surface of it lit, and a visible wave of dark-gold energy went out from the core in every direction. Where the wave passed over a spider, the red-quicksilver micro-crystal in the spider's belly overloaded, and the spider burned to a wisp of blue smoke in its hole.

"Omega self-healing nerve-fibre," Alfonso said, low. "He has it in the prototype as well."

"And not only the prototype," Licinius's voice said, from the lip of the platform, where he had not moved. He was crouched in the shadow of one of the old wall-niches with Franco's neural-current reader in his hand, and the reader was still trained on the Gurnos II. "The neural coupling on this Gurnos II is new. The pilot's spinal signal is being read direct by the Omega self-healing fibre. There is no mechanical delay in the chain at all."

"How fast does that make him?" Cesare asked.

"Faster than the last Gurnos. At least twice as fast."

Cesare said nothing.

He stood in the middle of the platform, with the cross at his back and the Gurnos II in front of him. The vapour ran around him in slow red sheets. The heat of the pit pulled at the edges of his hair and at his clothes. His purple eyes caught the orange of the lake and threw it back, and for a moment the eyes looked like two small dark stones wrapped in flame.

"Get into the suits," he said, to the men behind him.

Alfonso did not hesitate. The neural coupling of the Solomon King came up. The back-plates of the suit folded out to either side and showed the cockpit within, a small golden light. Alfonso stepped into it; the plates closed; the coupling-needles went into his spine. Quintilian, at the same moment, climbed into the Augustus. The heavy plate came down on him piece by piece, with a series of deep metallic sounds; he lifted the mithril great shield in one hand, and the closed-eyed lion on the face of it looked back down the platform at the Gurnos II.

Don Juan's Rose Ghost had no plates to fold. The ultra-light frame took him as it stood, with a quick, dry clicking of joints, the way a folded metal spider might extend.

Valentyna moved. The plates of the modified Wrath III came down around her, and the permafrost jade at the spinal coupling broke into a fine powder as it took her weight. The Yenisai Princess's red-quicksilver core, set in the chest of the suit, beat once, hard, and the energy pulse that came off it was twice the size of the pulse from a standard core.

"Go to Belle," Cesare said, to Licinius. "Get her out of the ring."

Licinius nodded. He took the black-cross honeycomb handcuff-gun from the small of his back, and he and Taraxia went flat against the edge of the platform, working their way around the lip of it toward the cross.

"And us?" Don Juan asked.

"You take the Gurnos II's auxiliaries," Cesare said. "When they come out."

"Auxiliaries?" Alfonso said.

He had not finished the word when the sound of boots on stone came out of the three mine entrances at the edge of the platform. They were not human boots. They were the sound of a great deal of metal being moved very quickly.

Three of them.

The first-generation Prometheus mass-production suits came out of the mine in a column. They were four metres tall, each of them, plated in matte-black light armour, with the prayers of the World Tree's nervous system cut into the joints. Their fingertips glowed with dark-gold heat-wire. Six-barrel rotary guns were unfolding out of their forearms.

"Now we are talking," Juan said, and his voice came out of the Gurnos II's speaker. "Belle Dantie is the aperitif. These three are the dinner."

The three mass-production Prometheuses came up to the platform in a line. The six-barrels of all three began to turn. The sound of the barrels, and the deeper sound of the Tyrannosaurus core in the Gurnos II, went through the stone under Cesare's feet and made the platform shake.

"Don Juan. Quintilian. Alfonso," Cesare said.

"Here."

"The three are yours."

"Understood."

The three trial-type Seraphim suits went forward at the same time.

Quintilian's Augustus was first into them. The five-layered mithril great shield came up in front of him, and the first Prometheus put all six of its barrels into that shield, and the bullets came down on the face of it in a long unbroken metallic hammering. The shield did not move. The closed-eyed lion on the front of it did not blink. The shadow-metal and hard-gold in the laminations of the shield caught the fire of the impacts and threw it back as a dull blue shine.

"Come on, then," Quintilian said, under his breath.

Alfonso, behind him, did not move. He had a long-barrelled sniper's gun on his shoulder, the barrel of it twice as thick as a normal rifle's, and the muzzle of it was the dark red of a brute-force Thunderbolt Fang. The quicksilver load in the bullet was three times the standard, and the timing of the detonation was being run from a tiny steam-valve set into the breech of the thing.

He was waiting.

Don Juan's Rose Ghost went out of the vapour like a breath.

The weight of the ultra-light frame was a third of the Augustus's; the articulation of it was twice the Augustus's, and in the thick rolling red air of the platform the suit was almost invisible. He came around behind the first Prometheus, and the place he came to was the place the production suits were weakest — the seam where the chest-core fed the arms. The energy conduits of the suit lay along that seam, exposed between the plates, like a row of dark-red veins.

Don Juan drew the Green Snake sword.

The blade of it was long and narrow and curved like the body of a snake, and the old green patina of the copper still clung to the metal. It was one of the seven named swords of the da Vinci inheritance, made of the same stuff as the first Seraphim weapons, and it had been waiting for the hand it was made for.

He cut.

The Green Snake took the right-arm conduit of the first Prometheus in a single clean stroke from behind. The conduit parted. A jet of high-pressure steam went out of the broken end. The right arm of the Prometheus jerked, and the six-barrel on it went quiet.

He did not stop. He took the recoil of his own cut and used it to turn himself in the air; he came down on the shoulder-plate of the Prometheus; his second stroke took the left-arm conduit. The left arm went slack, and the Prometheus, with both arms out of action, came down on the stone with a long clatter of metal on rock.

"One down," Don Juan said, in the comms.

"Clean," Alfonso said.

His rifle fired.

The brute-force Thunderbolt Fang went through the chest-plate of the second Prometheus. The bullet went into the core, and the quicksilver in the core lit the energy cycle of the core from the inside. In three seconds, the chest of the Prometheus was an orange ball of fire.

"Two," Alfonso said.

The third Prometheus tried to turn its guns on Don Juan and Alfonso. Quintilian was already there. The mithril shield of the Augustus went flat into the chest-plate of the Prometheus. The five layers of the shield gave, for a single instant, by a few millimetres — the permafrost jade in the lamination cooling the metal and letting it contract for the second part of the buffer — and then the force of the blow went on through, and the Prometheus went backwards on its heels.

"Move," said Quintilian.

Don Juan was over Quintilian's shoulder in a single step. The Green Snake went in through the seam of the third Prometheus's face-plate, and the point of it found the cockpit, and went through. There was the sound of metal parting, and the sound of steam, and a man's voice, cut short. The third Prometheus went down slowly, the way a tree goes down.

"Platform is clear," Quintilian said.

But the Gurnos II had already moved.

Juan had given them no time to breathe.

The Gurnos II took a step forward, and the platform shook under it. The prototype was more than twice the size of a production Prometheus, and each of its steps put a web of cracks into the stone. The great recurved saw-tooth sword came round from the side, and the teeth of it screamed in the air, like a beast with a great mouth that was learning to roar.

"Move!"

Valentyna's modified Wrath III went up into the vapour. The permafrost-ground axe of the Yenisai came down out of the air and met the great sword in the middle. The shockwave of the impact blew the red quicksilver vapour out of a ten-metre circle around them.

Valentyna went backwards. The Wrath III slid on the stone for five or six metres before it stopped. The permafrost jade in the joints cracked a second time.

"He is heavy," she said.

"Out of the way, Your Highness," Cesare said.

His voice was level.

Valentyna did not argue. She took the Wrath III to the edge of the platform and gave Cesare the middle of the floor.

There was no one on the platform now but Cesare and the Gurnos II.

The heat of the pit rose up between them and made long shadows of both of them on the stone, and the two shadows met and crossed each other in the red light, the way the shadows of two giants about to fight might cross.

The New Red Dragon suit was standing at the lip of the platform.

It was the reinforced Seraphim frame that the Minerva Bureau had built for Cesare, retaining the heavy-armed and the sword-dancer modes, and every weapon system in it had been strengthened. The suit stood in the vapour without moving. Across its chest the dark-red channels of its energy system pulsed like a slow second heart. On the left shoulder-plate, two characters in the eastern script had been engraved, and they were the two characters for *Red Dragon*.

Cesare walked to the suit.

His walk was unhurried, and each step was steady. He put a hand on the chest-plate. The moment his fingers touched the metal, the golden cannula in his neck gave a sharp surge of heat, and his hand flinched, once, before he steadied it.

The neural coupling of the suit came up.

The plates of the heavy-armed mode folded out to either side, and the cockpit was open, and there was a faint gold light inside it, and the light fell on Cesare's white face. His purple eyes caught that light, and for a moment the eyes looked like two pieces of obsidian wrapped in a pale gold flame.

He stepped in. The plates closed. The coupling-needles went into his spine.

The neural coupling of the New Red Dragon and the golden cannula in Cesare's neck were made for each other, and in the first instant of the link the coupling rose to ninety-seven per cent. Every plate, every joint, every energy conduit of the suit became a continuation of the body inside it, the way a hand is a continuation of an arm.

He raised his right hand.

The right hand of the New Red Dragon closed into a fist at the same time, and the metal of the fingers clicked, joint by joint.

"Red Dragon," Juan said, and his voice came out of the Gurnos II's speaker, low and patient. "Come on, then. Let us see what the Minerva Bureau has spent on its toy, and whether it is enough to take a third-generation Prometheus."

The Tyrannosaurus core of the Gurnos II roared. The prototype came forward in three long strides, each one of them five metres across, and the great recurved saw-tooth sword came down from above in a dark-red arc, the teeth of it burning in the heat of the air, like a reaper's sickle falling out of the sky.

Cesare lifted the Dragon Fang sword.

The blade of the Dragon Fang was a thing made of two parts joined. The broken end of an old blade had been married to a fragment of the holy sword furniture of Excalibur that Rommel had brought back from the Lotus Operation, and at the joint of the two metals there was a faint white light, as if the two pieces were repelling each other and holding each other at the same time.

The sword met the great blade in the air.

The shockwave of the meeting went out from the point of impact in every direction, and the stone under their feet cracked in a web, and the red vapour of the platform was pushed out in a ring.

The force of the Gurnos II came down the blade of the Dragon Fang and into the arm of the New Red Dragon, and the arm began to go numb. The Tyrannosaurus core of the prototype was giving Juan more power than Cesare had allowed for. The energy in it was snarling, and each beat of it put more weight on Juan's hands.

"Not enough, brother," Juan said, and there was something in his voice that had been held down for years and was now, at last, allowed out. "Is that all you have?"

The great blade came down another inch. The teeth of it ran along the flat of the Dragon Fang with a long, shrill metallic screaming, and the sparks that came off the contact flew out in a small meteor shower.

Cesare took a step back.

"Your sword is shaking," Juan said. "Look. Your whole arm is shaking."

He was right. If the neural-current reader was still running, the readout would have been showing the coupling of the New Red Dragon taking a punishment it had not been designed to take. The force of the Gurnos II was coming through the Dragon Fang, through the suit, and into Cesare's spine, and every second of it was eating the nerve paths in his back.

Cesare did not answer.

His left hand went behind him.

There was a sword at the small of his back. It was not the Green Snake. It was a sword older than the Green Snake. Its blade was plain, with no patina, only a dark grain in the metal. Its grip was wound in faded green silk. At the guard, almost too worn to read, was the badge of the Borgia house.

The First Broken Sword. The sword of Gonzalo Borgia, the first of the Broken-Sword Knights, three hundred years dead. The sword that Liansheng had taken from the da Vinci storehouse and put into Cesare's hand. The sword that could cut through anything the mechanical theocracies had ever made, the Omega prototypes included.

Cesare did not draw the sword.

Not yet.

Instead, his left thumb found a hidden stud on the left shoulder-plate of the New Red Dragon, and pressed it.

The auxiliary jets in the shoulders of the suit opened. A blast of high-pressure steam came out of them, dyed gold-red by the light of the pit, and fanned out behind Cesare in two wide wings of light. The high-pressure curtain of vapour stood between Cesare and the great blade and took some of the weight of it off the Dragon Fang.

He used the moment. He stepped back. The distance between him and the Gurnos II opened by three paces.

"Running?" Juan said, and came after him.

The Gurnos II was faster than Cesare had thought. The legs of the prototype had been re-worked; the reach of each stride was more than five metres, and in three strides the Gurnos II was on top of him. The great blade came down again, and this time Juan was putting everything he had into it. The Tyrannosaurus core bled its full output into the arm, and the teeth of the blade caught fire in the air, and the blade came down wrapped in a sheet of orange flame.

Cesare put up the Dragon Fang to meet it.

The two weapons met a second time.

The force of the Gurnos II was twice what it had been.

Cesare's knees bent. The knee-joint of the New Red Dragon gave out a long, strained metallic groan, and the stone of the platform under his feet gave way into two pits. His hand slipped on the grip of the Dragon Fang, and the white glove over the knuckle of his thumb tore, and the white of it went red.

"Kneel," Juan said.

His voice was no longer angry. It was the voice of a man who has, at last, got what he wanted.

"Kneel, Cesare. Kneel to me. Admit that you are not my equal. Admit that you are a bastard, a tool my father picked up, a thing that should have rotted in a Florence gutter."

The great blade came down another inch.

The vertebrae of Cesare's spine began to make small sounds inside the coupling, under the load the Gurnos II was putting on them. The world at the edges of his sight was beginning to go soft, the way a picture goes soft when the glass in front of it is heated. The red vapour and the orange of the pit had begun to run together into one colour.

But his purple eyes did not change.

They did not go the colour of fire. They did not show the lines of gold that meant the Immortal King system was coming up. The golden cannula at the back of his neck was burning, but it had not yet reached the threshold.

He was still holding.

"I will not kneel," Cesare said.

His voice was quiet. The sound of the great blade and the sound of the suit together almost buried it. But Juan heard him.

"What did you say?"

"I said," Cesare said, and his purple eyes took the fire of the great blade into themselves, "I will not kneel."

The broken end of the Dragon Fang — the part that held the Excalibur fragment — was put, with a precision that did not belong to a man who was losing, into the gap between two teeth of the great blade.

The white light at the joint of the two metals flared.

The repulsion of the two metals — the broken blade and the Excalibur shard — went off the joint in a single bright pulse, and the pulse ran down the great blade along the teeth, and where it passed, the metal of the teeth cracked, in fine bright lines, like the lines on a piece of porcelain that has been struck.

Juan's face changed.

"What is —"

He did not finish.

The pulse had shaken the great blade off the Dragon Fang, and in the moment the blade was loose, Cesare took the New Red Dragon three steps back.

But the Gurnos II was faster than the eye. The Omega self-healing nerve-fibre had read Juan's intent before Juan had time to think it, and the prototype was already coming after him, and the great blade came round from the side, low this time, and the teeth of it caught the New Red Dragon on the right shoulder-plate.

It was not a square hit. It was a graze. But the teeth of the great blade were sharp enough, even at a graze, to put a cut into the shoulder-plate that went almost to the metal of the joint inside. The plates at the edge of the cut peeled back, and a handful of the fine coupling conduits inside were cut through, and the broken ends of them spat small electric arcs.

The right shoulder of the New Red Dragon stopped obeying him. Three of the actuators in the joint went out, and the reach of the right arm fell to forty per cent of what it had been.

Cesare took the suit back. He stood with the Dragon Fang in his right hand, the right arm hanging lower than it should, the great blade of the Gurnos II coming up to take aim at him again.

"Brother," Juan said. "Your suit is broken. Are you going to keep going?"

The Gurnos II lifted the great blade.

The posture was different this time. The blade did not come down from above, and it did not swing from the side. It came up level, the point of it at the height of the cockpit of the New Red Dragon. A thrust, made to go through the cockpit in a single blow.

Cesare's purple eyes fixed on the point of the blade that was coming at him.

The heat of the air was warping the line of the great blade, and the red vapour around it had wrapped it in a faint orange halo. The teeth of the blade were burning in the heat of the chamber, and the burning had given the blade the look of a thing out of the pit of the world.

He lifted the Dragon Fang to meet it.

But the right shoulder of the New Red Dragon had slowed the movement by half a beat.

The great blade came through the guard of the Dragon Fang, and the point of it came on, straight at the cockpit. The point of the blade was a metre from the cockpit wall.

Half a metre.

Thirty centimetres.

In the shadow of the great blade, Cesare's purple eyes lit up.

Not purple.

Gold, and red through the gold. Like a piece of dark stone that has been put into a fire. Like the first thin line of light that the sun puts on the eastern horizon, in the minute before the sun is up.

The golden cannula at the nape of his neck began to burn.

The Immortal King system was coming up.

第253章 不朽之王的觉醒

【中文】
第253章 不朽之王的觉醒

后颈的黄金套管烫得像要烙穿皮肤。

西泽尔能感觉到芯片里超载的微电路正在一点一点苏醒——像冰层下的河水解冻，像冬眠的兽睁开眼。不朽之王系统正以他的神经为通路，一寸一寸爬进他的脊椎。

巨刃的锯齿距离骑士舱不到二十厘米。

他举起龙牙剑。

不是格挡。是刺。

龙牙剑的断茬在巨刃的阴影中划出一道银弧，穿过锯齿间的缝隙，刺向巨刃与机械臂的连接关节——整条巨刃最薄弱的位置。

"叮"的一声脆响，断茬嵌进关节的缝隙，擦出一蓬火花，但没刺穿。那是第三代高阶合金，厚度超过了龙牙剑的极限。

但这一剑让胡安被迫收回了巨刃。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ后退了一步，银白面具下的眼睛里闪过一丝意外。

"红——"

胡安没有说完这个词。

因为新红龙甲胄变了。

那些被切断的线路、断口飞溅的电火花、翻卷的装甲板——它们没有继续恶化。切口边缘浮现出一层极淡的暗红色纹路，像血管，像根须，从断口蔓延开来，将整台甲胄包裹。

蒸汽喷口不再是白色。

是暗红色。

新红龙甲胄的每一处排气口都喷出暗红色的蒸汽，温度高到在熔岩之心橘红色的光芒中像一层燃烧的薄纱。不朽之王系统彻底启动了。

西泽尔后颈的黄金套管已经烫得发红。

芯片里那些微电路全部点亮，神经接驳度从百分之六十七直线上跳。百分之八十。百分之九十。百分之九十五。

百分之一百。

完美耦合。

他感觉到自己的意识和新红龙甲胄完全融为一体。不是"操控"甲胄——是"变成"了甲胄。每一块装甲板是他的皮肤，每一根动力管道是他的血管，每一个电机是他的关节。

他还保留着自我。他知道自己是谁。

但同时，他能感觉到意识深处另一种东西正在苏醒——疯狂的，毁灭的，只想着杀戮的。不朽之王系统正用芯片压制着那股力量，可芯片的负荷已经濒临上限。

三分钟。安全阈值。

超过三分钟芯片就会过载。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ再次扑上来，巨刃从右侧横扫，速度比之前更快。欧米茄自愈神经纤维让胡安的指令传导延迟降到了零——但此刻西泽尔的传导延迟也是零。

他侧身。

巨刃擦着新红龙甲胄的左肩呼啸而过，距离骑士舱只有几厘米。这一次他躲开了。

右肩的损伤不再影响他。不朽之王系统接管了甲胄的次级控制回路，用剩余电机和备用线路重组了右臂的运动系统。右臂依然不灵活，但至少能动了。

"有意思。"胡安说。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的背部四门蒸汽加农炮同时开火。

四道橘红色的火焰从炮口喷涌而出，拖着长长的尾迹，像四头扑向猎物的火龙。整个熔岩之心都被炮口的闪光照亮了，圆形平台的岩壁上投射出四条交叉的火焰影子。

新红龙甲胄不退反进。

西泽尔从爆炸的间隙中穿过——那种闪避不是靠眼睛观察，是不朽之王系统通过神经接驳直接将火焰轨迹投射进他的意识。他"看见"了每一发炮弹的弹道，知道间隙在哪里，知道该从哪条缝隙穿过去。

四发炮弹全在他身后爆炸。

冲击波追着他的背影，热浪几乎把他按在地上。甲胄的警报系统疯狂鸣响，背部装甲板的红外温度指示器已经烧红——那块区域的温度超过了八百度。

但他没有停下。

新红龙甲胄冲到古洛诺斯Ⅱ面前，距离不到三米。这是巨型机动傀儡最不擅长的距离——巨刃太长，反而成了累赘。

西泽尔举起了龙牙剑。

但他没有立刻刺出。

他另一只手从腰后拔出了暴力增强型雷霆牙。

那是阿方索尼心为他改造的自杀式武器——三倍红水银注入量，五秒延时，三秒内铳身解体爆炸。他将雷霆牙的枪口对准了古洛诺斯Ⅱ的骑士舱外装甲板。

胡安的目光凝固了。

"你疯了！"他尖声说。

西泽尔扣下扳机。

铳口喷出将近两米长的暗金色火舌，红水银在高温中汽化，拖着金属质感的尾迹，像一条贴着地面飞行的金色巨蟒。这不是普通火药推动——是浓缩红水银直接在铳膛内爆燃，温度超过两千度，足够熔化影金属。

火舌撞上古洛诺斯Ⅱ的胸甲外板。

高阶合金的表面迅速变红，然后开始软化。两千度的红水银火焰持续灼烧着同一个点，哪怕有欧米茄自愈神经纤维修复，修复速度也赶不上熔化速度。

胡安被迫后退。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的巨刃从上方向下劈来——这是最直接的反制，用巨刃的重量和速度碾碎那支正在喷射火焰的武器。但西泽尔已经计算好了时机。

三秒。雷霆牙的延时还剩三秒。

他松开扳机。

雷霆牙的铳身开始发出不祥的嘎吱声，红水银蒸汽从每一条缝隙中喷涌而出，铳管已经热得发白。他没有丢弃它——他将这枚随时会爆炸的武器塞进了古洛诺斯Ⅱ右腿膝关节的缝隙里。

膝关节是巨刃挥动时受力最集中的位置之一，关节的活动让缝隙张开了几厘米。

足够了。

西泽尔同时后撤，举起龙牙剑。

龙牙剑的断茬——那截在红龙甲胄胸口镶嵌了整整一年的圣剑装具·Excalibur碎片——在熔岩之心的橘红色光芒中开始发亮。不是反射光，是它自己在发光，发出冰冷的银白色光。

圣剑碎片能刺穿任何机械神国造物的心脏。

龙德施泰特用生命换来的情报。

"爆。"

雷霆牙在古洛诺斯Ⅱ的膝关节内爆炸。

三倍红水银注入量的爆炸将膝关节彻底撕开。冲击波把附近三米的岩石地面震成碎屑，连圆形平台的岩壁都裂开了几条缝。暗红色火球腾空而起，映红了整个熔岩之心。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的右腿向内折断。

七米高的巨型机动傀儡失去平衡，巨刃擦着新红龙甲胄的头顶掠过——西泽尔已经侧身，巨刃的刃尖在距离他三米的地方砸进地面，将岩石劈开一道三米长的深沟。

巨型机动傀儡开始向左侧倾倒。

西泽尔等的就是这一刻。

他冲上去。

新红龙甲胄的背部蒸汽喷射口全部打开，暗红色的火焰从背后喷涌，推动他如同一枚暗金色的炮弹射向倾倒的古洛诺斯Ⅱ。龙牙剑的断茬刺入了骑士舱外装甲板——那片被雷霆牙烧软了的高阶合金。

圣剑碎片发挥出它的特性。

那道冰冷的银白色光芒从断茬尖端蔓延开来，沿着切口向内延伸，所到之处高阶合金的分子结构被直接破坏——不是切割，是分解。装甲板像是被某种无形的酸液侵蚀，几秒钟的时间就裂开了一个直径一米的洞。

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的骑士舱暴露在空气中。

西泽尔看见了胡安。

十五岁的少年坐在驾驶座上，银白色短发被汗水打湿贴在额头。他的眼睛死死盯着显示器——那些显示甲胄状态的仪表正在一个个变成红色。他的双手紧紧握着操纵杆，指节发白。

"不……"胡安喃喃。

他的左手疯狂拍向紧急弹射按钮——

但西泽尔的动作更快。

龙牙剑从洞口刺入，穿过骑士舱的间隙，刃尖停在胡安的胸口前方三厘米处。圣剑碎片的银白光芒照在胡安的脸上，将他的表情映得清清楚楚。

那是恐惧。

那是不甘。

那是某种更深的东西。

胡安低头看着自己胸口前那柄散发银白光芒的剑尖，嘴唇动了动。然后他抬起头，看着骑士舱外的西泽尔——新红龙甲胄的面甲已经升起，露出了西泽尔的脸。

苍白，冷静，紫瞳中金红色的纹路正缓缓流动。

"你不会杀我。"胡安说。

西泽尔没有回答。

"你不会杀我，"胡安又说了一遍，声音在发抖，"我是你弟弟。"

"是。"

西泽尔的声音很平静。

"但你驾驶这台甲胄要杀我，要杀我的人。"

他的右手握住龙牙剑的柄，左手抬起，按在了古洛诺斯Ⅱ的骑士舱边缘。

"下去。"

胡安盯着他，盯着那柄距离自己胸口三厘米的圣剑。银白光芒在胡安的脸上晃动，将他银白色的短发染成霜色。

"我不下去。"胡安说，"这台甲胄还没输。"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的左臂忽然动了。

左臂上搭载的副武器——一把蒸汽连射铳——从侧面转向新红龙甲胄的骑士舱。

西泽尔将头偏了半寸。

连射铳开火。

密集的弹丸擦着新红龙甲胄的骑士舱边缘飞过，有几发打在了肩甲上，金属碰撞的声音在熔岩之心里回响。有一发弹丸几乎是贴着西泽尔的耳朵飞过去的，热浪灼痛了他的耳廓。

西泽尔将龙牙剑向前推了半寸。

圣剑碎片的银白光芒触到了胡安军服的衣领。

胡安能感觉到那种光芒里蕴含的力量——那不是温度，是某种更深层的东西，像是有什么力量正在试图穿透他的身体，将他体内的金属结构全部烧毁。

那是欧米茄自愈神经纤维的克星。

胡安的左肩传来一阵剧痛——他植入体内的欧米茄自愈神经纤维开始剧烈痉挛，红水银核心的跳动变得混乱。古洛诺斯Ⅱ的左臂猛地抽搐了一下，蒸汽连射铳的弹道偏了。

"……哥哥。"胡安的声音变了。

不再是十五岁少年赌气时的那种尖声，是另一种声音，更低沉，更疲惫。

"你赢了。"

"认输？"西泽尔问。

"不，"胡安抬起头，眼睛在银白面具下闪着某种奇异的光，"但我输了。"

他伸手抓住了白银面具的边缘。

西泽尔皱眉。

"不要——"

胡安用力一扯。

白银面具的右侧被他扯了下来。

面具下不是脸。

是机械。

胡安右半边脸从颧骨开始就是金属结构，精密的青铜齿轮嵌在血肉中，下颌是一整块精密的机械假肢，颈部暴露在外的不是皮肤和血管——是分段式机械关节，每一节都刻着微型梵文。

但左半边脸还是血肉。

十五岁少年的左半边脸——一只棕色的眼睛，半个鼻子，半张嘴，皮肤细腻到几乎透明，下颌线条柔和，还带着属于少年的稚嫩。

一半血肉，一半机械。

"你……"西泽尔的声音发紧。

"他给我看了未来的样子，"胡安说，声音发颤，"他说……他说这是进化的方向……"

"闭嘴。"

"不，我说完。"胡安的独眼死死盯着西泽尔，"白银面具下的人……三百年来从未老去……他是……一切的源头……"

他的声音越来越轻。

"……哥哥，他和你长得很像……"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的红水银核心忽然发出一声巨响。

那声巨响从核心深处传来，像是什么东西爆炸了。巨型机动傀儡的动力系统开始崩溃——左肩关节冒出一股黑烟，然后是右肩，然后是胸腔。连锁反应。

"……走！"西泽尔猛地抽回龙牙剑。

但胡安的手抓住了龙牙剑的剑身。

圣剑碎片灼烧着他的掌心，将血肉烧成焦炭。胡安的脸扭曲了，但他没有松手。

"别……"胡安说，"别管我……我跑不掉了……"

"放手！"

"不！"

胡安的独眼里流出泪水。

"哥哥，我讨厌你，从你一出现我就讨厌你，但我从来没想过要你死。"他的声音断断续续，"是……是他让我这么做的……他说你是他最大的威胁……"

"谁？"

"他……"胡安的声音更轻了，"他说他叫……"

古洛诺斯Ⅱ的红水银核心爆炸了。

那声爆炸将整个熔岩之心震得摇晃起来，圆形平台的岩壁上出现了更多裂缝，岩石碎屑从穹顶落下。巨大的火球从古洛诺斯Ⅱ的胸腔中喷涌而出，将西泽尔的视野完全吞没。

新红龙甲胄被冲击波推出十几米远，重重撞在了圆形平台的岩壁上。

西泽尔的意识在那一刻变得模糊。

他隐约看见一个身影被火球吞噬——银白色的短发在火焰中飘散，独眼里最后的光芒被暗红色的火海吞没。

那张半边血肉半边机械的脸最后看了他一眼。

然后消失在了火海中。

"胡安！"

西泽尔的声音被爆炸声淹没。

火焰持续了将近一分钟。

当火焰终于散去，古洛诺斯Ⅱ已经变成了熔岩之心地面上的一堆焦黑残骸。巨型机动傀儡的残骸还在燃烧，暗红色的火焰在残骸中跳动，红水银蒸汽从残骸中升起，弥漫在空气中。

不朽之王系统的安全阈值已经到达。

西泽尔感觉到意识深处那种疯狂的、毁灭的冲动正在冲击芯片的控制。他用力闭了闭眼，将那股冲动压下去。芯片的温度已经到了极限，再过几秒就会过载。

"关闭。"西泽尔低声说。

芯片关闭了。

新红龙甲胄表面的暗红色纹路开始消退，蒸汽喷口从暗红色变回了白色。神经接驳度从百分之一百快速下降，百分之八十，百分之六十，百分之四十，最后稳定在百分之五十二。

西泽尔的全身都在发抖。

他低头看着自己握剑的手——那只手在剧烈颤抖，几乎握不住剑柄。不朽之王系统的反噬正在通过神经接驳传回他的身体。

"西泽尔！"

唐璜的声音从不远处传来。

圆形平台的另一侧，唐璜、昆提良、阿方索三人的甲胄静静停着。地面上散落着大量机械残骸——那是古洛诺斯Ⅱ的附属机械兵，被他们三人全部清除了。蔷薇之鬼的刀刃上还挂着一只机械兵的手臂，所罗门王的炮管还在冒烟，奥古斯都的秘银重盾上多了几道新划痕，闭眼狮头纹章的狮眼被划开了。

"碧儿！"阿方索第一个冲向十字架。

李锡尼和塔拉夏已经把碧儿·丹缇从十字架上解救下来。碧儿的脸色苍白，嘴唇干裂，但她的眼睛还是亮的。她看见西泽尔走来，立刻挣开李锡尼的手，踉跄着跑向他。

"少爷！"碧儿喘着气说，"阿黛尔——阿黛尔还在里面——"

她指向圆形平台深处的一扇巨大的黑铁门。

那扇门在熔岩之心的尽头，岩壁的最深处，被一层暗红色的光晕笼罩着。

"我听到了她的声音，"碧儿的声音带着哭腔，"从那扇门后面……她在唱歌……那首歌是您小时候教她的那首……"

西泽尔的目光落在那扇黑铁巨门上。

门上刻着机械神教的齿轮徽记——齿轮中心嵌着一颗五芒星，五芒星的五个角末端各连接一圈更小的齿轮。

这个徽记他见过。

在琳琅夫人的银莲花项链坠背面。

两个徽记完全一致。

"我母亲……"西泽尔低声说。

他的手下意识地伸向自己的胸口，从衣领下拉出了那枚银莲花项链坠。

项链坠背面的徽记开始发出淡金色的光芒。

那光芒向黑铁巨门蔓延过去。

门上的机械神教齿轮徽记也亮了起来，发出同样的淡金色光芒。两个徽记的光芒在空气中相遇，融合——

"咔嚓"一声轻响。

黑铁巨门中央裂开了一条细缝。

那条细缝向两侧延伸，越来越大，最后整扇门无声地向内退开。

门后是一条通道。

通道的地面铺满六瓣暗金色金属莲花花瓣，两侧墙壁镶嵌着刻有梵文的微型黄铜齿轮。那些齿轮正在缓慢转动，发出细微的嗡鸣声。

一股清冷的香气从门后飘来。

那是金色莲花花瓣的香气。

和阿瓦隆残片完全一致。

和母亲身上的香气完全一致。

西泽尔盯着那条通道，紫瞳中的金红色纹路再次浮现。

"门开了。"他低声说。

【English】
Chapter 253 — The Awakening of the Immortal King

The gold sleeve at the back of his neck was burning.

Not warm. Burning. The kind of heat that lives just past the threshold of flesh's forgiveness, the kind that whispers of brands and penance and the long arm of the divine reaching down through brass and bone. Cesare could feel it against his skin like a coal pressed to the nape of a heretic.

Inside the chip, the overloaded microcircuits were waking.

One by one. Strand by strand. Like a river thawing under spring ice. Like something with too many eyes opening after a long sleep. The Immortal King system was threading itself along his nervous system, vertebra by vertebra, claiming him.

The serrated edge of the giant blade hung less than a hand's breadth from his cockpit.

He raised the Dragon Fang.

He did not block. He thrust.

The broken tip of the sword — a length of Excalibur, the sacred blade, that had lain in the Red Dragon's chest for a year — cut a silver arc through the shadow of the great blade. He did not aim for the steel. He aimed for the joint where the blade met the arm, the place where every giant weapon is weakest, the place where a single bar of alloy has to bear the weight of every stroke.

Clink.

The broken tip caught in the seam of the joint. A handful of sparks flew. But it did not pierce. Third-generation high-grade alloy, thicker than the sword was ever meant to bite.

It did not need to pierce.

The thrust forced Juan to retract.

Gulo Nos II stepped back. Behind the silver mask, the eyes flashed — surprise, quick as a snake's tongue, and gone.

"Red —"

Juan did not finish the word.

Because the New Red Dragon was changing.

The severed cables. The sparks that had been leaping from torn housings. The peeled-back plates of armor. None of it worsened. The cut edges began to glow. A faint dark-red tracery spread from every wound, vein-like, root-like, creeping along the metal until it had wrapped the whole suit of armor as if the armor had been grafted back into the body of something alive.

The steam vents were no longer venting white.

They were venting red.

A dark, arterial red, so hot in the orange light of the Lava Heart that it hung in the air like a sheet of burning gauze. The Immortal King system had finished waking.

The gold sleeve at the back of Cesare's neck had gone from burning to glowing.

Every microcircuit in the chip lit. The neural coupling reading climbed. Eighty percent. Ninety. Ninety-five.

One hundred.

Perfect coupling.

He felt his consciousness and the New Red Dragon fuse. Not piloting. Becoming. Every plate of armor was his skin. Every power conduit his vein. Every actuator his joint.

He was still himself. He knew his own name.

But at the back of his mind, something else was rising. Something feral. Something with a single appetite. Something that knew only the word kill. The chip was holding it down. The chip's load was already clawing at the limit.

Three minutes. The safe threshold.

Past three, the chip would burn out.

Gulo Nos II came at him again. The giant blade swept in from the right, faster than before. The Omega self-healing nerve fibers had collapsed Juan's command latency to zero — but Cesare's was zero too.

He leaned.

The blade screamed past the New Red Dragon's left shoulder, a finger's width from the cockpit. He had read the stroke through the steel before it had begun, had felt it in the way the arm's actuators pre-loaded, had simply leaned the way a man leans away from a falling wall.

The damage to his right arm was no longer a problem. The Immortal King system had taken over the suit's secondary control circuits, rewired the remaining motors and the backup lines, rebuilt the arm's motion system on the fly. The arm was stiff, graceless, but it answered.

"Interesting," Juan said.

Four steam cannons on Gulo Nos II's back opened at once.

Four ribbons of orange flame roared from the muzzles, long-tailed, four dragons of fire lunging for a single prey. The whole of the Lava Heart was lit by the muzzle-flash. Four crossing fire-shadows painted the rock walls of the circular platform.

The New Red Dragon did not retreat. It advanced.

Cesare ran through the gaps between the explosions. It was not evasion by eye. The Immortal King system, through the neural link, was casting the trajectories directly into his mind. He saw each shell's path the way a man sees a road drawn on a map. He saw where the gaps were. He saw which slit between the four streams of fire would close a man safely in.

All four shells burst behind him.

The shockwave caught his back. The heat pressed him down toward the stone as if the air itself had taken a hand to his shoulders. The New Red Dragon's alarms screamed. The infrared temperature gauge on his back plate had gone white — eight hundred degrees and climbing across the whole rear of the suit.

He did not stop.

The New Red Dragon came in to less than three meters from Gulo Nos II. Inside that distance, the giant puppet lost its chief advantage. The blade was too long. It was a hindrance. Cesare had learned that from watching the old footage of the Battle of the Black Coast — the only place any knight of the Order had ever survived a duel with one of the Holy City's war-puppets by getting inside the swing.

He raised the Dragon Fang.

He did not thrust at once.

With his other hand, he drew from the small of his back the Violent-Enhancement Thunderbolt Fang.

Alfonso had built the thing as a suicide weapon. Three times the normal charge of red mercury. A five-second fuse. After three seconds, the gun body would tear itself apart. Cesare leveled the muzzle at the outer armor of Gulo Nos II's cockpit.

Juan's gaze went still.

"You're mad," he said, and his voice was high.

Cesare squeezed the trigger.

A tongue of dark gold fire, nearly two meters long, roared from the muzzle. The red mercury vaporized in the heat, trailing a long metallic tail — a gold serpent flying along the ground, a hand's breadth above the stone. This was not the push of common powder. Concentrated red mercury burned inside the barrel itself, two thousand degrees and more, hot enough to soften shadow-metal.

The flame struck the chest plate of Gulo Nos II.

The surface reddened. Then it began to sag. Two thousand degrees of red mercury flame, held on the same spot, was doing what no blade and no shell could do. Even with the Omega fibers racing to repair, the healing could not keep up with the melting.

Juan was forced back.

Gulo Nos II's great blade came down from above. The most direct counter. The weight and speed of the thing, meant to crush the weapon that was burning into the chest. But Cesare had already counted the time.

Three seconds. The Thunderbolt Fang's fuse had three seconds left.

He let go of the trigger.

The gun body began to groan. Red mercury vapor poured from every seam. The barrel had gone white. He did not throw it away. He stepped forward and jammed the bomb-that-was-still-a-gun into the seam of Gulo Nos II's right knee joint.

The knee was one of the points of greatest stress when the giant blade swung. The motion of the joint had opened the seam a few centimeters. A few centimeters was enough.

Cesare stepped back. He raised the Dragon Fang.

The broken tip — the Excalibur fragment — began to glow in the orange light of the Lava Heart. It was not reflecting. It was emitting. A cold silver-white, the color of a winter moon, the color of bones in deep water.

The fragment could pierce the heart of any construct the Holy City had ever made.

Von Lettow-Vorburg had bought that knowledge with his life.

"Now," Cesare whispered.

The Thunderbolt Fang blew inside the knee.

Three times the red mercury. The joint came apart. The shockwave smashed three meters of stone floor into gravel. Cracks ran up the rock walls of the circular platform. A dark red fireball climbed into the air and painted the ceiling of the Lava Heart the color of old blood.

Gulo Nos II's right leg folded inward.

The seven-meter puppet began to fall. The great blade skimmed the top of the New Red Dragon's head, then drove into the ground three meters from Cesare, splitting the stone into a three-meter furrow.

The puppet was tipping left.

That was the moment he had been waiting for.

He ran at it.

The New Red Dragon's back vents all opened at once. A dark red fire roared from his shoulders and his spine, hurling him forward like a dark gold shell. The Dragon Fang's broken tip met the outer plate of the cockpit — the plate that the Thunderbolt Fang's flame had softened to the color of cooling iron.

The Excalibur fragment did what it did.

A cold silver-white light spilled from the broken tip and ran along the cut, into the metal. The alloy's molecular structure simply fell apart — not cut, not melted, decomposed, as if an invisible acid had been poured into the bone of the metal. In a few seconds the plate had split open into a hole a meter across.

Gulo Nos II's cockpit was bare to the air.

Cesare saw Juan.

A boy of fifteen at the controls. Silver-white hair stuck to his forehead with sweat. His eyes were on the readouts, those little dials that tracked the suit's condition, and one by one they were turning red. His hands gripped the control levers so hard the knuckles had gone bone-white.

"No," Juan whispered.

His left hand flew to the emergency eject —

Cesare was faster.

The Dragon Fang went in through the hole. The tip stopped three centimeters from the boy's chest. The silver-white light of the fragment fell on Juan's face and laid his expression open.

It was fear.

It was rage.

It was something deeper than either.

Juan looked down at the sword tip glowing against his shirt. His lips moved. Then he looked up, past the cockpit edge, at Cesare. The New Red Dragon's faceplate had been raised. Cesare's face was there, in the light.

Pale. Composed. The gold-red traceries in his violet eyes moving like slow lightning.

"You won't kill me," Juan said.

Cesare did not answer.

"You won't kill me," Juan said again, and his voice was shaking. "I'm your brother."

"Yes."

Cesare's voice was even.

"But you are wearing that suit to kill me. And to kill the people who are mine."

His right hand held the sword. His left rose and pressed against the rim of the cockpit.

"Get out."

Juan stared at him. At the blade three centimeters from his chest. The silver light moved over the boy's face, turning his silver hair to frost.

"I won't get out," Juan said. "This suit hasn't lost."

Gulo Nos II's left arm moved.

The auxiliary weapon mounted on it — a steam-fed repeating gun — swung sideways toward the New Red Dragon's cockpit.

Cesare tilted his head half an inch.

The repeating gun fired.

A burst of slugs screamed past the edge of the New Red Dragon's cockpit. A few of them struck the shoulder plate. The metallic clang of the impacts went ringing off the rock walls of the Lava Heart. One slug passed so close to Cesare's ear that the heat of its passage seared the rim of the auricle.

Cesare pushed the Dragon Fang forward another half-inch.

The silver light touched the collar of Juan's uniform.

Juan could feel the force in that light. It was not heat. It was something else, something that reached through cloth and skin toward the metal in his body, that wanted to burn the Omega fibers out of him at the root.

A flare of agony ran through his left shoulder. The Omega fibers inside him began to seize. The red mercury core's rhythm broke. Gulo Nos II's left arm jerked. The repeating gun's stream went wide.

"...brother," Juan said.

Not the sharp voice of a fifteen-year-old in a tantrum. Another voice. Lower. Tired.

"You win."

"Do you yield?" Cesare asked.

"No," Juan said, and looked up. Behind the silver mask his single working eye was lit with a strange, calm light. "But I have lost."

His hand closed on the edge of the silver mask.

Cesare's brow went tight.

"Don't —"

Juan pulled.

The right side of the silver mask came away in his hand.

Beneath the mask was not a face.

It was a machine.

From the cheekbone down, Juan's right side was bronze gearwork embedded in raw flesh. His jaw was a single piece of intricate mechanical prosthesis. The neck that was visible above his collar was not skin and blood. It was segmented metal, joint by joint, each piece etched with tiny Sanskrit.

The left side of his face was still flesh.

A fifteen-year-old's left side. One brown eye. Half a nose. Half a mouth. Skin so fine it was almost transparent. The soft line of a jaw still carrying the last roundness of boyhood.

Half flesh. Half machine.

"You —" Cesare's voice tightened.

"He showed me what was coming," Juan said, and his voice shook. "He said — this was the direction of evolution —"

"Be quiet."

"No. I have to finish." Juan's single eye fixed on Cesare. "The man under the silver mask. He has not aged in three hundred years. He is — the source of everything —"

His voice thinned.

"...brother. He looks very much like you."

Gulo Nos II's red mercury core made a sound.

A deep, interior sound, as if something inside it had broken. The puppet's power system began to come apart. Smoke from the left shoulder joint. Then the right. Then the chest. A chain reaction running through the body of the machine.

"— go!" Cesare wrenched the Dragon Fang back.

But Juan's hand had closed on the blade.

The Excalibur fragment was searing his palm, burning flesh to char. Juan's face contorted. He did not let go.

"Don't —" he said. "Don't bother — about me — I can't get clear —"

"LET GO."

"No."

Tears ran from the boy's single eye.

"Brother. I have hated you since the day you appeared. I have hated you. But I never wanted you dead." His voice was breaking. "It was — he made me — he said you were the greatest threat to him —"

"Who?"

"He —" Juan's voice was almost gone. "He said his name was —"

Gulo Nos II's red mercury core exploded.

The blast shook the whole of the Lava Heart. More cracks split the rock walls. Stones came loose from the ceiling and fell. A huge fireball burst from the chest of the puppet and swallowed Cesare's sight.

The New Red Dragon was hurled backward, fifteen meters, and struck the rock wall of the platform with a sound like the tolling of a cathedral bell.

For a moment Cesare's mind went grey.

Through the smoke he thought he saw a figure taken by the fire. Silver-white hair drifting upward in the heat. The last light in a single eye drowned in a sea of dark red.

That half-face — half flesh, half machine — looked at him once.

And then was gone.

"JUAN!"

His voice was lost in the explosion.

The fire went on for nearly a minute.

When the flames at last thinned, Gulo Nos II was a heap of blackened wreckage on the floor of the Lava Heart. The remains of the great puppet were still burning. A dark red fire jumped among the broken girders. Red mercury vapor rose from the ruin and drifted through the air, slow, hanging.

The Immortal King system's safe threshold had passed.

Cesare felt the feral thing at the back of his mind slam against the chip's walls. He closed his eyes. He pressed it down. The chip was at the edge of its heat. A few more seconds and it would burn out.

"Shut down," Cesare said, low.

The chip shut down.

The dark red traceries on the New Red Dragon's skin began to fade. The steam vents went from red back to white. The neural coupling reading fell — one hundred, eighty, sixty, forty — and settled at fifty-two.

Cesare's whole body was shaking.

He looked down at the hand that held the sword. It was shaking so badly the pommel jumped in his grip. The backwash of the Immortal King system was pouring back along the nerve link into his flesh.

"Cesare!"

Don Juan's voice came from across the platform.

On the other side of the circle, the three suits — Don Juan, Quintilian, Alfonso — stood still. The floor between them was littered with the broken parts of Gulo Nos II's auxiliary constructs, every one of them destroyed. The blade of the Rose of Battle still had a mechanical arm hanging from it. The barrels of Solomon's Throne were still smoking. The mithril great-shield of Augustus had fresh scoring across its face; the closed-eyed lion of the heraldry had been scored open across one eye.

"Bianca!" Alfonso was the first to reach the cross.

Licinius and Tarashea had already cut Bianca d'Ante down. Bianca's face was white. Her lips were cracked. But her eyes were bright. The moment she saw Cesare she pulled free of Licinius and staggered toward him.

"My lord!" she gasped. "Adele — Adele is still inside —"

She pointed toward the deep end of the circular platform.

There, in the farthest wall of the Lava Heart, a great door of black iron stood set into the rock. A halo of dark red light hung around it.

"I heard her voice," Bianca said, and her voice was on the edge of tears. "From behind that door. She was singing. The song you taught her, when she was small —"

Cesare's eyes went to the black iron door.

The door was carved with the cogwheel seal of the Church of the Machine God. The seal's central gear held a five-pointed star; from the points of the star, smaller gears hung in rings.

He had seen that seal before.

On the back of Lady Linlang's silver lotus pendant.

The two seals were identical.

"My mother," Cesare said, low.

His hand went to his own chest. From under the collar of his uniform he drew the silver lotus pendant.

The seal on the back of the pendant began to glow a pale gold.

The light crept across the air toward the black iron door.

The cogwheel seal on the door lit. The same pale gold. The two seals' lights met in the air between them, and joined.

A soft click.

Down the center of the black iron door, a hairline crack appeared. The crack grew, spreading left and right, until the whole of the door was sliding open into the rock, silent, with the weight of a thing that had waited a long time to move.

Beyond the door was a passage.

The floor of the passage was paved with dark gold six-petaled metal lotus blossoms. The walls were inset with small brass gears carved with Sanskrit. The gears were turning, slowly, with a thin hum that was almost a sound and almost a thought.

A cool scent came through the door.

The scent of golden lotus petals.

The same scent as the Avalon fragment.

The same scent his mother had carried.

Cesare stared down the passage. The gold-red traceries in his violet eyes had begun to move again.

"The door is open," he said.

【中文】
第254章 原罪机关的主人

西泽尔踏出第一步时，脚下传来金属花瓣清脆的碰响。

那些暗金色的六瓣莲花不是嵌在地面上的装饰，而是真正铸出来的金属瓣，每一片都打磨得温润如水，边缘有极细的齿轮纹路，触感冰凉却带着微微的温度——那是红水银在金属内部流动时散发的热。

"这是达·芬奇叔叔手稿里提到的通道。"薇若兰低声说，声音里带着压抑不住的震惊，"世界树根须的延伸通道……我以为只是传说。"

通道两侧的墙壁上，黄铜微型齿轮正缓缓转动，发出极轻的嗡鸣。齿轮表面刻着梵文，那些文字西泽尔看不懂，但每一个字符都像是活的，齿轮转动时文字似乎在微微蠕动。

通道里弥漫着金色莲花的香气，浓得像一堵墙。

通道不长，大约三十步就到了尽头。

尽头的空间豁然开阔。

那是一个圆形的石室，穹顶极高，嵌满了数以万计的微型齿轮，那些齿轮缓慢转动着，像一片倒悬的金属星空。石室中央矗立着一台巨大的机械装置——黑铁骨架，黄铜齿轮，暗金色的管道从四面八方汇聚到这台机器上，机器中央是一根垂直的金属柱。

柱子上锁着一个人。

阿黛尔。

她被固定在那根金属柱上，双臂被黄铜环箍吊着，头低垂，浅色的长发散落遮住了半张脸。她的胸口贴着一块巴掌大的金属板，金属板上刻着齿轮嵌五芒星的徽记，正发着微弱的暗红色光芒。

"阿黛尔！"碧儿失声喊出来。

金属柱上的人动了一下，长发下的脸缓缓抬起。阿黛尔睁开眼，那双眼睛是清醒的，瞳孔里映着西泽尔的身影，嘴唇动了动。

"哥……"她的声音沙哑，像是很久没有喝过水，"别……别过来……"

西泽尔的脚步顿住了。

不是因为阿黛尔的话。

而是因为他看见了那台机器后面站着的人。

那人穿着一身深红色的长袍，长袍下摆拖在地上，长袍胸口绣着银色猫头鹰和五芒星交叠的徽记——既不是弥赛亚圣教的卡巴拉之树，也不是密涅瓦机关的六翼猫头鹰，而是一种西泽尔从未见过的图案：齿轮中心嵌着一颗五芒星，五芒星五个角末端各连着一圈更小的齿轮。

是机械神教的徽记。

达·芬奇版本的机械神教徽记。

那人的脸被一张白银面具遮住，面具造型简洁，只露出两只眼孔，眼孔中透出暗淡的暗金色光芒。

"欢迎来到熔岩之心最深处，红龙。"那人缓缓开口，声音像是精密齿轮咬合般清晰，没有一丝人类情绪的起伏，"我等你很久了。"

西泽尔盯着那张白银面具，没有说话。

"三百年，"那人继续说，"准确地说，三百一十七年。我等的就是你。"

他抬起右手，金属关节在空气中发出细微的咯吱声，缓缓摘下了那张白银面具。

面具落下。

露出的不是一张脸。

是一张脸和一部机械的结合体。

面具后面，那张脸只有右边一小半还是人类的皮肤，皮肤苍白干枯，贴在金属颚骨上。右眼眶里嵌着一颗暗红色的光学镜头，镜头中央有红光在微微跳动，像是一颗机械的心脏。右半边嘴角的肉已经风干，贴在金属颚骨上，像是干涸的皮革。

左半边脸完全是金属的。金属表面刻着极细的梵文纹路，金属的下颌关节处露出发条和齿轮，每一次开合都发出轻微的咔嗒声。

他不仅脸是这样。

他缓慢地转了转身，长袍下摆扫过石室地面。

长袍下面，他的身体有百分之八十以上都是机械。暗金色的金属骨架从肩膀延伸到指尖，每一根手指都是分节式的金属关节，关节处刻着微型梵文。胸腔的金属板微微起伏，板缝间透出暗红色的光——那是红水银核心在运转。长袍下摆的阴影里，两条腿是纯金属的液压结构，膝盖处有蒸汽管路连接，每走一步都发出低沉的嘶嘶声。

"惊讶吗？"那人——或者说那具人形的机械——嘴角那块干皮微微扯动，算是一个笑容，"三百一十七年的机械改造，每一年都要更换一部分血肉，用红水银核心驱动的金属骨骼替代。这不是痛苦，这是进化。"

他抬起右手——那只纯金属的手——指尖在空气中轻轻敲了敲，敲出了清脆的金属声。

"我是莱昂纳多·博尔吉亚，"他说，"初代教皇波吉亚一世的直系后裔。"

他停顿了一下，金属手指指了指自己机械的胸腔。

"三百一十七年前，我的曾祖找到了阿瓦隆冰原上的世界树残枝。他带回了一样东西，也带回了一个真相。"

"这个世界，"莱昂纳多的暗红镜头微微转动，扫过西泽尔、阿方索、唐璜、昆提良、薇若兰的脸，"从来就不是神创造的。"

"它是被'造物主'制造的。"

"'造物主'留下了一棵世界树，世界树是整个机械文明的能源核心。它产生红水银，红水银驱动所有的机动甲胄、所有的蒸汽机、所有的普罗米修斯和炽天使。弥赛亚圣教说的神创论，是谎言。教廷展示的卡巴拉之树，只是世界树最不起眼的一根须根。"

他抬起金属手指，指向身后那台锁着阿黛尔的机器。

"这台机器的背后，是世界树残枝在西方分支的核心。999架欧米茄原型体在等我的命令。只等我的手指按下这个按钮——"他指向机器上一个拳头大小的红色按钮，"整个翡冷翠，整个教皇国，整个西方世界，都会在一夜之间回到神的怀抱。"

"新神国。"

他慢慢转过头，暗红镜头死死盯着西泽尔。

"我培养了你三百年。从你的曾外祖母那一代开始，从锡兰星见家族的最后一位直系血裔开始。我等的就是你身上流淌的两种血——锡兰星见的紫瞳血，和博尔吉亚家的机械适配血。"

"你是唯一的完美神使载体。"

"我让你来，不是要杀你。"莱昂纳多嘴角那块干皮又扯了扯，"我是要你帮我打开黑铁巨门最深处的最后一道封印。那道封印只有你的血能解。"

"而你妹妹——"他指向阿黛尔，"只是确保你配合的筹码。"

"配合我，红龙。"莱昂纳多的金属手指悬在那个红色按钮上方，"帮我重启机械神国，我会让你成为新神国的副君。和我一起统治这个世界。"

"否则——"

他按下按钮。

"咔嚓"一声。

"——我就用这999架欧米茄原型体，把翡冷翠从这个世界上抹掉。"

然后整个熔岩之心都震动了。

不是机械的震动，是从地底深处涌上来的、连绵不绝的、像心跳一样的震动。

圆形石室的穹顶上，那数以万计的微型齿轮突然全部停止了转动，停了一瞬，然后以十倍的速度疯狂旋转起来。金属星空变成了金属漩涡，发出尖锐的嗡鸣。

然后西泽尔感觉到了。

从地面之下，从矿道之外，从维苏威火山的身躯里，从翡冷翠的地基里——数以千计的红水银核心同时苏醒。

天空亮了。

不是阳光。

是金色的光。

维苏威火山外，翡冷翠的天空上，无数道暗金色的光柱冲天而起，每一道光柱都是一架欧米茄原型体启动时释放的能量脉冲。远处的翡冷翠城，那些教堂的尖顶，那些贵族府的穹顶，那些圣堂装甲师的军营——一座接一座地亮起同样的暗金色光芒。

999架。

都在苏醒。

阿方索的蜘蛛巢腕表突然疯狂震动，他低头一看，脸色骤变："老板！欧米茄原型体的信号！从地面到地下一百公里范围内全部检测到了！它们在向这里移动！"

唐璜的蔷薇之鬼的通讯频道里传来薇若兰的急促声音："西泽尔！火山外围出现大量欧米茄原型体！从北麓、东麓、西麓同时向火山口集结！"

昆提良握紧备用战斧的手把，青筋暴起。

西泽尔没有回答他们。

他盯着莱昂纳多那只悬在按钮上的金属手，然后慢慢地、慢慢地抽出了腰间的Excalibur残刃。

圣剑碎片和龙牙剑断茬拼接成的残缺剑刃在空气中散发出暗金色的灼热光芒，剑身上梵文流转，像是在呼吸。

"我妹妹，"西泽尔的声音很轻，轻得几乎听不见，"放不放。"

不是问句。

是陈述。

莱昂纳多的暗红镜头盯着那柄Excalibur残刃，金属手指在按钮上轻轻敲了敲。

"杀了我，她就死。机器会在我心跳停止的瞬间释放红水银把她烧成灰。"

西泽尔的眼睛眯了起来。

紫瞳中的金红色纹路开始浮现，后颈的黄金套管滚烫，像是要在皮肤上烙出一个印子。他的血管里流淌的不再是血液，是某种更古老的、来自三百年前的力量。

"你以为只有你会用血脉吗？"西泽尔低声说。

他抬起Excalibur残刃，指向莱昂纳多。

剑身上的梵文突然亮了起来。

他踏前一步——

"砰"的一声闷响，从通道入口传来。

碧儿惊呼一声，所有人都转头看去。

圆形石室的入口处，那扇打开的黑铁巨门——门框上的卡巴拉之树圣徽开始疯狂闪烁，一道又一道暗金色的光从门缝中涌进来。那些光不是光柱，是光"潮"，是无数光点汇聚成的、像潮水一样涌入的暗金色洪流。

是欧米茄原型体。

它们到了。

第一架欧米茄原型体从黑铁巨门外挤了进来——五米多高的暗金色巨人，胸腔的红水银核心疯狂跳动，面甲竖缝中射出暗金色的光柱。光柱扫过圆形石室的穹顶，扫过石室的墙壁，扫过那台锁着阿黛尔的机器——

然后它停住了。

它没有攻击。

它只是静静地站在入口处，挡住了西泽尔一行人撤退的路。

第二架，第三架，第四架……

一架接一架的欧米茄原型体从黑铁巨门外涌入，五米多高的暗金色巨人排成扇形，把整个圆形石室的入口堵得严严实实。它们胸腔的红水银核心同时跳动，跳动的频率完全一致，像是一颗巨大的心脏在石室深处跳动。

999架中的先头部队，已经到了。

"你看，"莱昂纳多的声音从机器后面传来，带着金属质感，"你的选择其实只有一个。"

"服从，或者死亡。"

西泽尔没有回答他。

他看着那些涌入的暗金色巨人，看着它们胸腔跳动的红水银核心，看着它们面甲竖缝中射出的暗金色光柱——

然后他听到了一个声音。

很轻。

很细。

像风吹过金属花瓣。

是阿黛尔。

阿黛尔抬起了头。她的眼睛没有看西泽尔，没有看莱昂纳多，没有看那些涌入的暗金色巨人。

她看着穹顶那数以万计的微型齿轮。

她开始唱歌。

那是一首西泽尔从来没有听过的歌。歌词是陌生的语言，旋律简单却有一种穿透金属的力量。歌声很轻，轻得被欧米茄原型体胸腔的跳动声盖住了大半，但西泽尔还是听见了。

那首歌的底调，和琳琅夫人哼过的摇篮曲一模一样。

是锡兰的圣歌。

阿黛尔在唱锡兰圣歌。

那首能——

莱昂纳多的暗红镜头猛地转向阿黛尔，他的金属身体第一次有了明显的反应——金属脊柱僵硬地转动，金属手指在按钮上捏紧，捏得指节发出了咯吱声。

"停下！"他厉声说，"停下那首歌！"

阿黛尔没有停。

她的嘴唇还在动，歌声还在继续。

那首西泽尔听不懂的锡兰圣歌，像一缕细细的清泉，正在这个充斥着红水银蒸汽、金属齿轮和欧米茄原型体心跳的圆形石室里，缓缓地、缓缓地蔓延开来。

阿方索的蜘蛛巢腕表突然疯狂震动，他低头一看，脸色骤变："老板！欧米茄原型体的信号！从地面到地下一百公里范围内全部检测到了！它们在向这里移动！"

唐璜的蔷薇之鬼的通讯频道里传来薇若兰的急促声音："西泽尔！火山外围出现大量欧米茄原型体！从北麓、东麓、西麓同时向火山口集结！"

昆提良握紧备用战斧的手把，青筋暴起。

西泽尔没有回答他们。

他盯着莱昂纳多那只悬在按钮上的金属手，然后慢慢地、慢慢地抽出了腰间的Excalibur残刃。

圣剑碎片和龙牙剑断茬拼接成的残缺剑刃在空气中散发出暗金色的灼热光芒，剑身上梵文流转，像是在呼吸。

"我妹妹，"西泽尔的声音很轻，轻得几乎听不见，"放不放。"

不是问句。

是陈述。

莱昂纳多的暗红镜头盯着那柄Excalibur残刃，金属手指在按钮上轻轻敲了敲。

"杀了我，她就死。机器会在我心跳停止的瞬间释放红水银把她烧成灰。"

西泽尔的眼睛眯了起来。

紫瞳中的金红色纹路开始浮现，后颈的黄金套管滚烫，像是要在皮肤上烙出一个印子。他的血管里流淌的不再是血液，是某种更古老的、来自三百年前的力量。

"你以为只有你会用血脉吗？"西泽尔低声说。

他抬起Excalibur残刃，指向莱昂纳多。

剑身上的梵文突然亮了起来。

他踏前一步——

"砰"的一声闷响，从通道入口传来。

碧儿惊呼一声，所有人都转头看去。

圆形石室的入口处，那扇打开的黑铁巨门——门框上的卡巴拉之树圣徽开始疯狂闪烁，一道又一道暗金色的光从门缝中涌进来。那些光不是光柱，是光"潮"，是无数光点汇聚成的、像潮水一样涌入的暗金色洪流。

是欧米茄原型体。

它们到了。

然后它停住了。

它没有攻击。

它只是静静地站在入口处，挡住了西泽尔一行人撤退的路。

第二架，第三架，第四架……

一架接一架的欧米茄原型体从黑铁巨门外涌入，五米多高的暗金色巨人排成扇形，把整个圆形石室的入口堵得严严实实。它们胸腔的红水银核心同时跳动，跳动的频率完全一致，像是一颗巨大的心脏在石室深处跳动。

999架中的先头部队，已经到了。

"你看，"莱昂纳多的声音从机器后面传来，带着金属质感，"你的选择其实只有一个。"

"服从，或者死亡。"

西泽尔没有回答他。

他看着那些涌入的暗金色巨人，看着它们胸腔跳动的红水银核心，看着它们面甲竖缝中射出的暗金色光柱——

然后他听到了一个声音。

很轻。

很细。

像风吹过金属花瓣。

是阿黛尔。

阿黛尔抬起了头。她的眼睛没有看西泽尔，没有看莱昂纳多，没有看那些涌入的暗金色巨人。

她看着穹顶那数以万计的微型齿轮。

她开始唱歌。

那是一首西泽尔从来没有听过的歌。歌词是陌生的语言，旋律简单却有一种穿透金属的力量。歌声很轻，轻得被欧米茄原型体胸腔的跳动声盖住了大半，但西泽尔还是听见了。

那首歌的底调，和琳琅夫人哼过的摇篮曲一模一样。
