【中文】
第257章 梵天陨落倒计时

圆形大厅穹顶的齿轮还在缓缓转动。

数以万计的黄铜齿轮相互咬合，红水银驱动的脉动光芒将整座大厅映成一片暗红色的深海。嗡——嗡——嗡——那是数百颗机械心脏同时苏醒的声音，从穹顶上方传下来，闷沉而密集。

欧米茄原型体群正在升空。

暗金色的装甲板开始活动，关节处射出刺眼的白光，背后的飞行机构像折翼的巨鸟一样层层展开。它们的红水银核心温度在持续升高——西泽尔通过还没断开的神经接驳信号读到了那些数据。每一台欧米茄的核心内部压力都已经突破了安全阈值。

它们是炸弹。

数百颗正在倒计时的红水银炸弹。

西泽尔单膝跪在莱昂纳多的尸体旁边。Excalibur碎片已经从他失去力量的手指间滑落，叮当一声滚在地上。他感觉到自己的心跳正在放缓——不是平静，是英雄人格退潮后那种濒死的虚脱。视野还是模糊的，带着一层血红色的雾。

碧儿跌跌撞撞地从大厅边缘跑过来，脸上挂着泪痕和烟灰。

"少爷！"

她扑过来扶住他的手臂。他感觉到那双手在剧烈地发抖。

"还活着。"西泽尔的声音哑得像是从喉咙深处刮出来的金属碎片。

穹顶上方又传来一声沉闷的爆响，那是某台欧米茄原型体背部飞行机构完全展开的蒸汽喷射声。紧跟着第二台、第三台——像多米诺骨牌一样连锁启动。

"嘀。"

一声细微的电子音从圆形大厅侧面传来。

红水银微晶开始脉动，频率和人的心跳一致。

圆形大厅侧面那扇被锁死数十年的暗门从中间裂开，滚烫的热风从门缝里灌进来。薇若兰从门后走出来。

她浑身都是汗，军服被汗水浸透贴在身上，巧克力色的长发散乱地粘在脖颈上。她左手捧着一只金色的机械鸟——那只鸟比真鸟还小，翅膀张开不到一掌宽，通体鎏金，胸口嵌着一颗红水银微晶，腹部刻着一行古拉丁文：Rex Immortalis。右手握着一枚拇指大的银莲花项链坠，花瓣边缘嵌着细密的齿轮纹路。

那是琳琅夫人的遗物。

"找到了。"薇若兰的声音急促而清晰，"佛朗哥教授把它藏在旧基地武器库最深处的锡封匣里。"

她快步走到西泽尔身边，蹲下，把金色机械鸟放在地面上。鸟胸口的红水银微晶正在一明一灭地脉动，每闪一次就发出一声细微的电子音。

"嘀。"

"倒计时已经启动。"薇若兰抬头看着西泽尔，"三十分钟后，梵天陨落进入临界状态。届时只需要把您的血——"

她举起右手的银莲花项链坠。

"——滴在这上面。"

"嘀。"

西泽尔沉默了一秒。他的目光扫过穹顶上方正在编队升空的欧米茄群，又扫过大厅另一端那座矗立在红光中的黑铁王座。王座上嵌满了机械锁扣和蒸汽管路，一个纤细的身影被机械手臂固定在王座靠背上，长发散落在肩头，嘴唇还在轻轻翕动。

阿黛尔还在唱。

锡兰莲花之歌的旋律像流水一样淌过每一面刻着梵文的墙壁，钻进每一台被策反的欧米茄原型体铜绿色的核心里。那些原本围攻西泽尔的、被阿黛尔歌声唤醒的铜绿色核心的欧米茄，正在和红色眼睛的同族在穹顶上方缠斗。金属碰撞声和红水银核心爆裂的声音不断从上方落下来。

"先撤。"西泽尔说。

"阿黛尔小姐还被锁在王座上。"阿方索的声音从王座方向传来。他蹲在王座基座前，机械手里拿着一只从莱昂纳多改造体残骸上拆下来的蒸汽仪表，仪表上的指针正在疯狂旋转。"机械锁是八位数的锡兰星见祷文编码，我需要破解时间。"

"多久？"

"三分钟。"

"那就三分钟。"唐璜说着已经走了过去。

他帮阿方索稳住王座基座上晃动的蒸汽管，昆提良则单手举着秘银重盾挡在王座上方，替他们挡住从穹顶落下的金属碎片和红水银液滴。碧儿从腰间解下便携式神经电流控制器，快步走到西泽尔身边。

"少爷，不朽之王系统——"碧儿低声说。

"关闭。"

"您现在的身体——"

"关闭。"西泽尔重复了一遍。

碧儿咬了咬嘴唇，按下关闭键。一道细微的电流信号从控制器传向西泽尔后颈的黄金套管。

芯片开始断电。

英雄人格的反噬像退潮一样从神经系统里彻底抽离，那种铺天盖地的疯狂和力量感消失得无影无踪，取而代之的是巨大的虚脱。西泽尔感觉到自己的膝盖在发软，视野从血红色慢慢恢复成正常的深紫色——他的紫瞳不再有金色纹路跳动，只是普通的、带着疲惫的暗紫色。

他几乎是在同一瞬间倒下去的。

唐璜眼疾手快地扶住了他。

"老板！"

"没事。"西泽尔闭着眼说，声音低得几乎听不见，"就是……累。"

他靠着唐泽尔的肩膀勉强站稳，睁开眼睛看向王座的方向。阿方索正在用蒸汽仪表逐位匹配祷文编码，机械手指在仪表盘上飞快地跳动，汗水从他额头上滚落下来。

"嘀。"

"嘀。"

"嘀。"

机械鸟的倒计时声在圆形大厅里回荡。

穹顶上方，一台铜绿色核心的欧米茄被三台红色眼睛的同族围攻，红水银核心爆裂，整个身体从穹顶坠落下来，砸在距离王座不到十米的地面上，震得整个大厅都在颤抖。

"密码匹配中——六位——七位——"阿方索的声音急促。

西泽尔感觉自己的后颈在发凉。黄金套管的温度已经降到了正常值，那种与世界树残枝共鸣的灼热感彻底消失了。他现在只是一个虚脱的、靠着唐璜肩膀才能站稳的普通人。

"八位——匹配完成！"

金属锁扣松开的声音从王座上传来。机械手臂一根接一根地松脱，蒸汽从锁扣的缝隙中喷出。阿黛尔从王座上滑下来，被阿方索稳稳接住。

她还在唱。

歌声没有停过。

从西泽尔进入圆形大厅开始，她的声音就像一根不断裂的线，把锡兰星见三百年前的记忆缝进了这个时代里。她的脸色苍白得没有一点血色，眼睛半闭着，嘴唇在动，旋律像是从她身体最深处流出来的。

"阿黛尔小姐。"阿方索轻声叫她。

歌声停了。

阿黛尔睁开眼睛，那双和西泽尔一模一样的深紫色瞳孔里还有残余的金色纹路在闪烁，但已经在慢慢消退。

"哥……"她的声音像是从很远的地方传来，"我……我唱完了。"

她说完这句话就晕了过去。

阿方索弯腰把她背起来。她比他想象的还要轻。

"走。"阿方索说。

"从哪条路撤？"昆提良问。

"达·芬奇通道。"西泽尔说，"尽头连着旧矿道。"

"旧矿道我们进来的时候已经炸了一半——"唐璜皱眉。

"还有一半没炸。"阿方索已经迈开步子，"达·芬奇通道尽头有岔路，其中一条通向旧休息室。佛朗哥教授的全息留言里提到过，那里的岩壁上有一扇密涅瓦机关的暗门。"

薇若兰弯腰拾起地上的金色机械鸟和银莲花项链坠，把机械鸟小心地塞进军服内袋，项链坠攥在掌心里。机械鸟胸口红水银微晶的脉动透过衣料传出来，一明一灭。

"嘀。"

"嘀。"

圆形大厅穹顶上方又有一台铜绿色核心的欧米茄被撕碎，红水银核心爆裂的火焰把穹顶映成了白昼。剩余的铜绿色核心的欧米茄越来越少，已经被红色眼睛的同族彻底压制。

"快走。"西泽尔说。

---

地面在震。

维苏威火山北麓的旧矿道入口处，瓦莲京娜站在改装神怒Ⅲ型甲胇的肩部，仰头望着火山口。

火山口在喷发。

不是岩浆，是数百台欧米茄原型体。

它们从火山口里冲出来，暗金色的装甲板在初升的朝阳下闪着刺眼的光，背后的飞行机构喷出蓝白色的蒸汽柱，像一群从地狱里涌出来的巨型黄蜂。它们在编队——密集的菱形编队，每三台一组，组与组之间保持着精确的等距，朝着东方——朝着王屋山——全速飞行。

"有多少？"李锡尼骑在机械马上，抬头数着天空。

"三百二十七台。"瓦莲京娜说，"我能数到三百二十七，剩下的还在上升。"

"全部都是自毁状态？"

"每一台的核心温度都超过了临界值。"瓦莲京娜的声音很冷，"莱昂纳多把它们全部设成了飞行炸弹。"

李锡尼低头看着手里的朗基努斯圣枪碎片。那块碎片在剧烈地跳动，红水银微晶发出刺眼的光——它感应到了欧米茄原型体群的能量。

"三百二十七颗红水银炸弹飞向王屋山。"李锡尼低声说，"十五分钟。"

"嗯。"瓦莲京娜说。

她转过头，看着身后那列蓄势待发的叶尼塞蒸汽机械骑兵。数十台改装神怒Ⅲ型甲胇排成整齐的横列，蒸汽锅炉的轰鸣声在矿道入口处汇成一片低沉的雷鸣。骑士们坐在驾驶舱里，白手套紧握着操纵杆。

"所有人听令。"瓦莲京娜举起改装神怒Ⅲ型甲胇的右臂，"目标——红色眼睛的欧米茄原型体群。掩护井口，确保西泽尔一行人安全撤离。"

"是！"

"开火。"

改装神怒Ⅲ型甲胇背部的蒸汽喷射推进器点燃，蓝白色的火焰在矿道入口处升腾。叶尼塞蒸汽机械骑兵如同一道银色洪流涌入维苏威火山北麓的旧矿道。

---

旧矿道深处。

阿方索找到了佛朗哥教授全息留言里提到的那扇暗门。

门后是一台老旧的履带式装甲矿车。矿车车厢足有十五米长，外壳是生锈的铁皮——和普通的矿石运输车没什么两样，但车底焊着厚达半尺的影金属装甲板，驾驶舱前面还装着一面小型蒸汽盾。佛朗哥教授的手笔。

"还能用。"阿方索检查了一遍矿车的蒸汽锅炉，"备用能源，足够我们跑出去。"

所有人上车。

唐璜和昆提良把西泽尔安置在车厢后方的弹药箱上，让他靠着装甲板坐稳。薇若兰坐在他旁边，金色机械鸟放在膝上，掌心攥着琳琅夫人的银莲花项链坠，眼睛盯着胸口红水银微晶的脉动。

"嘀。"

"嘀。"

阿方索把阿黛尔放在车厢中央的维修台上，用一条旧毛毯盖住她。碧儿坐在驾驶舱里，操纵着矿车的蒸汽阀门。

"准备好了。"碧儿说。

"开车。"西泽尔说。

矿车的蒸汽锅炉轰鸣起来，履带开始转动，整台矿车像一头钢铁巨兽一样冲进了达·芬奇通道的黑暗里。

车轮碾过碎石的声音在矿道里回荡。两侧岩壁上刻着的达·芬奇版本机械神教徽记——齿轮中心嵌着五芒星——在矿车蒸汽灯的光芒中一闪而过。空气里弥漫着硫磺和红水银的腥味。

"嘀。"

"嘀。"

达·芬奇通道的尽头是一扇生锈的铁栅门。

阿方索从怀里摸出昂格里亚旧矿道铁栅门钥匙——那把黄铜钥匙在他手里微微发烫。他把钥匙插进锁孔，拧动。

"咔嗒。"

铁栅门轰然打开。

---

外面是维苏威火山北麓的清晨。

朝阳从东方升起，把整片天空染成了玫瑰红色。

西泽尔被唐璜和昆提良扶着走出矿车，他眯着眼适应外面的光线。远处传来改装神怒Ⅲ型甲胇的蒸汽连铳声和红水银核心爆裂的声音——瓦莲京娜的骑兵正在井口外和零星突破封锁的红色眼睛的欧米茄原型体缠斗。

"嘀。"

薇若兰低头看了一眼膝上的金色机械鸟。倒计时的红水银微晶在玫瑰红色的晨光中一明一灭。

"还有二十一分钟。"她说。

然后她抬起头。

对面的山顶上，站着一个人。

那人穿着一身月白色的长袍，衣摆在山风中猎猎作响。腰间佩着两把剑——一把长而直，纹路如凝固闪电；一把窄而弯，覆着淡绿色铜锈。他的眼睛是紫色的。

他的身后，密密麻麻地排列着数百台漆黑的重型机动甲胇。

每一台甲胇的头部都雕刻着夔龙首，胸甲浮雕着鎏金夔龙纹，右臂加装小型蒸汽连铳，左臂配备精钢重盾。蒸汽锅炉的轰鸣声汇成一片低沉的雷鸣，在山间回荡。

鬼武者Ⅱ型。

西泽尔的目光和山顶上那人的目光在玫瑰红色的晨光中相遇。

"嘀。"

金色机械鸟的倒计时还在继续。

【English】
Chapter 257 — The Brahma Countdown

The gears in the vault's dome still turned.

Tens of thousands of them, brass teeth biting brass teeth, a planetary mechanism so old no one living could remember who had first cut the teeth. Red mercury pulsed through the lubricating channels webbing the ceiling, and the light it cast was the color of old blood held up to a flame. The dome breathed. Three hundred mechanical hearts had woken in the last quarter-hour, and the bass note of their ignition drifted down through the gear-trees like sound through deep water.

The Omega prototypes were climbing.

Their armor plates — dark gold, oil-black in the seams — flexed along the spine, the way a mantis unfolds. Jets of white light stabbed from the knuckles. From the shoulders, the flight rigs fanned open in tiered layers, like the wings of some vast mechanical heron waking from sleep. Through the half-seated nerve-link in his broken spine Cesare could read the temperature curves of their cores. Every one of them was above safety. Every one of them was climbing.

Bombs. Three hundred of them, in flight, on a fuse.

He was on one knee beside Leonardo's body.

The last shard of Excalibur had rolled from his fingers some seconds ago. He could still hear it — the small, ridiculous, crystalline sound of a piece of divine metal ringing on the flagstone. His heart was slowing. Not the slowing of calm; the slowing of a tide going out, the sucking emptiness left behind when the hero in him had at last retreated. His sight ran in a red mist, the kind you get when you have bitten your tongue through.

Beryl came staggering out from the edge of the hall, soot and tears striping her face.

"Young master!"

She caught his arm. He felt the tremor running through her hands.

"Still breathing," he said. His voice came out like a shaving of metal drawn from the back of his throat.

Another muffled concussion above them — the second Omega's flight rig opening, then the third, the ignition rippling up the dome in a sequence, a slow chain of small detonations. The ceiling was alive with them now, a constellation of dark gold shapes swinging past one another in their slow orbits toward the oculus.

Beep.

A small electronic note, from the side of the hall.

A red mercury micro-crystal pulsing at the cadence of a human heart.

The sealed door — the one that had been locked shut for decades — split down its center, and hot air pressed in through the gap like the breath of an oven. Violante stepped through.

She was soaked. Her uniform clung to her; her dark hair stuck to her neck in long ropes. In her left hand she carried a golden mechanical bird — smaller than a real one, wingspan not a hand's breadth, gilded all over, a red mercury micro-crystal set into its breast, and along the belly a line of antique Latin: REX IMMORTALIS. In her right fist she held a silver lotus the size of a thumb, its petals traced with the fine teeth of a clockwork gear.

Lady Linara's relic.

"Found it," Violante said, quick and clean. "Professor Franco had it sealed in a tin coffer at the back of the old arsenal."

She crossed the floor in four strides, knelt, and set the bird down on the stone. The micro-crystal in its breast pulsed — on, on, off — each beat giving out that same patient, small note.

Beep.

"The countdown's started." Violante looked up at him. "In twenty-nine minutes the Brahma system crosses critical. Then all it needs is your blood —"

She lifted the silver lotus.

"— dropped onto this."

Beep.

Cesare was silent a second. His gaze went up, to the Omega swarm rearranging itself over the dome, and then across the hall to the black iron throne standing in its own column of red light. Mechanical clamps pinned a thin shape to the back of it. Long hair spilled over her shoulders. Her lips were still moving.

Adele was still singing.

The Ceylon Star-Viewer's Song moved through the vault like a slow river, finding every wall, every glyph, every copper-green core of every Omega her voice had turned against its brothers. Those turned Omegas — the green-cored ones — were tangling with the red-eyed cousins in the air overhead. Metal against metal. The pop of red mercury cores blowing out, like wet firecrackers going off in sequence.

"We pull out," Cesare said.

"Miss Adele is still bound to the throne." Alfonso's voice came from the direction of the throne. He was crouched at its base, his mechanical hand holding a steam gauge he had salvaged from what was left of Leonardo's modified body. The needle on the gauge was spinning like a wasp in a jar. "The lock is an eight-digit Ceylon prayer cipher. I need time to break it."

"How long?"

"Three minutes."

"Then three minutes it is." Don Juan was already walking.

He helped Alfonso brace the steam pipes that were shaking at the throne's base. Quintilian lifted the mithril pavise on one arm and held it over them both, a roof against the metal fragments and the droplets of red mercury falling from the fight above. Beryl unclipped the portable neural current regulator from her belt and went to Cesare's side.

"Young master — the Immortal King system —"

"Shut it down."

"Your body right now —"

"Shut it down."

Beryl set her teeth and pressed the key. A thin current ran from the regulator into the golden ferrule at the back of his neck.

The chip went dark.

The backlash came out of him like a tide leaving a sand flat — every inch of that mad, borrowed strength drawing back through his nerves, and the absence of it huge, like the room after a thunderclap. His knees folded. The red mist in his eyes thinned, thinned, and resolved back into the ordinary dark purple of his own irises — no gold traceries, no burning. Just tired.

He was, in the same instant, falling.

Don Juan caught him under the arms.

"Boss!"

"I'm all right." Cesare had his eyes closed. His voice was barely there. "Just — tired."

He let Don Juan take his weight, opened his eyes, and looked toward the throne. Alfonso's mechanical fingers were running the gauge through the prayer cipher, position by position; sweat ran down his temples in clean lines.

Beep.

Beep.

Beep.

The bird's note went on through the vault, patient.

Above them, a copper-green Omega was being taken by three of the red-eyed ones. Its core blew. The body tumbled out of the dome's air, struck the floor less than ten paces from the throne, and the whole hall shuddered on its foundations.

"Match — six — seven —" Alfonso's voice was clipped. "Eight — match complete."

The locks came off the throne one by one. Steam hissed from the seam of every clamp as it released. Adele slipped forward off the seat, and Alfonso caught her.

She was still singing.

The song had not stopped since the moment Cesare had entered the hall. Three hundred years of the Star-Viewer's memory, stitched through the present by a single unbroken thread of her voice. Her face was the color of chalk, her eyes half-shut, the words still moving on her lips, the melody running from somewhere deeper in her than her own lungs could account for.

"Miss Adele," Alfonso said, soft.

The song stopped.

Adele opened her eyes. The irises were the same dark purple as her brother's, and the last of the gold traceries were fading in them, dimming like coals in a hearth.

"Brother," she said, from very far away. "I — I finished."

She fainted before the second word was out.

Alfonso bent and lifted her. She weighed less than he had expected.

"Move," he said.

"Which way out?" Quintilian asked.

"The da Vinci passage," Cesare said. "It opens onto the old mine."

"The old mine's half-collapsed. We blew half of it on the way in —"

"Half's not all." Alfonso was already walking. "The far end of the da Vinci passage has a fork. One branch runs to the old rest chamber. Franco's holo-notes mention a Minerva lock on the rock face there."

Violante bent and picked up the bird and the silver lotus. She tucked the bird inside her uniform, against her ribs, and closed her fist around the pendant. The micro-crystal pulsed through the cloth of her coat — on, on, off — the small patient note of the countdown, traveling with her.

Beep.

Beep.

Another copper-green Omega was torn apart above them. Its core went off in a column of white flame that turned the dome briefly to daylight. Of the green-cored ones, fewer now. The red-eyed cousins were pressing them into a smaller and smaller corner of the air.

"Quickly," Cesare said.

---

The ground was shaking.

At the mouth of the old mine, on the north slope of Vesuvius, Valentina stood on the shoulder-plate of her modified Divine Wrath III and looked up at the crater.

The crater was erupting.

Not lava. Three hundred Omegas.

They came pouring out of the caldera, dark gold armor catching the early sun in long, blinding strokes, flight rigs firing pale blue columns of steam behind them, a swarm of great brass hornets boiling up out of the mountain's throat. They arranged themselves as they climbed — tight diamond formations, three machines to a cell, cells spaced with mechanical precision, all of them aimed east.

East. Toward Wangwu Mountain.

"How many?" Licinius asked, from the back of his mechanical horse. He was counting the sky.

"Three hundred and twenty-seven," Valentina said. "I can count to three hundred and twenty-seven. The rest are still rising."

"Every one of them on a self-destruct?"

"Every core is past critical. Leonardo set them all to fly and burn." Her voice was even. "Three hundred and twenty-seven red mercury bombs, all pointed at the same city."

Licinius looked down at the fragment of the Longinus Spear in his hand. It was jumping against his palm. The red mercury micro-crystal in its haft threw white sparks — it could feel the swarm.

"Fifteen minutes," he said, quietly.

"Yes," Valentina said.

She turned her head, and behind her the Yenisei Steam Mech Cavalry stood in its ranks. Dozens of modified Divine Wrath IIIs in a long, even line, boilers snarling, the deep bass of their ignition merging into a single sustained note that went on and on across the slope. The knights sat in their cockpits, white-gloved hands on the control yokes.

"All riders." Valentina raised the right arm of her suit. "Target: red-eyed Omega prototypes. Objective: cover the wellhead. Get Cesare and his people out alive."

"Yes, ma'am."

"Open fire."

The dorsal steam thrusters on the suits lit, blue-white flame blooming at the mine mouth, and the Yenisei cavalry went up the slope of the mountain in a single silver flood.

---

Deep in the old mine, Alfonso had found the door.

Behind it, a tracked armored mine car — fifteen meters of rusted iron skin, a half-foot of shadow-metal welded along the belly, a small steam shield mounted in front of the cab. Franco's work, plain as his signature.

"Still good," Alfonso said, after he had tapped the boiler. "Reserve pressure. Enough to get us out."

They climbed in.

Don Juan and Quintilian settled Cesare against an ammunition crate at the back of the car, his shoulders propped against the armor. Violante sat down beside him, the bird in her lap, the silver lotus closed in her palm, watching the pulse in the bird's breast.

Beep.

Beep.

Alfonso laid Adele down on a maintenance bench in the middle of the car and pulled a worn blanket over her. Beryl took the cab, her hands on the steam valve.

"Ready," Beryl said.

"Go," Cesare said.

The boiler caught, the tracks bit into the stone, and the mine car went into the dark of the da Vinci passage like a beast of iron that had been waiting a long time to be let out.

The wheels ground over loose rock. The light from the steam lamps ran along the walls of the passage, catching and losing the old da Vinci Guild's monogram — the five-pointed star set in a gear — over and over, in a steady rhythm. The air tasted of sulfur and red mercury, and the small sound of the bird's pulse ran underneath everything else.

Beep.

Beep.

The far end of the da Vinci passage was a rusted iron gate.

Alfonso pulled the Angria old-mine gate key from his coat — a brass key, faintly warm in his hand. He fitted it, turned.

Click.

The gate swung open.

---

Outside the mountain it was early morning, on the north slope of Vesuvius.

The sun was just up. It laid the whole sky out in rose.

Cesare came out of the car with Don Juan and Quintilian holding him up on either side. He squinted into the light. From somewhere downslope came the regular crack of steam repeaters and the duller pops of red mercury cores blowing out — Valentina's cavalry, working over the red-eyed Omegas that had strayed past the wellhead.

Beep.

Violante looked down at the bird in her lap. The micro-crystal was pulsing in the rose light of the new day — patient, on, on, off.

"Twenty-one minutes," she said.

And then she raised her head.

There was a man on the ridge opposite them.

He was wearing a robe the color of moonlight, and the wind moved the hem of it in slow, deliberate strokes. Two swords hung at his waist — one long and straight, its grain like frozen lightning, the other narrow and curved, furred with a pale green patina. His eyes were purple.

Behind him, the slope was black with machines. Hundreds of them. Heavy mobile armors, glossy as wet coal, kuí-drake heads carved into the helm of every one, gilded kuí-drake crests along the cuirass, a small steam repeater fitted to the right arm, a fine steel pavise to the left. The boilers of the whole line were running, and the sound they made was one long, low roll of thunder, going on and on across the mountainside.

Ghost Warrior Mk. II.

Cesare's gaze met the gaze of the man on the ridge, in the rose-colored air of the early morning.

Beep.

The bird went on counting.

第258章 大夏龙雀的守护

【中文】
第258章 大夏龙雀的守护

王屋山。黎明前最后一段黑暗里。

天穹是铁灰色的，东方的天际线刚刚裂开一道口子，露出了底下暗红色的光，像有人在墨色的天幕上浇了一盆滚烫的铜汁。山脚下的原野上，几百台漆黑的重型机动甲胇排成整齐的方阵，蒸汽锅炉的轰鸣声汇成低沉的雷鸣，在山谷间来回撞击。每一台甲胇的头部都雕刻着夔龙首，铜牙铁齿，龙睛嵌着红水银晶片，在晨曦未至的微光中泛着幽暗的赤红。胸甲上的鎏金夔龙纹被蒸汽凝结的水汽打湿，反射出朦胧的金光。

鬼武者Ⅱ型。夏国最锋利的刀。

甲胇方阵之后，是数千匹夔龙马。黑色的鬃毛在晨风中翻卷，像是大地本身在呼吸。马背上的骑士身穿玄色轻甲，腰佩环首长刀，手持夔龙纹圆盾，所有人的目光都朝着西边——看着天际线上那片正在渗血的天空。

楚舜华骑在队列的最前方。

他的坐骑是一匹通体红如朱砂的夔龙马，肩高近六尺，比周围所有的夔龙马都高出整整一个头。额前一道陈旧的弹洞，那是十七年前南疆之战留下的勋章，两枚嵌入额骨的弹片至今未取，伤口早已愈合成坚硬的疤痕。鬃毛不是黑色，而是罕见的赤红，在晨风中飞扬如火焰。

这匹马叫朱砂。

当年先帝御驾亲征南疆，十六岁的楚舜华骑着它冲入敌阵，中了三箭仍不肯倒下。战后御医说它废了，所有人都以为它活不过那个冬天。但它活了下来。后来楚舜华登上监国公爵之位，这匹本该被豢养在皇城御苑的老马却从御苑中消失了——有人说是被送回了北疆草原，有人说是老死了。

只有楚舜华知道，朱砂被他送到了王屋山下的一处秘密马场，藏在深山老林里养了十七年。

不是抛弃。是保护。

这匹马的心口，埋着一枚暗金色的微型金属容器。容器里装的不是红水银，而是王屋山地底深处世界树残根意识碎片提炼出的能量介质——楚舜华的母亲临终前交给他的最后一件遗物，嘱咐他将这东西植入最亲近的夔龙马体内。十七年来，朱砂以那枚容器为心脏，不知疲倦，不惧伤痛，能与残根意识共享危险感知。

楚舜华缓缓抬起了头。

西边。

天际线上出现了一片暗金色的云。不，不是云——是数以百计的钢铁身影，遮天蔽日地涌来。它们的暗金色装甲在黎明的微光中反射出刺目的光，胸前嵌着的红水银核心发出跳动的红光，像是一千只血红的眼睛同时睁开。

欧米茄原型体。

一架又一架，密密层层，像是从地狱中飞出的蝗虫群。每一架都被设置为自毁飞行炸弹，胸腔里的红水银核心将在十五分钟后全部引爆——引爆的范围足以将整座王屋山从地图上抹去。

目标：世界树残枝东方主根节点。

楚舜华抽出了腰间那柄长而直的佩剑。

剑身狭长，通体暗金色，那是用夔龙马朱砂幼年脱落的额前断角打磨而成。剑身保留着夔龙角天然的纹理，纹路如凝固的闪电，握在手中微微发热，仿佛仍有血液在剑身中流动。剑锷处刻着两个古老的篆字——龙雀。

夔龙角剑。夏国皇族代代相传的神器。

"传令。"

楚舜华的声音不大，却穿透了甲胇方阵的轰鸣，像一根银针穿透了滚雷。

"鬼武者Ⅱ型，前出迎敌，正面拦截。"

"夔龙马骑兵，两翼展开，截杀漏网之鱼。"

"目标——全歼。"

号角声响起，苍凉而悠远，在王屋山的山谷中回荡。那是夏国军中最古老的牛角号，号声所到之处，三军肃穆。

数百台鬼武者Ⅱ型甲胇同时启动，蒸汽锅炉喷出青白色的蒸汽，推动着这些钢铁巨人向前冲锋。左臂的精钢重盾举起，五层交错锻造的盾面在晨光中闪烁；右臂的小型蒸汽连铳开火了，弹雨呼啸着射向天空，在欧米茄原型体的装甲上炸开一朵朵刺目的火花。

欧米茄原型体群发出刺耳的金属啸叫，像是一群被激怒的黄蜂，分成数十个编队俯冲而下。它们的指尖射出暗金色的热能光束，光束所到之处，鬼武者甲胇的装甲板被烧穿，蒸汽管道爆裂，金属碎片四溅。一台鬼武者Ⅱ型被三架欧米茄原型体围攻，盾牌上出现了三个焦黑的凹坑，骑士怒吼一声，盾牌猛然挥出，将一架欧米茄撞飞，但另外两架的光束已经射穿了他的胸甲。红水银核心引爆，连锁的爆炸将那台鬼武者撕成了碎片，黑色的金属残骸散落一地。

"稳住阵型！"楚舜华沉声下令，"盾牌手前压，掩护射击！"

朱砂像是听懂了他的命令，长嘶一声，驮着楚舜华冲入了战阵。它的速度远超周围的夔龙马，在钢铁的洪流中如同一道赤红的闪电。十七年来它一直被藏在深山里，肌肉从未松弛，骨骼从未退化，此刻全力奔驰，四蹄翻飞，鬃毛如火焰般向后飘扬。

楚舜华的左手拔出了第二柄剑——一柄窄而弯的短剑，剑身覆着淡绿色铜锈，剑柄缠着褪色的绿绢。那是西泽尔在洛阳赠予他的青蛇剑，与夔龙角剑配合，一长一短，一古一新。

双剑。

夔龙角剑长而沉重，适合劈砍与突刺；青蛇剑窄而锋利，适合切入缝隙。两柄剑在他手中如同两条游龙，起伏翻卷间，每一剑都精准地切入欧米茄原型体的装甲缝隙——那些暗金色板甲之间仅有一指宽的接缝，是红水银核心与外层装甲的连接处，也是欧米茄原型体唯一的弱点。

一架原型体俯冲而下，指尖的光束朝楚舜华射来。楚舜华侧身，朱砂默契地向左一偏，光束擦着他的肩膀掠过，烧焦了月白色长袍的衣角。楚舜华的身体在马背上一拧，夔龙角剑从下向上撩出，剑锋精准地切入那架原型体胸甲的缝隙。

夔龙角剑与红水银核心接触的瞬间，剑身中沉睡了三百年的大夏龙雀之力猛然爆发。暗金色的闪电从剑尖炸开，将那架欧米茄原型体的胸口撕开了一个脸盆大的洞。红水银核心暴露在晨光中，跳动了三下，轰然爆炸。碎片四溅，朱砂灵巧地避开，继续向前冲。

第三架。第五架。第八架。

每倒下一架欧米茄原型体，爆炸的红水银火焰就在空中炸开，像是一朵朵暗金色的花。楚舜华从火焰中穿过，月白长袍被烧出了好几个洞，露出里面玄色的内衬，但他的眼神始终平静而锐利，像一柄被磨了三百年的古剑。

他在找缺口。

欧米茄原型体群的阵型虽然密集，但它们被设置为自杀式攻击，每一架都在疯狂地朝王屋山俯冲，根本不规避鬼武者的攻击。这意味着它们的阵型中央一定有一个薄弱点——最先到达的已经俯冲到山脚，后面的还在天上，彼此之间出现了脱节。

那里就是缺口。

"朱砂！"

楚舜华猛夹马腹。朱砂长嘶一声，四蹄翻飞，朝着欧米茄原型体群的中央冲去。鬼武者Ⅱ型的骑士们自动让开一条通道，盾牌举起，为他们的主帅提供掩护。夔龙马骑兵从两翼包抄，长刀挥舞，将试图填补缺口的原型体一一截杀。

楚舜华冲入了缺口。

眼前是密密麻麻的欧米茄原型体，像一堵由暗金色钢铁构成的墙壁。没有一具人形的面孔，只有暗金色的装甲板和跳动的红水银核心，像一千只没有灵魂的红色眼睛。楚舜华没有减速，反而将夔龙角剑高高举起。

"开！"

那一剑劈下，夔龙角剑中三百年前大夏龙雀的力量完全释放。暗金色的剑气从剑尖激射而出，化作一道十余米长的光弧，将面前的欧米茄原型体群劈开了一条路。爆炸接连响起，碎片四溅，硝烟和红水银的腥味弥漫在空气中。

楚舜华穿过了那堵钢铁墙壁。

眼前出现了王屋山的主峰。山体中央裂开一道深不见底的峡谷，峡谷的两侧岩壁上刻满了世界树的壁画。矿物颜料历经三百年依然鲜亮，画面上是世界树的全貌——树干为暗金色合金，树枝末梢挂着红水银核心当成果实，树叶是大小不一的金色齿轮，所有齿轮都画成缓缓转动的样子。壁画的最后一段画着一位紫瞳的年轻人，背景是那棵巨大的世界树。

那个紫瞳年轻人的面容，与西泽尔一模一样。

三百年前，有人走到过这里。

楚舜华从朱砂背上跃下。

夔龙马在峡谷入口处停下，鬃毛被山风吹得猎猎作响。它的眼睛是暗红色的，与楚舜华对视了一眼，然后转过身，面向身后蜂拥而来的欧米茄原型体群，独自挡在入口处。

"老伙计。"楚舜华伸手摸了一下朱砂额前那道陈旧的弹痕。

朱砂低嘶了一声，像是在说：去吧。

楚舜华转身，走入了峡谷。

峡谷两侧的壁画在晨光中渐渐亮了起来。随着楚舜华深入，那些画中的齿轮开始缓缓转动，发出细微的嗡鸣声。世界树残枝东方主根节点感知到了星见后裔的到来，正在苏醒。

峡谷的尽头是一扇巨大的石门，高逾十米，宽五米，表面刻满了机械神教的齿轮徽记和锡兰梵文。铭文与西泽尔母亲银莲花项链坠背面的铭文同出一源——同一个人刻的，同一套语言，同一种笔法。

楚舜华伸手按在石门上。

指尖触及石面的瞬间，整座王屋山都震了一下。

门后传来沉闷的震动，像一颗沉睡了三百年的心脏终于恢复了跳动。那是世界树残枝东方主根节点的脉搏——它感知到了星见后裔的归来，正在发出共鸣。

楚舜华深吸一口气，抽出夔龙角剑。

剑身在黑暗中发出暗金色的光，那是大夏龙雀之力与石门上梵文共鸣的光芒。光沿着梵文的笔画蔓延，从门扇的中央向四周扩散，将整扇石门都覆盖在一张金色的光网之中。

他高举夔龙角剑，朝石门劈下。

剑锋劈开了石门。石屑纷飞，梵文碎裂，封印了三百年的石门轰然倒塌。石门后，是一根暗金色的巨根——那是世界树残枝东方主根，比人腰还粗，从山体深处延伸出来，像一条沉睡了千年的巨龙。根须末端刻着细如发丝的梵文，每一道刻痕都在微微发光，与楚舜华后颈的紫瞳金纹产生着强烈的共鸣。

那是他母亲守护了一生的东西。

那是夏国三千年的国运所系。

楚舜华举起夔龙角剑。

"母亲。"他低声说。

"我来了。"

夔龙角剑落下。

剑锋触碰到世界树主根的那一刻，整座王屋山都震动了。暗金色的光芒从切口处喷涌而出，像是压抑了三百年的岩浆终于找到了出口。世界树主根发出了一声悲鸣——不是声音，而是一种直接作用于灵魂的震颤，传入楚舜华的脑海，穿透了他的神经，抵达了他血液最深处的每一个角落。

他看到了。

通过世界树的记忆，他看到了三百年前的画面。

一个白发的年轻女人站在这棵树下，紫瞳中流着泪。她的手按在主根上，正在将什么封印进去。那不是他的母亲——是他的外祖母，是三百年前从锡兰逃出翡冷翠的最后一个东方星见，是将东西方两支世界树残枝秘密分别交给两个家族守护的守秘人。

她将自己的灵魂与记忆封印在世界树的根中，等待着有朝一日，她的后代会回来斩断这棵树，结束这一切。

"对不起，外祖母。"

楚舜华说。

"您的等待，到此为止了。"

他将夔龙角剑深深刺入主根之中，然后猛然向下劈落。

大夏龙雀之力完全释放。

世界树主根从中间裂开，暗金色的汁液喷涌而出，浇在楚舜华的身上，灼热如岩浆。根须末端的梵文全部碎裂，那些细如发丝的文字在光芒中化为金色的尘埃，缓缓飘散。主根的断口处，一道暗金色的光柱冲天而起，穿透了王屋山的岩层，直射向天穹，将黎明前的最后一片夜色彻底撕碎。

那是世界树残枝东方支脉最后的告别。

与此同时，战场上的所有欧米茄原型体同时僵住了。

它们的红水银核心失去了来自母体的能量供给，跳动的频率急剧下降——欧米茄原型体是世界树残枝结出的果实，母体的根系被斩断，果实便失去了养分。一架接一架的欧米茄原型体从空中坠落，像断了线的风筝。它们的装甲在坠落过程中散架，红水银核心失控爆炸，在王屋山周围炸开了一朵又一朵的暗金色火花，像一场迟来了三百年的流星雨。

朱砂从烟雾中走出。

它的鬃毛被烧焦了一片，额头上多了几道新的伤口，左前腿的关节处嵌着一块欧米茄原型体的碎片，暗金色的体液顺着腿甲流下来。但它的眼神依然是那样——暗红色的，忠诚的，无惧的。

楚舜华走上前，扶住朱砂的脖子，手指触到那道陪伴了这匹马一生的弹痕。

"老伙计。"他的声音有些哑。

"你做到了。"

朱砂低嘶一声，伸出舌头舔了舔楚舜华被红水银灼伤的手背。

楚舜华抬头，看向西方的天际。

黎明的光正从那个方向涌来，把整片天空染成了玫瑰红色。楚舜华的目光穿过了千万里的距离，穿过了万水千山，穿过了一切钢铁与火焰。

他看到了。

在那个方向上，有一个人站在维苏威火山的山顶。苍白，锋利，紫色的瞳孔中流动着金色的纹路。那是他的血亲，是三百年前被分割的同一个灵魂的另一半，是另一个星见的后裔。

那个人也在看向东方。

两人的目光，在虚空中相遇。

没有任何语言。

这是两个星见后裔之间无需言语的确认。

楚舜华点了点头。

在西泽尔的方向。

那个方向上，西泽尔也点了点头。

东方之根，西方之叶。三百年的轮回，在这一刻终结。他们各自守护的东西，都已经被斩断。东方之根的枯萎带来了西方之叶的凋零，世界树残枝在两个星见后裔的合力之下，终于从这个世界退场。

楚舜华感觉到眼眶微微发热。

不是悲伤。是释然。

他转身，对身后幸存的鬼武者骑士们高声说：

"回洛阳！"

号角再次响起，苍凉而悠远，在王屋山的山谷中回荡。

朱砂驮着楚舜华，朝着东方奔去。晨光洒在他们身上，把人和马的影子拉得很长很长。身后，王屋山的峡谷中，那道暗金色的光柱正在缓缓消散。

而在千万里之外的翡冷翠，维苏威火山深处，莲花通道尽头的世界树残枝西方支脉，也在同一时刻枯萎了。金色的齿轮停止了转动，红水银的香气消散了。

母亲守护了三十年的秘密，终于落下了帷幕。

【English】
Chapter 258 — The Guardian of the Dragon-Sparrow

Mount Wangwu. The last dark of the night before dawn.

The sky was the colour of old iron. To the east, the horizon had cracked open like a wound, and through the crack spilled something that was not yet daylight but was not night either — a dull arterial red, as though someone had poured a basin of molten copper across the black cloth of the firmament. Below, on the plain at the foot of the mountain, several hundred black heavy mobile armours stood in close-ordered squares. The sound of their steam boilers gathered into a low thunder that ran to and fro in the valleys, finding no edge to die against. Every machine was carved at the head with a Kui-dragon's face: copper fangs, iron teeth, and a pair of red mercury crystals set where the dragon's eyes should have been, giving off a dim crimson glow in the light that was not yet light. The gilt Kui-dragon patterns on the breastplates were dark with condensed steam, and they caught what faint gold there was and held it.

Ghost Warrior, Mark II. The sharpest blade in the Xia.

Behind the squares, thousands of Kui-dragon horses. Their black manes moved in the dawn wind as though the ground itself were breathing. The riders wore light black armour, ring-pommeled long swords at their hips, Kui-dragon round shields on their arms. Every eye among them was turned west, toward that slow-bleeding sky.

Chu Shunhua sat his horse at the head of the column.

His mount was red as cinnabar from hoof to crest, a little under six feet at the shoulder, taller by a full head than any other horse in the line. There was an old bullet-hole at the brow, healed long ago into a hard ridge of scar — a wound from the Southern Frontier War, seventeen years gone. Two slugs of lead were still lodged in the bone. The mane was not black. It was the rare red of autumn leaves held up against a flame, and in the morning wind it streamed out behind him like a torch not yet blown out.

The horse's name was Cinnabar.

He had been a three-year-old when the old emperor rode south in person, and Chu Shunhua — sixteen then, a boy on a borrowed sword — had gone into the enemy lines on his back. Cinnabar took three arrows and would not go down. After the battle the imperial physicians said he would never rise again. They gave him to the winter. He refused it. When Chu Shunhua was raised to the rank of Guardian Duke, the old horse vanished from the imperial stud. Some said he had been sent back to the Northern Grasslands. Some said he had died of his wounds and been buried quietly in the night.

Only Chu Shunhua knew.

Cinnabar had been taken to a hidden horse-farm at the foot of Mount Wangwu, deep in the forests, and there he had lived for seventeen years, eating, sleeping, growing older, untouched.

It had not been abandonment. It had been protection.

Inside the horse's chest, set beside the heart, there was a small dark-gold metal container. It did not hold red mercury. It held a refined essence drawn from a fragment of consciousness preserved in the remnant root of the World Tree, far below the mountain. It had been the last thing his mother had pressed into his hand before she died, with the instruction to implant it in the body of the Kui-dragon he loved most. For seventeen years Cinnabar had carried that container as a second heart, tireless, fearless, and able to share in the remnant root's perception of danger.

Chu Shunhua raised his head.

West.

A dark-gold cloud was forming along the line of the sky. It was not a cloud. It was a moving wall of steel, hundreds of silhouettes, each exactly the same, each lit along its edges by the first thin wash of dawn. The dark-gold of their plate armour caught the light and threw it back sharper than the light that gave it. From the chest of each silhouette, a red mercury core pulsed at a steady rate, like a thousand crimson eyes that had decided to open at once and would not be closing again.

Omega prototypes.

They came on in layers, one rank riding upon another, like a flight of locusts risen out of the pit. Each one was set for a single end. In fifteen minutes the red mercury cores would detonate. The blast would take the mountain and everything in it off every map ever drawn.

The target was the eastern main root of the World Tree's remnant branch.

Chu Shunhua drew his sword.

The blade was long and narrow, dark-gold from end to end, polished from a sliver of horn that Cinnabar had shed as a foal. The natural grain of the Kui-dragon horn was still in it, frozen lightning run through with the dark of old bone. In the hand it warmed, as though blood still moved somewhere inside the metal. Two ancient seal-characters were cut into the guard.

Dragon-Sparrow.

Kui-dragon-horn blade. The sacred weapon of the Xia imperial line, passed from hand to hand for three hundred years.

"Relay the order."

His voice was not loud. It passed through the thunder of the boilers as a silver needle passes through rolling thunder.

"Ghost Warriors forward. Frontal intercept."

"Kui-dragon cavalry to the wings. Take anything that gets past."

"Objective: total annihilation."

The horn was blown.

It was the oldest horn in the Xia army, an ox-horn, hoarse and bleak, and it ran out over the valleys of Mount Wangwu and would not come back. Where it went, silence went with it.

Several hundred Ghost Warriors came alive in the same breath. The steam boilers opened; blue-white vapour fountained out, and the steel giants moved forward. The heavy steel shields on the left arms rose. Five-fold cross-forged, they caught the dawn and made a wall. The repeating steam-guns on the right arms opened, and a hail of lead went up into the sky. The bullets met the Omega prototypes halfway and burst against their armour in bright, brief stars.

The Omega swarm answered with a sound like metal being torn. A swarm, that was the word for it. They split into dozens of small formations and dived, fingers out, and from the fingertips the dark-gold thermal beams lashed down. Where they touched, Ghost Warrior plate boiled and parted; steam-pipes burst with a wet crack; shrapnel went every direction at once. One Ghost Warrior, set upon by three, took three black scorches in his shield. The knight inside roared. The shield swung out and caught one Omega and knocked it spinning into the air. The other two beams were already through his breastplate. The red mercury core went up. The chain blast took the machine apart. The black wreckage came down across the ground in pieces.

"Hold the line. Shield-bearers forward. Covering fire."

Cinnabar heard the voice as though it had been spoken into his ear. He screamed, once, the high, clean war-cry of his kind, and carried Chu Shunhua forward into the press of steel.

He was faster than any horse in the line. Seventeen years of pasture had not softened a single muscle. The bones were as they had always been. He ran now as he had run at three, the four hooves barely touching, the red mane blown flat behind him.

Chu Shunhua's left hand came up and drew a second sword.

It was a narrow, curved short sword, the blade filmed with a pale green patina, the hilt bound in silk that had once been a deeper green. The Green Snake, given to him in Luoyang by Cesare, to be carried with the Kui-dragon-horn blade. One long, one short. One ancient, one new.

Twin swords.

The Kui-dragon-horn blade was heavy, for the cut and the lunge. The Green Snake was thin, for the seam. In his hands they moved as two dragons, rising and turning, each strike setting into a finger-width gap in the dark-gold plate of an Omega — the join between the carapace and the red mercury core within, the only weakness the things had.

An Omega dived at him. The thermal beam from its fingertips lanced down. He leaned, and Cinnabar shifted a half-stride to the left, and the beam went past his shoulder and scorched the hem of his moon-white robe. His body turned on the saddle. The Kui-dragon-horn blade came up from below, found the seam in the Omega's breastplate, and entered it.

The blade touched the red mercury core.

The power of the Great Xia Dragon-Sparrow, which had slept in the metal for three hundred years, woke in a single breath. Dark-gold lightning blew out from the point. It tore a hole the size of a washbasin through the Omega's chest. The red mercury core came open to the dawn, beat three times, and went. The fragments came down. Cinnabar stepped through them as though they were leaves.

The third. The fifth. The eighth.

Each Omega that fell opened the air with a flower of dark-gold fire. Chu Shunhua rode through them. The moon-white robe took a few more burns and showed the black lining beneath. His eyes had not changed. They were the eyes of a blade that has been sharpened for three hundred years and has not forgotten what it is for.

He was looking for the gap.

The Omegas were set for suicide. Each one dived without thought for itself, without thought for the others, without thought for the Ghost Warriors waiting below. The first wave was already at the foot of the mountain. The second was still high. Between them the formation had thinned to nothing.

There. That was the gap.

"Cinnabar."

He drove his heels in. Cinnabar screamed and went forward, into the heart of the swarm. The Ghost Warriors parted to let him through, shields coming up to give him what cover they could. The Kui-dragon cavalry closed around the wings, and the long swords of the riders began to take the Omegas that tried to swing across and fill the opening.

Chu Shunhua went into the gap.

The wall was before him — dark-gold steel upon dark-gold steel, plates and cores, plate and core, no face, no thought, only a thousand red eyes that had been made for a single use. He did not slow. He put the Kui-dragon-horn blade above his head.

"Open."

That stroke fell. The power of the Dragon-Sparrow came off the steel in its full strength, three hundred years of waiting let go at once. The dark-gold sword-qi left the blade as an arc of light more than ten metres long, and the wall of Omegas was cut through along its middle. The detonations began as he came out the other side, one after another, so that the air filled with the smell of red mercury and iron.

He came out the far side of the wall.

The main peak of Mount Wangwu was before him. The mountain had been split down the middle by a canyon, deep, with no bottom that could be seen. Both walls of the canyon were painted. The paint was the mineral kind, three hundred years old, and it had kept its colour. The World Tree was painted there in full: a trunk of dark-gold alloy, branches at the ends of which hung red mercury cores for fruit, leaves that were golden gears of varying sizes, each gear shown in the act of slow turning. The last panel of the painting was a young man with purple eyes. The World Tree was behind him, taking up the whole wall.

The young man's face was the face of Cesare.

Three hundred years ago, someone had stood here.

Chu Shunhua swung down from the saddle.

Cinnabar stopped at the mouth of the canyon. His mane was blown flat by the mountain wind. His eyes, dark red, met Chu Shunhua's. He turned, then, of his own will, and put himself between the canyon and the Omega swarm that was still pouring in from behind. He stood alone at the entrance.

"Old friend." Chu Shunhua reached out and laid his hand on the old bullet-scar at the horse's brow.

Cinnabar gave a low, short sound, almost a word. Go.

Chu Shunhua turned and went into the canyon.

The murals on the two walls began, as he went deeper, to come up into the light. The painted gears moved. The movement was slow, and it made a thin humming that had not been heard for a long time. The eastern main root of the World Tree's remnant had felt the approach of a Star-Seer's child, and was waking.

At the end of the canyon there was a stone door. It was more than ten metres high and five wide. Its face was covered with the gear-and-shrine marks of the Mechanist Church and with Sanskrit out of Ceylon. The inscription shared an origin with the inscription on the back of the Anemone pendant that Cesare's mother had worn. The same hand. The same tongue. The same way of cutting the strokes.

Chu Shunhua put his hand to the stone.

The mountain shook.

A heavy beat came through the door from the other side, the slow, even beat of a heart that had been stopped for three hundred years and had just been started again. The pulse of the World Tree's eastern main root. It had felt a Star-Seer's child return, and was answering.

Chu Shunhua drew a long breath. He drew the Kui-dragon-horn blade.

The metal lit in the dark. The dark-gold of the Dragon-Sparrow

【中文】
第259章 新的黎明

天空是青黑色的。

维苏威火山从那不勒斯湾的北缘拔地而起，黑沉沉的轮廓压在海平线上，看不见一丝火光。从这个距离看过去，它只是亚平宁半岛南端一道沉默的剪影，和三百年来一样。

但西泽尔知道它内部正在发生什么。

口袋里那枚金色机械鸟还在轻轻跳动，每跳一下，胸口就传来一阵灼热。

三十秒。

只剩最后三十秒了。

他站在那不勒斯湾北侧的山顶上。风从海面上吹来，带着咸腥的湿气，把他苍白得近乎透明的头发吹得凌乱。他身边站着薇若兰、阿方索、唐璜、昆提良、阿黛尔、瓦莲京娜、李锡尼、碧儿和塔拉夏，所有人都没有说话，只是看着那座沉默的火山。

他们刚刚从达·芬奇三百年前开凿的秘密通道中爬出来。

通道的尽头是齿轮隧道，隧道的尽头是黑铁巨门，黑铁巨门的后面是莲花通道，莲花通道的尽头是世界树残枝所在的圆形大厅——那个被初代教皇藏了三百年的禁忌之地。

他们曾经站在那个大厅里。

看着那棵巨大的、由暗金色合金铸成的世界树，看着那些挂满红水银核心的金色齿轮，看着那些以莲花状同心圆排列的、编号从001到999的欧米茄原型体。看着莱昂纳多·博尔吉亚，那个把身体百分之八十二都改造成机械的疯子，三百年来一直在等待着这一刻的疯子。

然后他们打败了他。

然后他启动了所有欧米茄原型体的自毁程序，让它们飞向东方。

然后楚舜华在王屋山斩断了世界树的东方主根，让那些飞在天空中的炸弹失去动力，坠落、爆炸。

而现在，所有的一切，所有的秘密，所有的源头——维苏威火山——即将在三十秒后被彻底抹去。

"二十秒。"薇若兰轻声说。

她的声音很平静，但西泽尔注意到她的手在袖口里微微收紧了，指节发白。她也是刚刚才知道自己师父佛朗哥的真正身份是达·芬奇·博尔吉亚的直系后裔，也才知道达·芬奇就是三百年前的初代教皇，也才知道密涅瓦机关成立的真正目的是封印世界树残枝阻止重启机械神国。

三十年的秘密，她扛了三十年。

"十五秒。"

阿方索的机械手指在袖口里轻轻合拢，发出细微的齿轮声。他想起了自己藏在工具箱最底层的那瓶液体——那是欧米茄原型体引擎碎片中渗出的金红色血液，他一直舍不得扔掉。现在，那些东西马上要永远消失了。

"十秒。"

唐璜没有说话。他只是把手插进了口袋里，手指碰到了那枚叶尼塞忍冬花纹临时通行证戒指。

"五秒。"

西泽尔闭上眼睛。

他不需要看。

他想起很多事。

他想起八岁时在克里特岛手工做的那只黄铜机械鸟，母亲接过去端详了很久，笑着说很像真的鸟。

他想起十二岁时母亲带着他和阿黛尔离开克里特岛来到翡冷翠，母亲的眼神里有一种他当时看不懂的释然。

他想起十八岁时站在马斯顿王立机械学院的斗兽场里，用最基础的礼仪剑术击败了屠龙者腓特烈。

他想起二十四岁时在坎特伯雷堡的阳台上看着翡冷翠的万家灯火，想着阿黛尔什么时候才能从亚琛回来。

他想起母亲死前最后一次给他扎头发，那双温柔的手在晨光中微微颤抖。

他想起母亲临终前对他说的话。

"你会有一个家。"

他做到了。

他给阿黛尔留了一间卧室。他答应母亲会保护阿黛尔。他答应了。

三。

二。

一。

当。

一声闷响，仿佛大地深处有什么东西被撕裂了。

紧接着，一道白光从维苏威火山的山腹中央迸发出来，瞬间照亮了整片那不勒斯湾，把黑夜变成了白昼。

那不是火焰。

那不是爆炸。

那是湮灭。

白光所到之处，一切都在无声地消失。山体、岩石、岩浆、那些藏在火山深处四十年没有被任何人类看到的欧米茄原型体、那些铺满整个圆形大厅的金色齿轮、那些刻满梵文的同心圆纹路、那些被初代教皇留下的所有秘密……全部在白光中化为乌有。

连同初代总长达·芬奇·博尔吉亚的亲笔日记。

连同他三百年来留下的所有图纸、笔记、档案。

连同初代教皇背着自己建立的原罪机关的所有研究数据。

连同莱昂纳多·博尔吉亚的机械残骸。

连同贝尔纳黛特——那个用艾琳娜·博尔吉亚DNA和欧米茄碎片培育出的人造生命，那个继承了艾琳娜的记忆和执念的女孩。

全部。

白光没有向外扩散。它停在维苏威火山脚下，圆形的，像是被一只无形的手精确地画了一个边界。边界之外，那不勒斯城的灯火依然在闪亮，渔港里的渔船依然在摇晃，城墙上的哨兵依然在来回走动。

世界没有变。

只有维苏威火山变了。它从一座山，变成了一道灼热的、缓缓塌陷的光痕。

白光持续了整整三十秒。三十秒后，光芒慢慢消散，维苏威火山的位置升起了一根通天的暗金色烟柱。烟柱笔直地冲向天穹，顶部缓缓散开，像一朵盛开的、灰白色的莲花。

莲花。

那是三百年前末代星见用自己鲜血和骨头封印世界树时看到的莲花。也是初代教皇从阿瓦隆冰原带走世界树残枝时看到的莲花。也是母亲守护了三十年的莲花。

现在，那朵莲花永远地开放了，又永远地凋谢了。

西泽尔睁开眼睛。

他的脸被那道已经消散的白光映得苍白，紫色的瞳孔中流动着金色的纹路。他看着那朵正在升起的莲花形烟云，什么也没有说。

眼泪从他的眼角无声地滑落。

他没有伸手去擦。

薇若兰在他身边，同样安静地看着那朵烟云。她的眼眶也红了，但她也只是站着，任由海风把她的白色长发吹乱。达·芬奇·博尔吉亚的日记就藏在她胸口的口袋里，但日记的最后几页被她撕掉了，永远不会有人知道上面写了什么。

唐璜张了张嘴，想说点什么，最后只是把手插进了口袋里。

阿方索的机械手指在袖口里轻轻合拢，发出细微的齿轮声。

昆提良握紧了拳头，指节发白。

阿黛尔靠在碧儿身上，碧儿揽住了她的肩膀，两个人都没有说话。碧儿想起了琳琅夫人留给她的银莲花别针，背面刻着古锡兰文"愿莲花指引迷途之人"——现在，那朵莲花永远地开完了。

李锡尼摸了摸胸口那枚圣剑碎片的位置，圣剑碎片已经不再跳动了。它感应不到任何世界树残枝的气息了。

塔拉夏捂住了嘴，眼眶里有泪光。

瓦莲京娜把手轻轻按在西泽尔的手背上。她的手指冰凉，但很稳。

"结束了。"她轻声说。

西泽尔点了点头。

是的。结束了。

三百年的秘密，三百年的阴谋，三百年的轮回，全部被那道白光带走了。母亲守护了三十年的东西，父亲用尽一生想要压制的东西，梵蒂冈档案室里永远不能见光的东西……全部。连同那座火山里最后一架欧米茄原型体的残骸，连同初代教皇留下的所有机械装置，连同那些永远不应该重见天日的真相。

全部。

海风从西边吹来，把那朵烟云推向东边。烟云在风中慢慢散开，露出后面深蓝色的、缀满星辰的天穹。

星辰在慢慢隐没。

天穹在慢慢变亮。

不是从维苏威火山的方向。是从东方。

一丝玫瑰红色的光从海平线的尽头升起，慢慢地、慢慢地，把整片天空染成了浅浅的玫瑰色。月亮失去了光泽，最后一颗星也隐没了。

黎明了。

"他来了。"瓦莲京娜说。

西泽尔抬起头。

从东方的山道上，一队黑色的铁骑正缓缓地向他们走来。铁骑的前方是一面玄色的大旗，旗上绣着金色的夔龙纹，在晨光中猎猎作响。旗帜下面，数百台鬼武者Ⅱ型机动甲胄排成整齐的方阵，蒸汽从它们的关节处喷出，在清晨的冷空气中凝成淡蓝色的雾。

夔龙马骑兵紧随其后，马蹄踏在青石板上，发出有节奏的哒哒声，马蹄声整齐得像一个人的心跳。

最前方的那匹夔龙马是红色的。

朱砂。

朱砂的额头上有一道陪伴了它一生的弹洞。它的鬃毛在晨风中飘动，红得像一团燃烧的火焰。

楚舜华骑在朱砂的背上，一身黑色战甲，夔龙角剑斜挂在腰间。他的脸上有血污和硝烟的痕迹，但眼神明亮而平静。他刚刚在王屋山斩断了世界树的东方主根，刚刚完成了外祖母三百年前留下的遗愿，刚刚终结了东方星见家族三百年的轮回。

他来了。从东方来了。从那朵盛开的、凋谢的莲花的方向来了。

楚舜华在山脚下停住了马，翻身下来。朱砂在他身后低嘶一声，伸出舌头舔了舔他的手背。楚舜华轻轻拍了拍朱砂的脖子，然后抬起头，看向山顶。

他看到了西泽尔。

苍白的，锋利的，紫色的瞳孔中流动着金色纹路的西泽尔。三百年前被分割的同一个灵魂的另一半，另一个星见的后裔。

他向西泽尔点了点头。

西泽尔也向他点了点头。

楚舜华开始向山上走。朱砂想跟上来，被他摆手阻止了。夔龙马打着响鼻停在原地，红色的鬃毛在晨风中飘动。

楚舜华一步一步地走上山道，他的脚步声在山道上回响，清晰而沉稳。鬼武者Ⅱ型方阵在山脚下停住，夔龙马骑兵也停住，所有人都看着他们的统帅独自走向山顶。

西泽尔也向前走了一步。

两个人在山道的中央相遇。

晨光从东方洒下来，把他们的影子拉得很长。一个是西方新的守护者，一个是东方新的守护者。一个有着紫色的瞳孔和金色的纹路，一个有着深黑色的眼睛和深黑色的头发。

他们就这样面对面站着，相距不过三步。

"你来了。"西泽尔说。

他的声音很轻，但每一个字都清晰。

"我来了。"楚舜华说。

他的声音有些哑，像是刚刚喊过很多话。

楚舜华从腰间解下夔龙角剑，双手托着，递向西泽尔。夔龙角剑在晨光中发出暗金色的光泽，那是夔龙马额前断角打磨而成的剑，剑身保留着天然的纹理，纹路如凝固的闪电。

"这把剑跟了我三十年。"楚舜华说，"现在我把它交给你。"

西泽尔没有接。

"我不是来收剑的。"楚舜华说，"我是来和你握手的。"

他收回了剑，把剑重新挂回腰间。然后他伸出了右手。

西泽尔看着那只手。那是一只握了三十年剑的手，掌心有厚厚的茧，指节有旧伤留下的疤，食指上有一道深深的剑痕，是十年前在战场上留下的。但那只手很稳，没有一丝颤抖。

西泽尔也伸出了右手。

他的手同样有茧，同样有伤疤。右手中指上戴着瓦莲京娜送给他的那枚冰原寒玉银戒指，戒指在晨光中发出淡淡的冷光。

两只手在晨光中握在了一起。

没有铠甲，没有武器，没有蒸汽，没有红水银。

只是两只手。一个是西方新的守护者的手，一个是东方新的守护者的手。他们的手紧紧地握在一起。

"从今以后，"楚舜华说，"教皇国政教分离，新任教皇不再由枢机会选举，由教廷与各国共同推举。夏国仍以楚舜华为摄政王，两国永为兄弟之邦，平等相待，永不侵犯。东西方商道自由通行，红水银技术与机械技术共同发展。"

他的声音不大，但每一个字都清晰地传到了山顶上所有人的耳中。

"你愿意吗？"楚舜华问。

西泽尔握着他的手，紫色的瞳孔中流动着金色的纹路。他没有犹豫。

"我愿意。"

两只手握得更紧了。

然后他们松开了手。

楚舜华转身，对着身后所有的鬼武者骑士和夔龙马骑兵高声说：

"从今以后，西方与东方，平等！"

山道上爆发出一阵呼喊。呼喊声在山谷中回荡，惊起了远处树林中的飞鸟。飞鸟振翅而起，掠过那朵正在散开的暗金色烟云，飞向东方刚刚升起的太阳。

瓦莲京娜走到西泽尔身边。她的金色长发在晨风中飘动，发间有清冷的忍冬香气。

"叶尼塞王国也愿意加入这个联盟。"她轻声说。

西泽尔转头看她。

"我的父王让我转告你，"瓦莲京娜说，"从今以后，叶尼塞与你同进退。"

西泽尔看着她。瓦莲京娜的蓝色眼睛在晨光中像两块冰，冰下面有温暖的水在流动。

"谢谢你。"西泽尔说。

"不用谢我。"瓦莲京娜说，"我是你的未婚妻。"

唐璜在后面低声嘀咕："这下老板真的要娶两个老婆了。"

昆提良伸手捂住了他的嘴："闭嘴。"

阿方索在笑。他的机械手在袖口里轻轻合拢，发出细微的齿轮声，这是他开心的标志。

薇若兰也在笑。她的白色长发被晨风吹乱，但她的眼睛明亮。她想起了佛朗哥教授——她的老师，密涅瓦机关初代总长后裔——想起他藏了一辈子的秘密终于可以放下了。

阿黛尔擦了擦眼泪。她靠在碧儿身上，碧儿揽住了她的肩膀。

"哥哥。"阿黛尔轻轻叫了一声。

西泽尔转过头。

阿黛尔朝他笑了笑。那个笑容让他想起了母亲，母亲也是这样笑的。在克里特岛的那个斜窗小屋里，在翡冷翠的圣女塔下，在分别了十三年后重逢的那个暗巷里。母亲都是这样笑的。

西泽尔也笑了。

那是今天他第一次笑。

很淡，但很真。

太阳完全升起来了。

金色的阳光洒满了整片山脉、那不勒斯湾、维苏威火山曾经矗立的地方、翡冷翠的城邦、君士坦丁堡的穹顶、洛阳的宫阙、还有叶尼塞的冰原。

新的黎明到来了。

【English】
Chapter 259 — A New Dawn

The sky was the colour of tarnished steel.

From the northern rim of the Bay of Naples, Vesuvius rose against the sea-horizon, a black mass with no fire in it. At this distance it was only a silhouette, the same shape it had worn for three hundred years, since the last time it had tried to bury a city.

Cesare knew what was happening inside it.

The little golden bird in his pocket gave another throb against his thigh, and the heat ran up through his ribs.

Thirty seconds.

He stood at the top of a hill north of the bay, the salt wind off the water pulling at hair so pale it was almost white. Beside him, in a line, Verolana, Alfonso, Don Juan, Quintilian, Adele, Valentina, Licinius, Biel, Talaxia. No one was speaking. They were watching the silent mountain.

They had just climbed out of a passage that Leonardo had cut three centuries ago. At the end of the passage: a tunnel of gears. At the end of the tunnel: a black iron door. Behind the door: a corridor paved in stone lotus. At the end of the corridor: the round hall where the World Tree's severed branch had been kept, hidden by the first Pope for three hundred years, a forbidden place.

They had stood in that hall.

They had seen the tree — vast, cast in dark gold alloy, hung with the gold cogs that dripped red mercury at their cores. They had seen the Omega prototypes arranged in lotus-concentric rings, numbered from 001 to 999. They had seen Leonardo Borgia, the madman who had replaced eighty-two percent of his own body with brass and steel, who had been waiting for this moment for three centuries.

They had beaten him.

And then he had activated the self-destruct on every Omega prototype, and sent them flying east.

And then Chu Shunhua, on Mount Wangwu, had cut the World Tree's eastern root, and the bombs that had been sailing through the air had lost their power, and fallen, and broken.

And now, all of it — the source of all the secrets, the heart of all the lies, Vesuvius itself — was about to be wiped from the world in thirty seconds.

"Twenty seconds," Verolana said, quietly.

Her voice was calm. Cesare saw her hands tightening inside her sleeves. The knuckles were pale. She had only just learned that the master she had served for thirty years, Frango, was a direct descendant of Leonardo Borgia. That Leonardo had been the first Pope. That the Minerva Bureau she had given her life to had been founded for one purpose: to seal the World Tree's branch, and prevent anyone from ever restarting the Mechanical Kingdom of God.

Thirty years of secrets. She had carried them alone.

"Fifteen seconds."

Alfonso's mechanical hand, inside his sleeve, made the small sound of a ratcheting finger. He thought of the bottle at the bottom of his toolbox — the liquid, the colour of sun through wine, that he had bled from a broken Omega engine, and never had the heart to throw away. It would be gone now. Forever.

"Ten seconds."

Don Juan said nothing. His hand was in his pocket. His finger was on a ring stamped with a temporary pass, in the Yenisei honeysuckle pattern.

"Five seconds."

Cesare closed his eyes.

He did not need to see.

He thought of many things.

He thought of Crete, when he was eight. A brass bird he had made with his own hands. His mother had taken it and held it to the light, and smiled, and said it looked almost real.

He thought of his twelfth year, when his mother had taken him and Adele from Crete to Florence. Something in her eyes he had not understood at the time. A kind of release.

He thought of his eighteenth year, in the pit of the Marston Royal Mechanical Academy, beating Frederick the Dragonslayer with the most basic of the duelling forms.

He thought of his twenty-fourth year, on the balcony at Canterbury Keep, watching the lamps of Florence come on in the dark, and wondering when Adele would be back from Aachen.

He thought of his mother's hands, the last time she had combed his hair for him, and how they had trembled in the early light.

He thought of what she had said to him, at the end.

You will have a family.

He had done it.

He had kept a bedroom for Adele, in the house he had made. He had promised his mother he would protect her. He had kept the promise.

Three.

Two.

One.

A low sound, as if something deep under the earth had been torn in two.

Then a column of white light burst from the belly of Vesuvius, and the whole bay was lit as if it were noon.

It was not fire.

It was not explosion.

It was erasure.

Where the light passed, everything was silently gone. The mountain. The rock. The lava. The Omega prototypes that had lain in the volcano's heart for forty years, unseen by any human eye. The gold cogs that had paved the round hall. The concentric rings inscribed in Sanskrit. All the secrets the first Pope had left behind.

All of it, gone.

And with it: the diary, in Leonardo Borgia's own hand, that had waited three hundred years. The drawings. The notes. The files. The research data of the Original Sin Bureau, the body the first Pope had set up in secret. Leonardo Borgia's own mechanical remains. Bernadette — the girl built from Elena Borgia's DNA and Omega fragments, the girl who had inherited Elena's memories and her obsession.

All of it.

The light did not spread. It stopped, clean, at the foot of Vesuvius, in a perfect circle, as though an invisible hand had drawn a line in the air. Outside that line, the lamps of Naples still flickered. The fishing boats still rocked in the harbour. The sentries still walked the city wall, back and forth.

The world had not changed.

Only Vesuvius had. It was a mountain no longer. It was a burning line of light, slowly caving in on itself, slowly dimming.

The light held for thirty seconds. Then it faded, and a column of dark gold smoke began to climb out of the place where Vesuvius had been, straight as a pillar, into the high sky. At the top, the smoke spread, and the spreading took the shape of a flower.

A lotus.

A grey-white lotus, opening in the dawn.

The lotus the last of the Star-Seers had seen, three hundred years ago, when she had sealed the World Tree with her own blood and bones. The lotus the first Pope had seen, when he had carried the World Tree's branch away from the ice plains of Avalon. The lotus his mother had guarded, for thirty years.

Now it had bloomed, at last. And now it was withering.

Cesare opened his eyes.

His face, where the white light had washed it, was the colour of wax. In the purple of his irises, lines of gold were moving. He watched the flower of smoke opening in the sky, and said nothing.

A tear ran down his cheek, soundlessly. He did not lift his hand to wipe it.

Verolana stood beside him, watching the same flower. Her eyes were red, but she stood straight, and let the sea wind do what it wanted with her white hair. Leonardo Borgia's diary was in the pocket at her breast, but the last pages had been torn out. No one would ever read them.

Don Juan opened his mouth, as if to say something, and then shut it, and put his hand in his pocket.

Alfonso's mechanical fingers ratcheted softly in his sleeve.

Quintilian's fists were closed, his knuckles pale.

Adele was leaning against Biel. Biel's arm was around her shoulder. Neither of them spoke. Biel thought of the silver anemone brooch Lady Linlang had given her, with its old Ceylonese inscription — May the lotus guide the lost. The lotus, now, was done.

Licinius touched, through his shirt, the place where the holy sword fragment lay over his heart. The fragment was still. It could feel no World Tree branch anywhere in the world, any more.

Talaxia had her hand over her mouth. Her eyes were wet.

Valentina laid her hand, lightly, on the back of Cesare's hand. Her fingers were cold, and steady.

"It is finished," she said, softly.

Cesare nodded.

Yes. Finished.

Three hundred years of secrets. Three hundred years of conspiracy. Three hundred years of a cycle that had kept turning. The white light had taken it all. The thing his mother had guarded for thirty years. The thing his father had spent his life trying to suppress. The thing the Vatican archives would never let see daylight. All of it. The last Omega wreck in the volcano. Every mechanism the first Pope had left. Every truth that should never have come back to the sun.

All of it.

The wind off the bay blew from the west, and pushed the column of smoke eastward, and the smoke thinned, and behind it the deep blue of the sky opened, and the sky was thick with stars.

The stars were going out, one by one.

The sky was getting brighter.

Not from the direction of Vesuvius. From the east.

A thread of rose-red light was lifting itself off the sea's edge, slowly, slowly, staining the whole sky a pale rose. The moon was losing its colour. The last star was gone.

Dawn.

"He is coming," Valentina said.

Cesare lifted his head.

From the eastern road, a column of black cavalry was climbing the hill toward them. At the head of the column, a banner the colour of night, with a kui-long worked in gold thread across it, snapping in the early wind. Beneath the banner, hundreds of Ghost Warrior II mobile armours stood in ordered squares, steam hissing from their joints, the steam turning to a thin blue mist in the cold air. Behind them, the kui-long cavalry, hooves on the blue stone of the road, the hoofbeats a single rhythm, like one great heart beating.

The lead horse was red.

Cinnabar.

There was a bullet-hole over her left eye that she had carried all her life. Her mane was moving in the wind, red as a tongue of fire.

Chu Shunhua sat her, in black armour, the kui-long horn sword slung at his hip. There was blood on his face, and the grey dust of gunpowder. His eyes were clear. He had just cut the World Tree's eastern main root on Mount Wangwu. He had just completed the last task his grandmother had left him, three hundred years ago. He had just broken the three-hundred-year cycle of the eastern Star-Seer line.

He had come. From the east. From the direction of the lotus that had opened, and withered.

Chu Shunhua reined Cinnabar in at the foot of the hill, and swung down from the saddle. Cinnabar nipped softly at his wrist; he patted her neck, and looked up the hill.

He saw Cesare.

Pale. Sharp. Purple irises with gold lines moving in them. The other half of the same soul, cut in two three hundred years ago. The descendant of another Star-Seer line.

He inclined his head to Cesare.

Cesare inclined his head to him.

Chu Shunhua began to walk up the hill. Cinnabar tried to follow; he raised a hand, and she stopped, blowing through her nose, her red mane still moving in the wind.

He climbed the hill on foot, one slow step at a time. His boots on the blue stone were the only sound on the road. The Ghost Warrior squares waited at the bottom. The kui-long cavalry waited. Everyone watched their commander walking up the hill alone.

Cesare stepped forward, to meet him.

They met in the middle of the road.

The dawn was coming in from the east, and the shadows they cast down the hill were long. One was the new guardian of the West. One was the new guardian of the East. One had purple eyes and gold moving in them. One had eyes as black as his hair, and hair as black as his eyes.

They stood, three paces apart, face to face.

"You came," Cesare said.

His voice was soft. Every word was clear.

"I came," Chu Shunhua said.

His voice was hoarse, as if he had been shouting for hours.

Chu Shunhua drew the kui-long horn sword from his hip, and held it out to Cesare, in both hands, level. In the dawn, the sword was the colour of old gold. It had been ground from the broken horn of a kui-long mare's forehead, and the grain of the horn was still on the blade, in patterns like frozen lightning.

"This sword has been with me for thirty years," Chu Shunhua said. "I would like to leave it with you."

Cesare did not take it.

"I did not come for a sword," Chu Shunhua said. "I came to shake your hand."

He slid the sword back into its sheath, and held out his right hand.

Cesare looked at the hand. A hand that had held a sword for thirty years. The callus on the palm was thick. There were old scars across the knuckles. There was a deep sword-cut on the index finger, ten years old, from a battle. The hand was steady. It did not shake.

Cesare held out his own right hand. His hand had its own calluses, its own scars. On the middle finger he wore the silver ring of ice-plain jade that Valentina had given him, and the ring was cool in the early light.

The two hands met, in the dawn.

No armour. No weapons. No steam. No red mercury.

Just two hands. The hand of the new guardian of the West, and the hand of the new guardian of the East. They closed, hard, on each other.

"From this day," Chu Shunhua said, "the Papal State is to be governed with the Church and the Crown separated. The new Pope will not be chosen by the College of Cardinals, but jointly nominated by the Holy See and the kings of all the nations. The Xia Kingdom will continue under me as regent. The two countries are brother-states, in perpetuity, equal, and never to make war on each other. The trade roads between East and West are to be open. The arts of red mercury and the arts of mechanism are to be developed in common."

His voice was not loud. Every word of it, however, reached the top of the hill, and was heard by all who stood there.

"Do you accept?" Chu Shunhua asked.

Cesare's hand was in his. The gold was moving in the purple of his eyes. He did not hesitate.

"I accept."

Their hands tightened, once, on each other.

Then they let go.

Chu Shunhua turned, to the Ghost Warrior knights behind him, and to the kui-long cavalry, and called out, in a voice the size of the morning:

"From this day forward — the West and the East, as equals!"

The road broke open with a cheer. The cheer went up the hill, and into the valley, and startled a flock of birds from a tree at the wood's edge, and the birds rose up on their wings, and flew through the thinning column of dark gold smoke, and on, toward the sun that was just lifting itself above the sea.

Valentina came to stand beside Cesare. Her hair was the colour of wheat, and the morning wind was in it, and the cold honeysuckle scent of it.

"The Kingdom of Yenisei also wishes to join the alliance," she said, quietly.

Cesare turned to her. Her eyes were the colour of ice in the dawn, and there was warmth under the ice, like water under a frozen stream.

"My father has asked me to tell you," Valentina said. "From this day, Yenisei will go forward with you, and not behind."

Cesare looked at her.

"Thank you," he said.

"Do not thank me," she said. "I am your betrothed."

Don Juan muttered, behind them: "Well. The boss is actually going to marry two of them, then."

Quintilian put a hand over his mouth. "Quiet."

Alfonso was smiling. His mechanical hand, in his sleeve, made the small ratchet-sound of a finger closing. That was how Alfonso said he was glad.

Verolana was smiling, too. Her white hair was a wreck in the morning wind, but her eyes were clear. She thought of Professor Frango — her teacher, descendant of the first Director of the Minerva Bureau — and how the secret he had carried all his life could now, at last, be set down.

Adele wiped her eyes. She was leaning against Biel. Biel's arm was around her shoulder.

"Brother," Adele said, softly.

Cesare turned.

Adele smiled at him. The smile was his mother's. Their mother had smiled like that, in the small room with the slanted window on Crete, and at the foot of the Holy Maiden's Tower in Florence, and in the dark alley where he had found her again, after thirteen years. Their mother had always smiled like that.

Cesare smiled, too.

It was the first time he had smiled, that day.

A small smile. A true one.

The sun was fully up.

The light of it poured down the side of the mountain, and out over the Bay of Naples, and across the place where Vesuvius had been, and over Florence, and the domes of Constantinople, and the palace roofs of Luoyang, and the long ice of the Yenisei plains.

The new dawn was here.

第260章 红莲绽放的时代

【中文】
第260章 红莲绽放的时代

黄昏的光把坎特伯雷堡的屋顶染成了蜂蜜色。

西泽尔坐在烟囱旁边的石栏上，脊背靠着暖了一整天的红砖，靴子踩着瓦片上一片被风卷上来的银杏叶。整座翡冷翠在脚下铺开，圣母百花大教堂的穹顶在夕阳中泛着铜色，阿尔诺河像一条发亮的银蛇穿过旧城区，远处的丘陵上种满了葡萄藤，藤叶在暮色中转为深红。

这是他在这座古堡屋顶上的第二个秋天了。

楼下传来孩子们的声音。

"老师，今天学什么？"

"今天学一首新歌。"

"又是那个听不懂的吗？"

"那叫锡兰语。是妈妈教给我的。"

"妈妈在哪里？"

"妈妈去了很远的地方。但她把歌留给了我，我把歌留给你们。"

西泽尔没有动。他端着一杯红茶，瓷杯已经凉透了，但他没放下。茶杯里映着天边那抹将散未散的霞光，也映着他自己的脸——比一年前多了一点血色，颧骨的线条不再那么锋利，眼窝下的青黑也淡了许多。

一年前的这个时候，他正从维苏威火山北麓的废墟里爬出来。身上还沾着灰，妹妹的莲花之歌还在耳畔回响，右手无名指上还有一圈冰原寒玉银戒指留下的浅浅压痕——瓦莲京娜上个月把戒指退回来了，附了一行字：戒指留你手上太凉，等我去看雪时你再还我。

一年后，很多事情都变了。

枢机会解散的消息传来那天是深秋。他正在厨房帮碧儿揉面，听见唐璜在门外喊，他没有放下手里的面团，只是把面粉在围裙上擦了擦，走到窗前看了一眼。十二位佩戴白银面具的枢机卿在全民公投中一个接一个摘下了面具，梵蒂冈广场上人头攒动，导火索是梵天陨落——当翡冷翠人亲眼看到那朵暗金色烟云在维苏威火山上空散开、而那不勒斯城的灯火纹丝未损时，他们终于知道枢机会和原罪机关在过去三百年里做过什么。异端审判局的黑天使档案被解密，圣域屠杀的真相印在了《翡冷翠公报》的头版上，七位枢机卿被移交审判，三位主动走进修道院，此生不再出来。

他把面团放回盆里，回去了。

新教皇由全民选举产生。都灵大主教安塞尔莫以绝对多数票当选。老人七十岁，虔诚，博学，对军事和政治一窍不通——这正是所有人需要的：一个真正的精神领袖，不是穿着白袍的政客。他的职权被重新定义为纯粹的宗教事务，主持弥撒、封圣、祝圣，不能指挥军队，不能任免官员，不能签署教廷之外的法令。三百年来第一次，弥赛亚圣教的十字架和世俗的王冠被彻底分开。

新教皇安塞尔莫亲自来过坎特伯雷堡。老人穿着素白长袍，没带随从，在花园里和阿黛尔聊了半个小时孩子们的歌声，然后走到书房里把一份烫金的任命书递给西泽尔。

上面写着"新教皇国政教协调大臣"。

西泽尔看了一眼就推了回去。

"我不是当官的料。您另请高明。"

安塞尔莫没有生气，老人的眼睛里反而露出笑意。"那你打算做什么？"

"教我妹妹弹琴。"

老人愣了半天，走的时候脸上的笑容一直没收。任命书第二天送到了唐璜手里，唐璜倒是欣然接受——用他的话说是"有权不用过期作废"，但实际上他把大部分事务都推给了新任外交部，自己还是整天泡在红莲骑士团的训练场上。

所以西泽尔的位置是红莲骑士团的荣誉团长。一个只在关键时刻才会出现的影子团长。日常事务由唐璜处理，新甲胄设计由阿方索负责，情报工作由宝儿·拉瑟秘密提供，训练新兵的事归昆提良管。

这是他给自己选的位置。不是最高的，不是最显眼的，但是最自由的——他可以随时抽身，回到坎特伯雷堡的屋顶上喝茶，看银杏叶飘落，听阿黛尔教孩子唱歌。

他终于有了一个家。

不是为了给谁看，不是为了谋取什么利益，只是因为家里有人等他回来。

---

夏国那边同样改天换地。

楚舜华在王屋山劈开世界树东方主根后回到洛阳，没有废帝，而是扶持弟弟楚昭华复位——这一次是真正的复位，不是傀儡。兄弟俩在太庙里关起门谈了三天三夜，出来的时候楚昭华的眼眶是红的，但脊背比以往任何时候都直。

楚舜华任摄政王，楚昭华任皇帝。分工明确，楚舜华管军务和外交，楚昭华管内政和民生。他们偶尔吵架，吵完了一起喝酒，第二天接着吵。上个月楚舜华从洛阳寄来一封信，信里夹着一片风干的桂花——王屋山下的桂花树今年开了三百年来的第一次花，兄弟俩在树下喝了一整夜的酒。信的最后一行写的是：你的那份我替你喝了，等你来洛阳我重新酿。

叶素理成了中山国首相。他用三十年时间在西方建立的情报网被完整保留，由他亲手改组为正规外交机构。中山国加入了东西方平等联盟，成了联盟在远东的桥头堡。纯公主没有再被安排去联姻——她现在是叶素理的副手，专管教育和文化，上个月刚在洛阳办了一所女子学堂。叶素理在给西泽尔的信里写：公主殿下把剑钉在了学堂门口的墙砖上当装饰，说谁再提联姻她就拿那把剑砍谁。老臣觉得这样挺好。

新罗马帝国换了新皇帝。查士丁尼七世退位为太上皇，皇太子继位。新皇帝年轻气盛，三个月内连发三道改革诏书，其中一道就是任命拜伦为狮心骑士团团长。拜伦拿到校长奖学金的真正目的从来就不是为了学术——他后来在信里跟唐璜坦白了，是新罗马帝国军方早就看上了他，他在马斯顿的两年只是走个过场。事实证明走这个过场是有用的，狮心骑士团的将军们很快注意到了这个在马斯顿拿了满分的年轻人。拜伦通过非正式渠道给唐璜送了一封信，说狮心骑士团随时愿意和红莲骑士团进行联合训练，当然他会付训练场地的租金。唐璜回信只有一个字：滚。

瓦莲京娜被叶尼塞沙皇正式任命为驻新教皇国和驻夏国的特命全权大使。一个公主同时担任两个国家的大使，这是叶尼塞外交史上前所未有的。叶素理私下评价说老沙皇比狐狸还精——他知道女儿和西泽尔的婚约意味着叶尼塞已经同时和西方、东方绑在了一起，索性一个公主换两个铁杆盟友。瓦莲京娜的金色长发留长了，垂到腰间，用一根绣着忍冬花的白缎带扎起来。她每次来翡冷翠述职都住在坎特伯雷堡的客房里，碧儿已经习惯了在她的枕头里塞忍冬花干花瓣。上次她来的时候带了一箱叶尼塞冰原的雪松木，说要给堡里的壁炉换柴，被碧儿拦下来了——翡冷翠的冬天没那么冷，用不着烧雪松木。瓦莲京娜不服气，说翡冷翠的冬天比起叶尼塞根本不算冬天，但最终还是听了碧儿的话。

五国联盟在翡冷翠签署了《平等联盟条约》，条约只有三章：平等、通商、不侵犯。简单得让老牌外交官们难以置信。签署仪式的当天，有人问西泽尔为什么条款这么少，他想了想说："大人物总喜欢把简单的事情搞复杂。"

---

楼下的莲花之歌唱到了最后一段。

那是锡兰的摇篮曲，三百年前锡兰的星见们对着世界树唱的歌。阿黛尔的母亲教给她，她现在教给翡冷翠的孩子们。

孩子们听不懂歌词，那些古锡兰语早就不是任何地方的口语了，它们只活在歌里。但旋律很简单，像水面的波纹一圈一圈荡开，孩子们很快就学会了。

"莲花开在清晨的水面上——"
"根扎在看不见的泥土里——"
"风吹过的时候花会点头——"
"雨落下来的时候根会喝水——"

阿黛尔一句一句教，孩子们一句一句学。一个扎双马尾的小女孩把"点头"唱成了"点刀"，把"喝水"唱成了"喝雪"，逗得其他孩子哈哈大笑。

"莉莉丝，'点头'，不是'点刀'。"

"可是老师，刀比头厉害呀！"

"厉害也不许唱错。"

莉莉丝不服气地撅了撅嘴。她是附近教区一个退役老兵的女儿，五岁半，每天准时出现在堡门口，风雨无阻。阿黛尔从来不锁门。

西泽尔在屋顶上听着那首歌。他的紫瞳里映着天边最后一线玫瑰色的光，映着银杏叶从枝头飘落的弧线，映着花园里那个穿着白裙子的姑娘弯腰给孩子们纠正发音的身影。

他想起了一年前——阿黛尔还在翡冷翠的贵族区里做笼中鸟，一份婚约被递到她面前，迪迪埃国王的使者笑容满面地要求她嫁给一个她从未见过面的王子。那天晚上她没有哭，只是安安静静地坐在窗前，把母亲留下的那本棕榈叶预言书合上。

现在她站在银杏树下教孩子们唱歌，没有任何人再能要求她嫁给谁。

---

新密涅瓦技术研究院在维苏威火山北麓亮着灯。

阿方索是研究院的总工程师。密涅瓦机关被改组为公开的技术研究院，院徽从六翼猫头鹰换成了齿轮与橄榄枝交织的图案，入口处的叹息之墙被保留了下来，但不再有黑铁冰封棺从里面运出——三百年里那些被封存的秘密档案全部被解密，变成了教科书里的公开课。

薇若兰是新密涅瓦的第一任院长。

她在拿到密涅瓦机关总长六翼猫头鹰黄铜徽章的那天没有举行任何仪式，只是把徽章挂在了办公室门背后，然后开始做她最擅长的事——给新一代的工程师上神经接驳系统的入门课。她的白色长发比一年前更长了，平时用一根素银簪子别起来，课上讲到关键处时会习惯性地用簪子敲黑板，簪子敲在黑板上发出清脆的叮叮声，底下的年轻工程师们大气都不敢出。

佛朗哥教授留给她的那本达·芬奇日记已经被她影印了三百份，编入新密涅瓦的必修教材。三百年来密涅瓦机关积累的所有机密资料都变成了公开的研究课题。薇若兰在教材的扉页上写了一行字：密涅瓦的真正遗产不是武器，是对真相的尊重。

红莲骑士团在这一年里从五台试制甲胄发展到了三十台正规编制。瓦莲京娜从叶尼塞带来了神怒Ⅲ型的全部技术资料，阿方索把密涅瓦机关的神经接驳技术和叶尼塞的冰原寒玉技术融合，新一代红莲骑士可以在甲胄里连续作战六个小时而不会对神经系统造成永久性损伤。

唐璜是团长。他的蔷薇之鬼甲胄被重新设计了，涂成了酒红色，胸口印着一朵盛开的红莲——那是西泽尔亲手画的。团部设在翡冷翠旧圣堂装甲师的营房里，训练场就在维苏威火山北麓——现在那里已经长出了新草。唐璜偶尔还会犯贫嘴的毛病，但他训练新兵的时候极其认真，据昆提良说"他认真起来像换了个人"。上个月他拒绝了美第奇家族的一笔赞助金，理由是"我们红莲骑士团不接受有条件的钱"，那位美第奇家的少爷当场翻脸走了，唐璜在背后冲他做了个鬼脸。

昆提良是副团长。他的奥古斯都甲胄是团里最重的，五层交错锻造的秘银重盾可以正面硬抗普罗米修斯的劈砍。训练新兵的时候他最凶，嗓门大到隔三个营房都能听见，但新兵们都喜欢他，因为他会记住每一个人的名字。艾莲偶尔来营地看望他，会带一罐她自己做的蜜饯，昆提良训练完就着蜜饯吃三个面包——这个习惯从翡冷翠的特洛伊酒店时代一直保留到现在。

阿方索是总机械师。他的机械手在一次训练事故中又坏了一次，他自己修好了，然后用剩下的时间设计了一套全新的蜘蛛巢系统——八只微型机械蜘蛛可以从手腕释放，在半径一百米内形成电子干扰幕，烧穿欧米茄自愈神经纤维都不在话下。他把图纸拿给薇若兰看的时候，薇若兰看了半天，说："这比我当年设计的暴力增强型雷霆牙还暴力。"阿方索说："暴力是我的专业。"

宝儿·拉瑟成了翡冷翠最有名的女演员。她的成名作是《莲花公主》——一个关于锡兰王国覆灭的悲剧，她在台上唱了三个小时的歌，最后一场是穿着白纱从高塔上跳下来。演出结束后的谢幕持续了二十分钟，她回到后台，给西泽尔发了一条密语：今晚有两个前公爵的线人在第三排。

米内·斯蒂尔——现在是新教皇国的外交大臣，绰号"翡冷翠最圆滑的人"——当天下午就派人把那两个人请去"喝茶"了。米内本人在斗兽场时代就认识西泽尔了，他在斗兽场里混过、被人叫过"最聪明的纨绔子弟"，但一年的外交生涯证明他不只是会花家里的钱——他和拜占庭大使卢瑟打成了朋友，又通过卢瑟的渠道重新和叶素理搭上了线，外交界都说他"把翡冷翠的每一扇门都打开了，却没让任何一扇门关上"。

红莲骑士团的荣誉团长是西泽尔——一个只在关键时刻才会出现的影子。

---

楼下的歌声进入了尾声。

"等到太阳落山的时候——"
"莲花就合上了花瓣——"

莉莉丝这次没有唱错。她认真地唱完最后一句，然后跑过去抱住阿黛尔的腰。

"老师！明天还唱！"

"好。明天唱。"

"后天呢？"

"后天也唱。"

"大后天呢？"

"大后天也唱。"

莉莉丝满意了。其他孩子也满意了，他们排着队跟阿黛尔告别，一个一个抱了抱她的腰，然后嘻嘻哈哈跑出花园大门。门外站着各自的父母，退役老兵、农夫、小店主、手艺人，他们朝阿黛尔挥挥手，带着孩子回家吃晚饭。

花园安静下来。

阿黛尔站在银杏树下，仰头看着屋顶的轮廓。她看不清西泽尔的脸，但知道他坐在那里——她哥哥总是喜欢坐在高处，翡冷翠的每一座钟楼、每一道城墙、每一处屋脊，他都坐过。

"哥哥！下来喝茶！碧儿姐姐烤了栗子蛋糕！"

"知道了。"

西泽尔放下那杯凉透了的红茶，沿着屋顶的暗梯走下去。烟囱边搁着的黄铜机械鸟拍了拍翅膀跟上来，绕着他的头顶飞了一圈，停在了他的肩膀上。那是他在克里特岛八岁时做给阿黛尔的小玩意儿，后来阿黛尔转送给了母亲，母亲去世后碧儿保管了十三年，现在又回到了他手里。鸟身上的漆已经斑驳了，一只翅膀的铰链是阿方索帮他换的，但鸟眼里的两颗红水银微晶还亮着，在暮色中一闪一闪。

他走进花园的时候，阿黛尔递过来一块栗子蛋糕。蛋糕烤得金黄，奶油上点缀着糖渍银杏果。碧儿在围裙上擦了擦手，给他拉好椅子。她比一年前丰润了一些，脸颊有了血色，手指上沾着面粉和奶油。坎特伯雷堡的生活比翡冷翠的贫民区好得多，她也不用再白天做女侍长晚上帮人洗衣服了。

"瓦莲京娜的信今天到了。"她说，"在书房里。"

"嗯。"

"还有唐璜的信、昆提良的信、阿方索的信。"

"嗯。"

碧儿无奈地笑了笑，转身去端茶。阿黛尔已经切好了一块蛋糕递给西泽尔，自己也拿了一块。

兄妹俩坐在银杏树下吃蛋糕。夕阳从圣母百花大教堂的穹顶后面沉了下去，天空从蜂蜜色变成了玫瑰色，又从玫瑰色变成了深蓝色。最先的几颗星星亮了。

"哥哥。"

"嗯。"

"你笑了。"

西泽尔伸手摸了摸自己的嘴角。

是的。他在笑。

那是一个极淡极淡的笑容。嘴角弯起的弧度几乎看不出来，但紫瞳里有一种以前从未出现过的东西——柔软、温暖，像黄昏最后一缕光落在水面上的倒影。

一年前的西泽尔不会这样笑。一年前他的紫瞳像刀刃，嘴角永远抿成一条直线，笑容里带着审视世界的寒意。那时候他不知道母亲在临终前把一朵锡兰纸莲花托付给碧儿保管，不知道妹妹在翡冷翠的贵族区里被当作联姻的筹码，不知道瓦莲京娜在叶尼塞的冰原上等他等了十年，不知道自己后颈的黄金套管里藏着世界树的钥匙。

但现在他知道了。他知道了所有的真相，也失去了该失去的东西。他亲手终结了三百年世界树的轮回，代价是数不清的牺牲和一场差点把翡冷翠变成火海的爆炸。维苏威火山消失了，那不勒斯的海湾前只剩下一个巨大的凹陷，凹陷里长满了新草。

他从那个凹陷里爬出来的时候，碧儿给他披了一件外套。阿黛尔在他怀里哭得发抖，瓦莲京娜握着他的手，薇若兰站在远处擦眼泪。那是今天他第一次觉得自己活着的意义不只是为了活着。

一年后的现在，他坐在自家花园里吃蛋糕。栗子蛋糕的味道很好，碧儿的手艺又精进了。

"妈妈如果能看见就好了。"阿黛尔轻声说。

西泽尔没有立刻回答。他看着花园里满地的银杏叶，看着天边越来越亮的星星，看着黄铜机械鸟从阿黛尔的肩膀飞到碧儿的肩膀又飞回来。

"她会看见的。"他说。

声音很轻，像风穿过银杏叶的沙沙声。

阿黛尔靠在他肩膀上。兄妹俩坐在铁桌边，身后是亮着灯的古堡，头顶是越来越深的蓝天。

---

更远的地方，翡冷翠的灯火一盏一盏亮起来。圣母百花大教堂的穹顶在夜色中泛着柔和的月光。阿尔诺河上的驳船拉响了汽笛，悠长的汽笛声从河面上飘过，飘过旧桥，飘过阿尔诺河南岸的窄巷，飘过那些三年前还贴着"私生子""怪物""红龙"字样的墙壁——那些字已经被新粉的白灰盖住了，没有人再提。

更远的地方，叶尼塞冰原上飘着今冬第一场雪。瓦莲京娜裹着白狐皮站在皇宫的窗前，手里握着那枚她退给西泽尔又被他退回来的冰原寒玉银戒指。她看着窗外的雪，忽然笑了，对着空气说："等雪停了，我去看你。"

更远的地方，洛阳的宫阙亮着灯。楚舜华和楚昭华在太庙里喝酒，酒是楚舜华母亲三十年前埋在王屋山下的桂花酿。楚昭华喝多了，拉着哥哥的袖子说："哥，那天在假山里，我其实特别害怕。"楚舜华拍了拍弟弟的后脑勺："怕什么？你哥在。"

更远的地方，新密涅瓦技术研究院在维苏威火山北麓亮着灯。薇若兰趴在办公桌上睡着了，面前摊着一本教科书清样，素银簪子搁在旁边，一缕白色长发垂在纸页上。阿方索在隔壁的车间里画图纸，唐璜端着一杯咖啡推门进来，被阿方索瞪了一眼——阿方索工作的时候不喝咖啡，要喝白水。唐璜不以为然地在他对面坐下，从口袋里摸出一块糖塞进嘴里。

更远的地方，拜伦在君士坦丁堡的军营里写训练报告，写到一半停下来，提起笔在信纸的空白处画了一朵潦草的红莲。画完他自己也笑了，摇着头把那页纸撕下来揉了。

更远的地方，中山国的首相府里亮着灯。叶素理坐在案前批阅公文，桌角搁着一枚纯公主白天丢给他的青丝古剑——公主说剑太沉了不想带回来，让舅舅帮忙磨一磨。叶素理看了看那把剑，提笔在公文上写了最后一行字：准。公主殿下终于能用自己的剑了。

更远的地方，一架红莲骑士团的新型甲胄静静地站在训练场上。酒红色的涂装在月光下泛着柔和的光，胸口那朵盛开的红莲图案被风吹得猎猎作响。昆提良在甲胄旁边坐着，面前摊着一摞训练日志，他正在一个一个名字地核对。艾莲抱着蜜饯罐子靠在他肩头，已经睡着了。

更远的地方，贝尔纳黛特·卡米耶·伊莎贝尔·索菲·薇若妮卡——曾经叫璎珞的那个姑娘——在查理曼王国的修道院里安静地生活着。她不太和人说话，每天清晨在院子里种一株莲花。她不知道自己从哪里来，也不知道自己为什么还活着，但她知道世界上有一个紫眼睛的男孩曾经对她说过"回家"。那三个字她记了很久。

更远的地方，达·芬奇·博尔吉亚三百年前修建的秘密通道里已经长满了苔藓，黑铁巨门上的倒置五芒星圣徽被藤蔓遮住了大半。门后面的莲花通道里，齿轮停止了转动，金色莲花花瓣的边缘开始氧化变暗。世界树残枝已经枯萎了，三百年的守护在这个秋天终于落幕。通道的入口处有阿方索尼提良和唐璜合力钉上去的一块铜牌，上面刻着：

此路不通。
后人勿入。
这是命令。

这是佛朗哥教授临终前的遗愿，也是西泽尔代表东西方星见后裔共同做出的决定。他们不需要再打开那扇门了。

更远的地方，翠绿的山谷深处，梵天陨落留下的那朵暗金色烟云早已散尽。爆炸的中心点长出了一棵小树，嫩绿的叶子在风中轻轻摇晃，没有人知道那是什么品种的树，也没有人知道它为什么能在那种地方生长。阿黛尔上次去看过那棵树，她蹲在树苗前面坐了很久，回来后对西泽尔说："哥哥，那棵树是绿色的。"

西泽尔说："绿色好。"

---

夜深了。

花园里只剩下萤火虫的光和古堡窗户里透出来的暖黄色灯光。阿黛尔已经睡了，碧儿给她掖好被角，轻轻带上了房门。塔拉夏在堡门的值班室里打盹，她现在是坎特伯雷堡的管事——不再做机械师了，她说年纪大了手抖，画不了图纸。

西泽尔回到了屋顶上。

他坐在烟囱旁边的老位置，手里换了一杯热茶——碧儿刚才送上来的，还冒着气。天上的星星比一年前亮了，或者只是翡冷翠的灯火比一年前少了。空气里有银杏叶的干燥气味，有远处阿尔诺河的水汽，有壁炉里雪松木的烟气。

他闭上眼，听见了风穿过银杏叶的声音。

他想起了很多人。很多事。

想起母亲在克里特岛的小屋里教他认星星，想起莉诺雅在诺丁山初等学校的走廊里给他一块面包，想起托雷斯在训练场上陪他练剑的身影，想起阿黛尔在翡冷翠重逢的那个夜晚扑进他怀里的重量。

想起瓦莲京娜在敞篷礼车的驾驶座上跷着白靴子对他说"要不要送你们一程"，想起阿方索在深夜的修理店里给他倒一杯劣质咖啡，想起唐璜在马其顿阵弩机里冲他竖大拇指，想起昆提良在十连战最后一场把甲胄砸向地面时发出的轰然巨响。

想起薇若兰在密涅瓦机关的走廊里快步走过，白色长发在身后飘起来。想起宝儿·拉瑟在后台的化妆镜前对着他笑。想起李锡尼在矿道里把打磨好的朗基努斯圣枪碎片递给他。想起风林在翡冷翠的小巷里递来楚舜华的亲笔信。想起达·芬奇在三百年前写下的那些字。

想起苏伽罗从高塔上坠落。想起蒂兰在铁棺里沉睡了百年。想起安妮在马斯顿的街头烧成了灰。想起琳琅夫人在行刑的火焰中合上了眼睛。

那些脸在他脑海里一张一张地闪过，像阿尔诺河上的驳船一样慢慢地漂远。

他睁开眼。

紫瞳在星光下泛着淡淡的光泽，不是从前那种像刀刃的冷光，而是像玻璃穹顶上映出来的最后一缕晚霞。紫瞳深处有什么东西在轻轻发光——不是金纹，不是世界树残留的痕迹，只是一种平静的、温暖的、属于他自己的光。

他端起茶杯，喝了一口。

茶是热的。

*（全书完）*
